a_rows_sample.anchor: The Annotated Bilattice Kernel (ABK-1) extends First-Degree Entailment (FDE / Belnap-Dunn 4-valued logic) to eliminate the structural distinction collapses identified in prior kernel evaluations ... ABK-1 resolves these deficiencies by embedding the standard 4-valued truth space BF_4 into an Annotated Bilattice Frame B_ABK. Each proposition is represented as an annotated truth tuple that pairs an FDE valuation with a justification graph, a temporal validity window, and modal/scope metadata.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces ABK-1: an architecture that embeds standard 4-valued FDE (BF_4) into an Annotated Bilattice Frame, pairing each proposition's FDE valuation with a justification graph, temporal validity window, and modal/scope metadata, explicitly targeting the lineage/temporal/underdetermined collapses previously measured against bare FDE (this batch's r-req-fde-kernel-test-vectors-result).

a_rows_sample.anchor: State(phi) = <nu(phi), J(phi), tau(phi), mu(phi)> ... FDE Truth Valuation nu in BF_4 ... Justification Graph J = <V_J, E_J, m> ... Temporal Validity Window tau = <t_start, t_end, v_D, TTL> ... Modal and Boundary Metadata mu = <Type, Modality, ScopeMask>
a_rows_sample.statement: Formal definition of the ABK-1 state 4-tuple State(phi)=<nu,J,tau,mu>: nu is the FDE truth valuation in the powerset of {T,F}; J=<V_J,E_J,m> is a justification DAG (premise nodes, derivation edges, justification mode in {Evidenced,Inferred,Reported,Assumed}); tau=<t_start,t_end,v_D,TTL> is a temporal validity window with a dependency version vector; mu=<Type,Modality,ScopeMask> carries Analytic/Synthetic, Necessary/Contingent, and a scope bitmask.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Order (<=_k): S1 <=_k S2 iff (nu1 subseteq nu2) and (J1 sqsubseteq_DAG J2) ... Truth Order (<=_t): S1 <=_t S2 iff (T in nu1 implies T in nu2) and (F in nu2 implies F in nu1) ... Conjunction (x_t) ... Disjunction (+_t) ... combining FDE valuation, justification-DAG union, temporal intersection, and metadata AND (mu1 (dot) mu2).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines ABK-1's algebraic lattice structure over B_ABK = BF_4 x J x T x M: a Knowledge Order (<=_k, comparing valuation-subset and DAG-substructure) and a Truth Order (<=_t, standard FDE truth ordering), plus lattice conjunction and disjunction operators that combine FDE valuations via standard FDE meet/join, union justification DAGs, intersect temporal validity windows, and combine modal metadata via a metadata-AND operator.

type_signature.codomain: boolean order relations, or a combined ABK-1 state

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suite 1.2 Underdetermined vs. Unknown | FAIL | PASS (via J.nodes.length > 0) | PASS ... Suite 2.1 Inferred vs. Assumed | FAIL | PASS (via J.mode) | PASS ... Suite 3.1 Stale vs. Expired | FAIL | PASS (via tau.tEnd and v_D) | PASS ... The Annotated Bilattice Kernel (ABK-1) achieves a 100% Pass Rate across all Tier P1 and Tier P2 distinction verification suites, qualifying it for ratification as a fully R_req-compliant KnowledgeOS kernel engine.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports that ABK-1, re-run against the SPEC-RREQ-TEST-2026-V1 suite, converts all three of the bare-FDE test failures found earlier in this batch (Underdetermined-vs-Unknown via presence of justification-graph nodes; Inferred-vs-Assumed via J.mode; Stale-vs-Expired via temporal window and dependency-version comparison) into PASSes, alongside the two bare-FDE PASSes it retains (Contradiction-vs-Unknown; Absence-vs-Evidence-of-Absence), yielding a claimed 100% pass rate across Tier P1/P2 and a recommendation to ratify ABK-1 as R_req-compliant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: export class ABKState { public val: FDEValue; public justification: JustificationGraph; public temporal: TemporalWindow; public metadata: ModalMetadata; ... resolveKnowledgeStatus(currentTime, upstreamVersions): KnowledgeStatus { if (this.resolveCurrency(...) === 'Expired') return 'NotAssessed'; switch(this.val) { case 'B': return 'Contradictory'; ... case 'N': { if (this.justification.nodes.length > 0) return 'Underdetermined'; return 'Unknown'; } } }
a_rows_sample.statement: Provides a full TypeScript reference implementation of ABK-1: an ABKState class carrying val/justification/temporal/metadata fields with resolveKnowledgeStatus (currency-checks first, then value-switches, distinguishing Underdetermined from Unknown by non-empty justification nodes), resolveCurrency (Expired if past tEnd, Stale if any dependency version has advanced, else Current), and resolveJustificationMode methods; and an ABKAlgebra class with a hard-coded FDE conjunction truth table and a meet() operation merging justification DAGs (node/edge union), temporal windows (intersection), and metadata (conjunctive AND, scope-mask bitwise AND).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Architectural Specification: ABK-1 / Contr Bridge Interface (ABK-CONTR-INT-v1) ... The Contr Isolation Module operates directly on top of the Annotated Bilattice Kernel (ABK-1) to handle non-explosion, contradiction trap frames, and resolution state tracking for paraconsistent evaluations. ... When an inbound assertion or lattice operation produces a contradictory valuation (nu(phi)=B), the ABK-1 engine delegates contradiction containment to ABKContrBridge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a bridge architecture (SPEC-ABK-CONTR-2026-V1) between ABK-1 and a Contr contradiction-isolation engine: whenever an ABK-1 lattice operation produces a contradictory valuation (nu=B), the engine delegates containment to an ABKContrBridge that traps the state in a local frame, sets ResolutionStatus=Unresolved, and initializes an evidential polarity edge graph, ensuring downstream inference cannot propagate the contradiction beyond a bounded contextual scope.

a_rows_sample.anchor: export interface IABKContrBridge { shouldIsolate(state): boolean; isolateContradiction(...): ContrIsolationPayload; updateResolutionStatus(...): ContradictionTrapFrame; evaluateResolution(frameId): ABKState; } ... evaluateResolution ... if (totalWeight > 0.5) { resolvedVal='T'; resolution='Resolved'; } else if (totalWeight < -0.5) { resolvedVal='F'; resolution='Resolved'; } else { resolvedVal='B'; resolution='Irresolvable'; }
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the IABKContrBridge TypeScript interface (shouldIsolate, isolateContradiction, updateResolutionStatus, evaluateResolution) and its ABKContrBridge implementation: contradiction resolution sums signed evidential-polarity weights across conflicting sources and resolves to True (Resolved) if the sum exceeds +0.5, False (Resolved) if below -0.5, or remains contradictory (Irresolvable) if the weights are near-balanced -- a simple threshold-based weighted-voting resolution rule for the contradiction lifecycle.

type_signature.domain: a contradiction trap frame with polarity-weighted evidence edges
type_signature.codomain: a resolved (or still-contradictory) ABKState plus a ResolutionStatus

a_rows_sample.anchor: describe('ABK-1 / Contr Bridge Integration Suite' ... it('should detect contradictory valuations (B) and trigger isolation' ... it('should mark frame as Irresolvable when evidence weights cancel out' ...
a_rows_sample.statement: Provides a runnable Jest end-to-end integration test suite (abk-contr-integration.test.ts) covering contradiction detection and trap-frame creation, non-explosion verification (an isolated contradictory proposition does not pollute an unrelated proposition's algebra), and resolution-lifecycle management (transition through InProgress/Resolved, resolving to True when positive evidence dominates, and remaining Irresolvable when weights cancel).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Documents: RREQ-SPEC-v1.0, ABK-1-SPEC-v1.0, ABK-CONTR-v1.0 ... The Governing Insight: R_req is the semantic contract. ABK-1 is the implementation vehicle. ABK-1 achieves 100% compliance across all Tier P1 and P2 distinctions. The Contr Bridge provides non-explosive contradiction isolation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executive summary frames the package's governing insight: R_req is the semantic contract, ABK-1 is the implementation vehicle achieving claimed 100% compliance across Tier P1/P2, and the Contr Bridge provides non-explosive contradiction isolation -- packaging three previously-separate documents (R_req, ABK-1, ABK-Contr) plus a test-verification document for joint ratification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 5.2 What Remains OPEN: Contr Now has a concrete implementation path via ABK-1/Contr Bridge; Zero Now has formal definition via R_req compliance; delta Still open -- ABK-1 provides state representation but not transition semantics; Equality Still open -- D-1.4 provides identity distinctions but not full equality semantics; Kernel Selection Now has a candidate (ABK-1) that is R_req-compliant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evaluation: the tuple is promising, but not yet proven ... nu positive/negative standing Strong candidate; J justification/lineage Strong candidate; tau temporal qualification Candidate; mu modal/context scope Candidate; Product tuple as the canonical EVal OPEN. EVal != just a tuple of everything useful. We need to prove that each component is semantically necessary for the declared evaluation questions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Grades each component of the proposed EVal=<nu,J,tau,mu> tuple by separate epistemic status: nu (strong candidate), J (strong candidate), tau (candidate), mu (candidate), with the product tuple itself as the canonical EVal rated OPEN; states EVal is not merely a tuple of everything useful -- each component must be shown semantically necessary for the declared evaluation questions, or the exercise degenerates into constructing a database schema rather than deriving a kernel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 6 test cases (R-INV-01 through R-INV-06), each a Python function asserting the corresponding distinction is preserved (e.g. test_R_INV_01_standing_distinction asserts standing.S_plus != standing.S_minus and 'Failed R-INV-01: Standing collapsed to net scalar'; test_R_INV_03_state_distinction asserts eval_contr.state != eval_unknown.state) ... ABK-1 Compliance Status: 6/6 Tests Passed implies Adequacy(R_ABK-1, R_req) = 1.0
a_rows_sample.statement: SPEC-TEST-ABK1-2026-v1.0 provides a six-test Python compliance suite (one per R-INV, each with a test fixture using Context/Provenance/agent-id objects), reporting the ABK-1 representation passes all six (6/6), concluding Adequacy(R_ABK-1, R_req)=1.0 -- notably applying the SPEC-R-REQ-2026-v1.0 six-invariant taxonomy (Standing/Boundary/State/Provenance/Temporal/Reasoning) to the SAME ABK-1 architecture that earlier in this batch was tested and rated compliant against a different, D-1.x-numbered R_req taxonomy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ABK-1 -- representation candidate can be closed ... this does not prove: 'ABK-1 is the KnowledgeOS kernel.' It proves only: ABK-1 is adequate for the tested R_req. So: ABK-1 representation: CLOSED as a validated candidate. ABK-1 kernel: NOT CLOSED. This distinction is extremely important.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the scope of ABK-1's six-test PASS result: it proves ABK-1 is adequate for the TESTED R_req distinctions, not that 'ABK-1 is the KnowledgeOS kernel' -- ABK-1-as-representation is CLOSED as a validated candidate, but ABK-1-as-kernel remains NOT CLOSED, a distinction judged extremely important.

a_rows_sample.anchor: There is one additional missing bridge ... Adequacy -> Executability ... we need one more formal relation: ExecutableAdequacy. EA(K,O,Q,Gamma) meaning: the representation and operations together can answer the required questions while preserving every required distinction and producing an auditable transition. This is the real bridge from representation theory to kernel theory. Without it, ABK-1 can be perfectly adequate as a representation while still being insufficient as a kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Executable Adequacy EA(K,O,Q,Gamma) as a proposed missing formal relation between representation-adequacy theory and kernel theory: the representation K and operations O together must be able to answer the required questions Q while preserving every required distinction AND producing an auditable transition; without EA, a representation (e.g. ABK-1) could be perfectly Adequate(R,Q,Gamma) while still being insufficient as a kernel.

type_signature.domain: (representation K, operations O, question Q, context Gamma)

a_rows_sample.anchor: C1 Required Distinction Framework: CLOSED (with wording correction) R_req(Q,Gamma) subseteq D, not 'the non-negotiable subset of distinctions required by the system kernel' ... C2 Representation Adequacy: CLOSED ... C3 ABK-1 as Representation Candidate: CLOSED (as candidate, not kernel) ... C4 Non-Explosion Principle: CLOSED (principle only).
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally records four items as CLOSED (no further action needed): the Required Distinction Framework R_req (with the earlier circularity wording corrected to R_req(Q,Gamma) subseteq D), Representation Adequacy (Adequacy(R,Q,Gamma) iff R_req(Q,Gamma) subseteq Preserved(R,Gamma)), ABK-1 as a validated representation candidate (explicitly not as the kernel), and the Non-Explosion principle (as a principle only, not its exact isolation-boundary algorithm).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The ABK-1 '100% proof' is not actually a proof ... 6/6 tests passed implies Adequacy=1.0. That implication does not follow. Six tests demonstrate: adequate on six tested scenarios. They do not establish: forall x in R_req, Preserve(x). And the supplied tests are pseudocode against a hypothetical KnowledgeOSKernel, not evidence of an executed implementation. Therefore replace Adequacy=1.0 with: ABK1 passed all declared tests in the tested scope, and Adequacy_tested(ABK1,R_test)=1.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a statistical/mathematical fallacy in ABK-1's compliance claim: '6 of 6 tests passed implies Adequacy(R_ABK-1,R_req)=1.0' is an invalid generalization from finitely-tested scenarios to a universal quantifier over all of R_req; additionally notes the supplied tests are pseudocode against a hypothetical KnowledgeOSKernel class, not results from an executed implementation. Proposes the defensible replacement Adequacy_tested(ABK1,R_test)=1, explicitly scoped to the tested distinction set R_test rather than claiming universal Adequacy=1.0.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Four representative kernel candidates were evaluated against the Executable Adequacy matrix: K-FLAT (Flat RDF Triples): Collapses provenance, Global explosion -- REJECTED. K-FDE (Pure FDE Bilattice): Preserves truth values but Scalar collapse -- REJECTED. K-REL (Relational Projections): Preserves schema, Scoped constraints, but Join explosion -- REJECTED. ABK-1 (Attributed Bipartite Graph): Preserves R_req, Scoped Firewalls, O(|V|+|E|), Deterministic -- SELECTED. ABK-1 is the unique minimal Kernel Architecture satisfying EA(M*,Q,Gamma).
b_rows_sample.statement: Performs the batch's first actual comparative kernel-selection evaluation: four named candidate architectures are scored against the four Executable Adequacy dimensions. K-FLAT (flat RDF triples) fails Soundness (collapses provenance) and Isolation (global explosion); K-FDE (pure FDE bilattice) preserves truth values but fails Isolation (scalar collapse); K-REL (relational projections) preserves schema and scoped constraints but fails Termination (join explosion); ABK-1 (Attributed Bipartite Graph) passes all four dimensions. Declares ABK-1 'the unique minimal Kernel Architecture satisfying EA(M*,Q,Gamma)'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Master Status Register Consolidation: With the execution and ratification of CLOSURE-5, all closure vectors across the KnowledgeOS architecture are finalized. CLOSURE-1 through CLOSURE-5: all RATIFIED.
b_rows_sample.statement: Declares all five CLOSURE vectors (Evaluation, Determination, Operations Algebra, Semantic Equivalence/Composition, Executable Adequacy/Kernel Selection) RATIFIED and finalized, the concluding governance statement of this file's closure sequence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The document is a good consolidation, but I would NOT ratify it as 'KnowledgeOS Kernel Theory v1.3 fully closed and complete.' ... it correctly identifies the earlier over-claims, but then reintroduces essentially the same problem at CLOSURE-3/4/5: a small executable demonstration is being promoted into a mathematical/architectural proof.
b_rows_sample.statement: Overall verdict: accepts the CLOSURE consolidation's Section-1 downgrades as sound but refuses to ratify the whole document as complete, identifying that CLOSURE-3/4/5 repeat the exact same error-pattern the earlier sections corrected -- promoting a small executable demonstration into a mathematical/architectural proof.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CLOSURE-5 is where the document fails the strongest test ... the EA test is not actually testing the stated predicates. Soundness: the declared requirement is forall d in R_req: Preserve(d,...)=true. But the implementation only checks 'provenance' in node for active nodes ... required_distinctions=['provenance','isolation_boundary'] but does not actually verify both distinctions. So: Declared R_req != Tested R_req. That invalidates the claimed general soundness result.
b_rows_sample.statement: Audits the CLOSURE-5 Soundness test's implementation against its stated predicate and finds a mismatch: the code passes a required_distinctions list of two items (provenance, isolation_boundary) but the check_adequacy implementation only tests presence of a 'provenance' key on active nodes, never actually checking the second declared distinction -- Declared R_req != Tested R_req, invalidating the claimed general soundness result for that test.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Isolation test is effectively tautological ... It checks whether a node that is not the firewall target is also in the firewall set. It does not actually execute Det(EVal(K_isolated,q,Gamma)) and verify that the clean node remains determinable. So the mathematical requirement q not-in Scope(Contr(p),Gamma) implies Actionability != BLOCKED is not what the test implements. It tests a much weaker structural property.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies that the CLOSURE-5 Psi_Isolation test is tautological: it merely checks that a non-firewall-target node is not itself in the firewall set (structurally true by construction), and never actually calls Det(EVal(...)) to verify the clean node remains determinable with non-BLOCKED actionability -- the implemented check is strictly weaker than the stated mathematical requirement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The termination test is not a complexity proof ... T <= C(|V|+|E|) but the implementation checks elapsed<0.05 ... A 50ms runtime on one small graph cannot establish O(|V|+|E|). Complexity requires analysis of the algorithm or systematic scaling experiments. Therefore: Termination: NOT VERIFIED. At most: implementation completed within the selected benchmark timeout.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies that the CLOSURE-5 Psi_Termination test (a single 50ms wall-clock timeout check on one small graph) does not and cannot establish the claimed asymptotic bound T<=C(|V|+|E|); asymptotic complexity requires algorithmic analysis or systematic scaling experiments across graph sizes, neither of which is present. Downgrades the finding to 'implementation completed within the selected benchmark timeout', marking Termination NOT VERIFIED.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Determinism test is the strongest CLOSURE-5 result ... Replay of the same operations from the same initial state gives the same state hash ... But even here, it proves determinism of that implementation, not determinism of ABK-1 as a mathematical architecture. ... Replay determinism: tested. Constitutional determinism: candidate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Judges the CLOSURE-5 Psi_Determinism test the strongest of the four (replaying the same operation sequence from the same initial state reproduces the identical state hash), but scopes the result carefully: it proves determinism of that specific implementation, not of ABK-1 as a mathematical architecture in general, and notes deterministic hashing depends on canonical serialization -- classifying Replay determinism as tested but Constitutional determinism only as candidate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Unique minimal' ABK-1 is not demonstrated ... The candidate table compares four representations. That can establish at most: ABK-1 was the only candidate among these four tested candidates that passed the declared test suite. It cannot establish: ABK-1=unique minimal architecture unless you have [7 listed requirements]. None of those are demonstrated. So: ABK-1 SELECTED FROM TESTED CANDIDATES may be defensible later. But: ABK-1 mathematically proved uniquely minimal is not.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the 'ABK-1 is the unique minimal Kernel Architecture' claim as unsupported: the four-candidate comparison establishes at most that ABK-1 was the only one of these four tested candidates to pass the declared test suite, which is not the same as mathematical uniqueness-and-minimality, which would require a defined candidate space, an explicit minimality ordering, exhaustive or justified candidate coverage, valid adequacy predicates and implementations, independent test scenarios, and no hidden favoritism toward ABK-1 -- none of which are demonstrated. Proposes the defensible restatement 'ABK-1 SELECTED FROM TESTED CANDIDATES'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: There is also a serious circularity in CLOSURE-5 ... the candidate being evaluated is already defined with: nodes, edges, firewalls, provenance. And the EA tests require: provenance, isolation. So the candidate is structurally equipped with the exact properties the test asks for. This creates a potential representation-selection circularity: ABK-1 -> defines tested distinctions -> EA -> ABK-1 passes. rather than: R_req -> independent adequacy criteria -> candidate comparison -> selection.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a representation-selection circularity in the CLOSURE-5 kernel-selection process: ABK-1's own data structure (nodes/edges/firewalls/provenance) already contains exactly the fields the Executable Adequacy test checks for, so the process runs ABK-1 -> defines tested distinctions -> EA -> ABK-1 passes rather than the intended independent chain R_req -> independent adequacy criteria -> candidate comparison -> selection; warns this is a structural risk regardless of whether it was deliberate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would reduce the remaining work to four decisive packages. C1 -- Determination semantics ... No Actionability inside Determination. C2 -- Operations + delta ... C3 -- Composition + equivalence ... define approx_{Q,Gamma,O} as observational equivalence first. Only promote it to semantic equivalence if a bridge is established. C4 -- Independent kernel selection ... The test must be candidate-independent. R_req -> Adequacy Criteria -> Independent Test Suite -> Candidate Architectures -> Evidence -> Selection. I would still avoid 'unique minimal' unless we formally prove minimality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reduces remaining closure work to four decisive packages: C1 Determination semantics (excluding Actionability); C2 Operations+delta (per-operation Pre/Input/Post/Invariants/Provenance/Failure/Partiality, then test delta against identity/persistence/retraction/supersession/invalidation/isolation/provenance); C3 Composition+equivalence (establish composition-algebra properties, define observational equivalence FIRST and only promote to semantic equivalence if a bridge is separately established); C4 Independent, candidate-blind kernel selection following the chain R_req->AdequacyCriteria->IndependentTestSuite->CandidateArchitectures->Evidence->Selection, still avoiding 'unique minimal' language unless minimality is formally proven.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would issue: CLOSURE-SYNTHESIS-2026-v1.3 -- Falsification Correction with a very explicit distinction: Ratified constitutional principles versus Validated candidate mechanisms versus Open mathematical parameters versus Unverified implementation claims. ... My senior review is: Discovery phase: CLOSED. Constitutional principles: substantially established. Kernel candidate ABK-1: strongly motivated, not proven. Kernel reduction: NOT YET CLOSED.
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends a next artifact 'CLOSURE-SYNTHESIS-2026-v1.3 -- Falsification Correction' organized around a four-way status taxonomy (Ratified constitutional principles / Validated candidate mechanisms / Open mathematical parameters / Unverified implementation claims); final verdict: Discovery phase CLOSED, constitutional principles substantially established, ABK-1 as kernel candidate strongly motivated but not proven, Kernel reduction NOT YET CLOSED. Recommends building an independent falsification suite for CLOSURE-1 through CLOSURE-5 as the single most important next task, starting with Det, then composition/equivalence, then candidate-independent EA.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The closure packages (C1-C5) have successfully completed the formal closure of KnowledgeOS Theory v1.3. This is the most disciplined architectural derivation I have witnessed in this programme ... Verdict: [READY FOR RATIFICATION].
b_rows_sample.statement: Declares the C1-C5 closure packages have 'successfully completed the formal closure of KnowledgeOS Theory v1.3' and calls the derivation 'the most disciplined... I have witnessed in this programme', issuing verdict READY FOR RATIFICATION -- directly contradicting the immediately preceding file's (S2584) refusal to ratify the same C1-C5 packages and its specific finding that CLOSURE-3/4/5 'reintroduce essentially the same [overclaiming] problem' as the corrections they were meant to fix.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 5.2 What Remains: Nothing. The formal closure is complete.
b_rows_sample.statement: States plainly that nothing remains open and formal closure is complete -- the single strongest overclaim in this batch's entire closure-cascade lineage, issued despite an intervening review in this same batch (S2584) that explicitly listed at minimum four decisive remaining packages (Determination semantics without Actionability, Operations+delta per-operation identity resolution, Composition+equivalence algebraic properties, and independent candidate-blind kernel selection).

b_rows_sample.anchor: No -- I would not close KnowledgeOS Theory v1.3 yet ... The document repeatedly moves from 1 (a specification being written) -> 2 (an implementation satisfying that specification on one test case) -> 4 (a kernel architecture being uniquely selected) without establishing the necessary bridges ... EA(M*) implies KernelReductionComplete implies ABK-1 is not established.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the central diagnostic distinction of the review: a specification being written, an implementation satisfying it on one test case, a theory being mathematically closed, and a kernel architecture being uniquely selected are four different things, and the reviewed document repeatedly jumps from step 1 to step 2 directly to step 4 without establishing the intermediate bridges -- most visibly in CLOSURE-5's unestablished EA(M*) => KernelReductionComplete => ABK-1 inference.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What CAN be closed now? ... I would close these: 1. Epistemic separation ... 2. Non-explosion ... 3. Required distinctions R_req(Q,Gamma) subseteq D ... 4. Representation adequacy principle ... 5. Provenance preservation ... 6. Historical state preservation ... 7. Kernel/non-kernel responsibility separation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists seven constitutional principles judged genuinely closeable now: epistemic separation (Truth!=Evaluation!=Determination!=Decision), the non-explosion principle, the required-distinctions framework R_req(Q,Gamma) subseteq D, representation adequacy relative to a question/context, provenance preservation, historical-state preservation (retraction != physical deletion), and kernel/non-kernel responsibility separation (queries/explanations/governance are not automatic kernel state mutations).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Specification != Verification != Selection. And: Passed Test != Mathematical Proof. ... ~80-85% of the constitutional theory is mature enough to freeze; the remaining 15-20% is concentrated in a small number of mathematically decisive coupling problems.
b_rows_sample.statement: States two summary maxims distinguishing Specification from Verification from Selection, and Passed Test from Mathematical Proof, as the central methodological lesson of the review; gives a quantitative maturity estimate that roughly 80-85% of the constitutional theory is mature enough to freeze, with the remaining 15-20% concentrated in a small number of mathematically decisive coupling problems.

b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms the newer material's rescinded status (Discovery CLOSED, Constitutional Core CLOSED, Kernel Theory OPEN/closure-blocked) as the correct starting point, while judging the project close to a legitimate theoretical stopping point but not yet entitled to declare kernel theory mathematically closed or ABK-1 finally selected.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'kernel-candidate-comparison-abk1-selected' POSSIBLY relates to 'abk-1-annotated-bilattice-kernel-candidate' (batch B0062). Note: The first actual comparative kernel-selection act in this batch's closure cascade: four named candidate architectures are evaluated against the four-dimension Executable Adequacy matrix (Psi_Soundness/Isolation/Termination/Determinism) -- K-FLAT (flat RDF triples) REJECTED for collapsing provenance and permitting global explosion; K-FDE (pure FDE bilattice) REJECTED for scalar collapse despite preserving truth values; K-REL (relational projections) REJECTED for join explosion despite preserving schema and scoped constraints; ABK-1 (Attributed Bipartite Graph) passes all four dimensions and is declared 'the unique minimal Kernel Architecture satisfying EA', with a Python ExecutableAdequacyEvaluator harness and a passing test.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AAG=(V,E) ... V=V_C∪V_K∪V_I∪V_E∪V_T∪V_F
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Architecture Assurance Graph AAG=(V,E) with node types V_C (components/bounded contexts), V_K (contracts), V_I (invariants), V_E (enforcement mechanisms), V_T (verification tests), V_F (evidence/artifacts), and typed edges Component-owns->Invariant, Contract-carries->SemanticProperty, Mechanism-enforces->Invariant, Test-verifies->Invariant, Evidence-supports->Test/Claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I -> Owner -> Mechanism -> Test -> Evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: For a critical property I, the complete assurance chain is I->Owner->Mechanism->Test->Evidence; a missing edge is potentially an assurance gap. Worked example: I_Authority->Governance->AuthorizationPolicy->NegativeTest->TestEvidence is a complete chain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A — Defined and enforced ... D — Claimed but unverifiable
a_rows_sample.statement: Every invariant is classified into one of four situations: (A) defined and enforced and verified; (B) defined but not enforced (M=empty); (C) implemented but not architecturally declared (a mechanism exists but nobody established which invariant it protects); (D) claimed but unverifiable (documentation asserts I=True but no evidence exists). D is flagged as particularly dangerous.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Gap(I)=RequiredAssurance(I)-ActualAssurance(I) ... Gap(I) in {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical}
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines assurance gap conceptually as Gap(I)=RequiredAssurance(I)-ActualAssurance(I), explicitly refusing to assign arbitrary numerical values and instead classifying into {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} 'until we establish a justified scoring model'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Component correctness =/=> System correctness
a_rows_sample.statement: An architecture may have every individual bounded context (Evidence, Assessment, Governance) correct while still having a critical global assurance gap, e.g. if the contract Assessment->Governance silently drops uncertainty; boxed conclusion: component correctness does not imply system correctness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance(I_global) <= min{Assurance(I_1),Assurance(I_2),...}
a_rows_sample.statement: States a weakest-link property: for a critical end-to-end property I_global, assurance is bounded by the minimum assurance of its constituent links, explicitly qualified as 'not a universal mathematical law; it is a useful conservative assurance model' — if one indispensable boundary lacks a provenance guarantee, end-to-end provenance cannot be honestly claimed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Traceability_syntactic=True but Traceability_historical=False
a_rows_sample.statement: Decision traceability example D->A->E: traceability is only True if each reference (Decision->Assessment ID->Evidence ID) remains resolvable and semantically versioned; if the Assessment ID resolves only to the latest Assessment, syntactic traceability can hold while historical traceability fails — 'this distinction is crucial'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SyntacticCorrectness =/= SemanticCorrectness ... HTTP 200 ... JSON schema valid
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes SyntacticCorrectness != SemanticCorrectness: an HTTP 200 proves transport success but not BusinessMeaningCorrect; a valid JSON schema does not prove SemanticContractValid.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A=(A_s,A_m,A_e,A_t,A_p,A_g)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate six-dimension KnowledgeOS assurance vector A=(A_s,A_m,A_e,A_t,A_p,A_g): A_s structural (component exists, boundary explicit, dependencies controlled, contracts defined), A_m semantic (meaning preserved, no overloaded concept, no Boolean replacing a richer state), A_e epistemic/statistical (evidence, inference, assumptions, uncertainty, correlation vs causation, model version), A_t temporal (which version/policy/model applied when, historical reconstructability), A_p provenance (claim origin, traversable chain), A_g governance (who was authorized, under which valid policy, permission vs execution).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues a single global assurance score is dangerous: if A_s=1 but A_p=0, a scalar like 0.83 could falsely imply reasonable assurance, whereas for critical systems one missing indispensable property may be enough to block certification; boxed principle: vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization — an explicit statistical-design principle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C0 — Informational ... C4 — Critical assurance
a_rows_sample.statement: Provisionally classifies invariant criticality into five levels: C0 Informational (documentation/style), C1 Functional (normal business behavior), C2 Semantic (meaning/context preservation), C3 Governance (authority/policy/compliance), C4 Critical assurance (safety, irreversible action, high-impact decision, legally significant state); flagged as needing later validation against real KnowledgeOS use cases.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Mechanism(I)=f(Criticality(I))
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes assurance-mechanism selection as a function of criticality: low-risk -> Documentation+UnitTest; medium -> IntegrationTest+ContractTest; high -> PropertyBasedTest+Replay+AuditEvidence; critical -> FormalModel/Proof where practical — self-labeled 'a proposed framework, not yet a frozen standard'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A=(InputRef,ModelRef,InstructionRef,Output,Uncertainty,Validation,Provenance)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an AI-generated-artifact metadata schema A=(InputRef,ModelRef,InstructionRef,Output,Uncertainty,Validation,Provenance), stating the schema must be derived from the actual KnowledgeOS implementation but conceptually AI output should not be treated as an unexplained opaque fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AI -> CandidateResult -> DeterministicValidation -> AcceptedArtifact. Not: AI -> ProductionTruth
a_rows_sample.statement: States the architecture must route AI output through AI->CandidateResult->DeterministicValidation->AcceptedArtifact, never directly AI->ProductionTruth, calling this distinction 'central to our KnowledgeOS design'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TrustedFor(x,p,t) ... Valid(x,Context,Time,Purpose)
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns against another bare Boolean (`trusted = true`); trust/assurance must be contextual, TrustedFor(x,p,t) — an artifact trustworthy for Task_1 need not be trustworthy for Task_2. Generalizes to Valid(x) being usually incomplete; the better form is Valid(x,Context,Time,Purpose), called 'a major insight for KnowledgeOS': validity is not absolute but ValidForPurpose(P).

a_rows_sample.anchor: StructuralValid ... SemanticValid ... EpistemicallyValid ... TemporallyValid ... GovernanceValid
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes five validity types (Structural/Semantic/Epistemic/Temporal/Governance Valid), concluding Valid(x) should be treated as shorthand only when the intended dimension is explicitly known.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Different missing edges represent different classes of architectural weakness
a_rows_sample.statement: States the missing-node principle: Invariant->Owner with no Enforcement is a design gap; Enforcement->Test missing is an assurance gap; Test->Evidence missing is an auditability gap — different missing edges are different classes of architectural weakness, letting the architecture 'diagnose itself' via forall I_i: Complete(AAG(I_i))? producing a reproducible gap report.

a_rows_sample.anchor: System -> Output + EvidenceOfCorrectness
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the architecture's strongest form as System->Output+EvidenceOfCorrectness rather than merely System->Output, stated as precisely what deterministic assurance is trying to accomplish.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We should not claim: 'The architecture is mathematically proven.' ... FormalizableArchitecture
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit self-warning: the architecture must not be claimed as mathematically proven; what exists is a FormalizableArchitecture, and the next task is determining which portions can actually be Formalized->Specified->Verified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### DDD ... VERY STRONG ... Gītā 1–4 ... DEEP CONSISTENCY
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 211 verdict: DDD, Mathematics, Statistics, Governance, and AI are each rated VERY STRONG, and Gita chapters 1-4 rated DEEP CONSISTENCY, citing continued distinctions Identity!=State, Knowledge!=Action, Capability!=Authority, PastState!=CurrentState, Decision!=Outcome.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status) ... EL=∪_i EL_i
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence Ledger as a per-step 10-field record EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status), with the overall ledger EL as the union across all steps, turning step 213's F/D/P/U discipline into a working data structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation -> Fact -> Derivation -> Architectural Principle -> Invariant ... Invariant -> Implementation -> Test -> Evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: States the ledger's two-directional fundamental chain (forward: Observation->Fact->Derivation->Architectural Principle->Invariant; feedback: Invariant->Implementation->Test->Evidence->New Knowledge), diagrammed as the architecture's epistemic feedback loop.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge_t != Knowledge_{t+1} ... The fact that H_2 is better does not mean H_1 never existed
b_rows_sample.statement: States that the ledger must preserve chronology (when a belief was held), not only its content, since a later, better hypothesis H2 does not erase the historical fact that an earlier hypothesis H1 was held -- essential to reconstructing the real engineering journey rather than a retrospectively idealized one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Calendar chronology ... Engineering chronology ... Epistemic chronology ... The code may exist before the architectural concept has been named
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three non-identical chronologies (calendar: when it happened; engineering: what was built before what; epistemic: when it was understood), illustrated by Implementation->Observation->Understanding, where code can precede the naming of its own underlying architectural concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: implementation -> repeated problem -> experiment -> pattern recognized -> concept named ... The later name should not be projected backward as though it had been consciously designed from the beginning
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the 'late naming' phenomenon: a pattern can exist implicitly in the implementation before it is given a formal concept name, and warns against projecting the later name backward as if it had been consciously designed from the start, since that would distort the history.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | Field | Purpose | ... Rejected alternative | What was not chosen |
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a practical 15-field Evidence Ledger schema (Step ID, Artifact, Date/sequence, Observation, Fact, Interpretation, Derived principle, Decision, Rejected alternative, Architectural consequence, Invariant, Verification, Evidence status F/D/P/U, Confidence, Open question).

b_rows_sample.anchor: What we rejected ... as by: What we selected ... That rejection itself is architectural knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues architecture is defined as much by what was rejected as by what was selected (e.g. Alternative A rejected because SemanticLoss(A)>0), justifying a dedicated 'Rejected alternative' ledger field as architectural knowledge in its own right.

b_rows_sample.anchor: NegativeKnowledge ... knowledge about approaches, assumptions, transitions or interpretations that have been demonstrated to be unsuitable under specified conditions ... different from failure
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces NegativeKnowledge as knowledge about approaches/assumptions/transitions/interpretations demonstrated unsuitable under specified conditions, distinguished from mere failure -- a failure becomes useful (negative) knowledge only once its cause ('why it failed') is understood.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment=(Hypothesis,Setup,Observation,Result,Interpretation,Consequence) ... Result -> Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-field experimental-lineage record (Hypothesis, Setup, Observation, Result, Interpretation, Consequence) intended to let the eventual book demonstrate the scientific/engineering nature of the work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A hypothesis says: X may be true ... An invariant says: X must remain true ... Hypothesis -[evidence]-> Pattern -[validation]-> Invariant. Not every hypothesis becomes an invariant
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes hypothesis (X may be true) from invariant (X must remain true) and defines the promotion pipeline Hypothesis->(evidence)->Pattern->(validation)->Invariant, explicitly noting not every hypothesis is promoted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observed(H) does not imply Universal(H) ... AllAI -> InconsistentCode [is unwarranted from one tested workflow]
b_rows_sample.statement: States a statistical-discipline guardrail: evidence for H under tested conditions (Observed(H)) must not be generalized to Universal(H), illustrated by a prompt-strategy-specific inconsistency finding that must not be generalized to all AI.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) ... Valid(C) should really mean: Valid(C | Context,Conditions)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes representing every conclusion as Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) so that validity is always conditioned (Valid(C|Context,Conditions) rather than bare Valid(C)), framed as a connection between DDD and statistical reasoning; extends this to bounded knowledge (Knowledge_A != Knowledge_B across DDD bounded contexts, requiring an explicit ubiquitous-language-guarded translation when a concept crosses a context boundary).

b_rows_sample.anchor: p(C_A) => p'(C_B) ... where p' is the explicitly defined interpretation in the target context. If that implication does not hold, the contract may introduce semantic loss
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a semantic-preservation condition for cross-context evidence transfer: a property p holding in context C_A after transformation T to C_B must imply the target-context-defined interpretation p' holds in C_B, or the contract introduces semantic loss; states evidence for a claim in one context does not automatically establish it in another without an explicit Mapping and evidence the property survives translation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ELG=(V,E) ... V=Artifacts∪Facts∪Observations∪Hypotheses∪Decisions∪Principles∪Invariants ... substantially richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence Ledger as a graph ELG=(V,E) with seven node types (artifacts, facts, observations, hypotheses, decisions, principles, invariants) and seven edge types (supports, contradicts, derives, motivates, rejects, implements, verifies), explicitly positioned as richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C_1 <-[contradicts]-> C_2 ... We should not immediately delete one. Instead record: Contradiction(C_1,C_2) ... Sometimes the contradiction disappears once context is made explicit
b_rows_sample.statement: Treats contradiction as a first-class graph edge to be recorded rather than resolved by deletion; investigating Context(C_1) vs Context(C_2) can dissolve an apparent contradiction, and more generally an apparent contradiction (ModelA accurate vs inaccurate) can resolve into conditional coherence once Context/Population/Time/Purpose dimensions are introduced -- framed as contradiction potentially revealing a missing dimension.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Generation != Adjudication ... Candidates -> Evidence -> Adjudication -> AcceptedKnowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the contradiction-as-evidence principle to AI-generated competing interpretations: rather than declaring one AI output true and another false, treats {AI_1,AI_2} as an explicit candidate knowledge set requiring adjudication, architecturally separating Generation from Adjudication via Candidates->Evidence->Adjudication->AcceptedKnowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KState in {Observed,Hypothesized,Derived,Corroborated,Contested,Rejected,Accepted,Deprecated} ... should not automatically be treated as a single linear lifecycle ... Accepted + Contested
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an eight-value knowledge-item epistemic state (Observed/Hypothesized/Derived/Corroborated/Contested/Rejected/Accepted/Deprecated), explicitly not a single linear lifecycle -- states may coexist, e.g. Accepted+Contested when knowledge is operationally accepted but still scientifically disputed; reiterates the anti-Boolean discipline (verified=true is insufficient; use KnowledgeState+Evidence+Context+Time).

b_rows_sample.anchor: UnderlyingPrinciple != CurrentManifestation ... The analogy helps us ask better architecture questions. It does not prove them
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies a Gita chapter-4 analogy (enduring knowledge vs changing manifestation) to DomainInvariant!=CurrentRuntimeState and HistoricalKnowledge!=CurrentRepresentation, explicitly bounding the analogy as interpretive/heuristic ('helps us ask better questions, does not prove them').

b_rows_sample.anchor: S_{t+1} does not contain all information about S_t ... S_{t+1} ⊉ S_t ... CurrentState + HistoricalRecord -> HistoricalUnderstanding
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the 'new state does not know old state' principle as S_{t+1} not-superset-of S_t in general, requiring an additional historical mechanism H_t; concludes CurrentState alone is insufficient and CurrentState+HistoricalRecord is needed for HistoricalUnderstanding, distinguishing CurrentState, HistoricalRecord, and HistoricalInterpretation as three different things.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) ... Update does not necessarily erase prior knowledge ... KnowledgeVersion [distinct from] KnowledgeState ... Git commit != current working tree
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a knowledge-continuity model K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) with K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_{t+1}), where Update may supersede/qualify/contradict/preserve/deprecate rather than erase prior knowledge; proposes distinguishing KnowledgeVersion from KnowledgeState by analogy to a git commit vs the current working tree, again explicitly flagged as analogy not proof.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Freedman repeatedly attacks hidden assumptions. ... assumptions are frequently not stated or tested, and when assumptions fail, the mathematical guarantees of the method no longer apply.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes Assumption as a first-class object under Model (statement/type/justification/evidence/testability/status/consequence_if_false/scope) with states SUPPORTED/PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED/UNSUPPORTED/UNTESTED/UNTESTABLE/CONTRADICTED, illustrated with the example assumption 'The observations are independent' (status: unverified, testability: limited, consequence_if_false: confidence_intervals_invalid, inference_weakened); introduces an AssumptionLedger chaining Research Question -> Model -> per-assumption evidence/status.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 82.54 — This is a major KnowledgeOS property ... A change in Assumption can propagate through Model→Prediction→Decision. Therefore assumptions need dependency lineage.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that because a change in an Assumption can propagate through Model→Prediction→Decision, assumptions require explicit dependency lineage tracking.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Freedman repeatedly attacks hidden assumptions. ... assumptions are frequently not stated or tested, and when assumptions fail, the mathematical guarantees of the method no longer apply.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes Assumption as a first-class object under Model (statement/type/justification/evidence/testability/status/consequence_if_false/scope) with states SUPPORTED/PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED/UNSUPPORTED/UNTESTED/UNTESTABLE/CONTRADICTED, illustrated with the example assumption 'The observations are independent' (status: unverified, testability: limited, consequence_if_false: confidence_intervals_invalid, inference_weakened); introduces an AssumptionLedger chaining Research Question -> Model -> per-assumption evidence/status.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the AI output becomes: Recommendation / Evidence / Assumptions / Reasoning / Alternatives / Contradictions / Scope / Failure Conditions. That is much more trustworthy than a generic 'confidence score.'
b_rows_sample.statement: AI must not hide assumptions: for any recommendation, the system should elicit why/what-assumptions/what-evidence-supports/what-evidence-contradicts/what-alternatives/what-would-make-it-wrong, restructuring AI output as Recommendation{Evidence, Assumptions, Reasoning, Alternatives, Contradictions, Scope, Failure Conditions} rather than a bare confidence score.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation, Evidence, Inference, Claim, Assumption, Model, ResearchQuestion, ResearchDesign, Mechanism, RivalExplanation, Confounder, Validation, IdentificationAssessment, Anomaly, Uncertainty ... I would not automatically create duplicates.
b_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates the most important new candidate domain objects to add to the KnowledgeOS conceptual model (Observation, Evidence, Inference, Claim, Assumption, Model, ResearchQuestion, ResearchDesign, Mechanism, RivalExplanation, Confounder, Validation, IdentificationAssessment, Anomaly, Uncertainty), with an explicit caution that some may already exist under different names and duplicates should not automatically be created.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A model does not validate its own assumptions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Invariant 3: A model does not validate its own assumptions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: data alone are insufficient; identifying assumptions must be supplied. ... Exchangeability / Positivity / Consistency ... claims about the conditions under which an inference is valid.
b_rows_sample.statement: Assumption Lens: exchangeability, positivity, and consistency are identifying assumptions (not mathematical details but claims about validity conditions); Inference should store evidence/method/assumptions/assumption_provenance/assumption_status/conclusion, described as a 'huge architectural fit' with existing evidence/assurance/governance emphasis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 82.51 — Experiment 25 ... Causal estimate assumes NoUnmeasuredConfounding. But that assumption is unverified. Expected: AssumptionRisk must be exposed. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 25: a causal estimate resting on an unverified NoUnmeasuredConfounding assumption must have that AssumptionRisk exposed; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 82.52 — Assumptions are first-class ... Assumption(A) with Status: Supported or Unverified or Contradicted.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes Assumption(A) as a first-class object carrying a Status in {Supported, Unverified, Contradicted}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 82.53 — Experiment 26 ... Decision depends on assumption A. A becomes contradicted. Expected: DependentDecision must be reconsidered. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 26: a decision that depended on assumption A must be flagged for reconsideration when A becomes Contradicted; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 82.54 — This is a major KnowledgeOS property ... A change in Assumption can propagate through Model→Prediction→Decision. Therefore assumptions need dependency lineage.
b_rows_sample.statement: States that because a change in an Assumption can propagate through Model→Prediction→Decision, assumptions require explicit dependency lineage tracking.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 84.31 — Causal assumptions become first-class knowledge ... A1: NoUnmeasuredConfounding. A2: StableTreatmentDefinition. A3: NoInterference. A4: CorrectTemporalOrdering. Each assumption has evidence status.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names four standard causal-inference assumptions as first-class knowledge objects with evidence status: A1 NoUnmeasuredConfounding, A2 StableTreatmentDefinition (SUTVA-related), A3 NoInterference, A4 CorrectTemporalOrdering.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 84.32 — Experiment 15 ... Counterfactual depends on A1. Later evidence contradicts A1. Expected: CounterfactualInvalidation. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 15: when evidence later contradicts an assumption (A1) a dependent counterfactual relied on, the counterfactual must undergo CounterfactualInvalidation; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Language test · Ownership test · Change-reason test ... A context can pass all three with no code (rules-only contexts are real)
a_rows_sample.statement: A three-part strategic-DDD test (language, ownership, change-reason) is applied to every declared bounded context, explicitly allowing a context with zero executable realization to still pass (rules-only contexts are real), while a context failing the language test cannot be rescued by code.

a_rows_sample.anchor: BC-1..BC-6 verdict table: CONFIRM boundary UNRESOLVED (BC-1) · CONFIRM but overloaded (BC-2) · CONFIRM (BC-3) · CONFIRM capability/CHALLENGE context (BC-4) · CHALLENGE as declared Core (BC-5) · CONFIRM cleanest boundary (BC-6)
a_rows_sample.statement: Each of the six declared bounded contexts receives a distinct strategic verdict from the three-part test: BC-1 confirmed but with a possibly-two-systems internal boundary unresolved; BC-2 confirmed but overloaded (hosts a second, foreign orchestration language); BC-3 confirmed cleanly; BC-4's capability is real but its context status is challenged (no state, no component, realized only by role model and human acts); BC-5's declared-Core status is challenged as not matching the measured center of gravity; BC-6 is the cleanest confirmed boundary in the system.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PROMOTE TO CANDIDATE BC-7 ... the strongest candidate on the record
a_rows_sample.statement: An undeclared area realized entirely by workflow-record mechanisms (work item, session, role, transition, grant, handoff, human act) is promoted from the baseline's low-confidence Inferred status to the strongest candidate bounded context, named 'Governed Session Orchestration' (candidate BC-7), pending an ADR since it would reverse a recorded Increment-1 parsimony decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: M-1..M-5 Misplaced responsibilities ... M-3 Composition root (CMP-001) | registry only — no declared context at all
a_rows_sample.statement: Five misplaced-responsibility findings are recorded, including the workflow-record mechanism sitting in the wrong declared context (M-1), the platform registry sitting under Design & Decision Support rather than its own governance context (M-2), and the composition root having no declared context home at all (M-3).

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-1..C-6 Coupling problems ... Authority state has no provenance — all workflow records gitignored, zero history
a_rows_sample.statement: Six coupling problems are recorded, most materially that the candidate orchestration context's own authority store has no provenance (gitignored, zero history, C-3) despite the context's purpose being auditable authority, and that the registry-first contract is declared binding but measured bypassable by three unregistered hooks (C-6).

a_rows_sample.anchor: PLATFORM → PRODUCT (PublicDigit / Election = declared CORE DOMAIN, AIP-14) ... platform reads/guards app/; product never invokes platform
a_rows_sample.statement: A current-state context map is produced showing the human PO/ARB as the authority origin flowing through a governance-registering role into the candidate orchestration context, out to the other declared contexts, and states the platform-to-product relationship as a one-way Supporting-to-Core guard seam that is never inverted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ADR-C1 Recognize or decline BC-7 Governed Session Orchestration ... highest — every other boundary question touches it
a_rows_sample.statement: Eight ADR candidates (ADR-C1..C7) are proposed as future governed decisions, with ADR-C1 (recognize/decline BC-7) marked highest priority since every other boundary question in the report depends on it; drafting and deciding them is explicitly left to future PO/ARB work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Create Architecture Landscape v2: update the bounded-context map from 6 to 7 contexts · introduce BC-7 Governed Session Orchestration · update the capability map with CAP-14
a_rows_sample.statement: KOS-ARCH-BASELINE-002 is commissioned to formally grow the strategic model from 6 to 7 bounded contexts, recognizing BC-7 and assigning it CAP-14, following the ADR-AIP-03 decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The seven-context strategic model is the authoritative architecture model ... ADR-AIP-01's frozen six-context table is hereby amended
a_rows_sample.statement: The PO/ARB formally accepts the seven-context strategic model (Landscape v2, Context Map v2, Capability Map v2), which amends ADR-AIP-01's previously frozen six-context table, recognizing BC-7 as a Supporting Subdomain with CAP-14.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The platform's strategic model grows from six declared bounded contexts to seven: BC-7 Governed Session Orchestration — the context the platform was already organized around
a_rows_sample.statement: The Architecture Landscape v2's central statement: BC-7 is recognized as the context the platform was already organized around, receiving its declared boundary, capability (CAP-14), and relationships, while all physical component placement remains unchanged (a model-level change only).

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD-as-analysis: bounded-context/aggregate identification is candidate-only, derived from language · ownership · invariants · lifecycle · authority · consistency · dependency direction — never from folders/containers/repos/deployment units. No formal DDD validation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Bounded-context and aggregate identification in this archaeology is candidate-only, derived from language, ownership, invariants, lifecycle, authority, consistency, and dependency direction -- never from folder/container/repository/deployment-unit structure -- and constitutes no formal DDD validation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ownership discipline (recorded): BC-1 owns knowledge governance but is not built
a_rows_sample.statement: BC-1..BC-7 to CAP-01..14 ownership table: BC-1 Knowledge Governance/CAP-03 (NOT BUILT, convention only); BC-2 Implementation Guidance/CAP-05-06 (A); BC-3 Verification & Evidence/CAP-07-09 (C, guard surface, gate execution planned); BC-4 Adversarial Review/CAP-11 (E, deferred); BC-5 Design & Decision Support/CAP-10,12,13 (A); BC-6 Session Continuity/CAP-01-02 (A); BC-7 Governed Session Orchestration/CAP-14 (A, workflow engine). The six-role model's Knowledge Engineer and Communication Engineer are adopted as operating-model roles, not proof that knowledge/communication contexts exist.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Where do different models, invariants, ownership and lifecycles actually emerge? ... this remains a DDD hypothesis, not an architectural fact. The current implementation would have to prove the boundaries.
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate (explicitly unproven) bounded-context landscape: Evidence Context (observations, sources, measurements, provenance), Reasoning Context (causal inference, assumptions, uncertainty), Decision Context (actions, recommendations, policies, consequences) under KnowledgeOS, flagged as a DDD hypothesis the implementation must still prove.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Core ... Does not own semantic interpretation or inference. ... Interpretation Context ... Its output is a candidate, never authoritative knowledge. ... Reasoning/Inference Context ... The context is deliberately replaceable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Eight recommended bounded contexts (Knowledge Core, Evidence, Assessment, Authority, Interpretation, Reasoning/Inference, Research/Evidence Design, Projection/Knowledge Product), each with a stated purpose and ownership list, notably Authority!=Truth and Interpretation producing only candidates never authoritative knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Yes: identity; admission; epistemic standing; state transitions; revision relationships; constitutional rules; conflict preservation; historical integrity; representation-independent references; deterministic admissibility checks. No: LLM inference; semantic parsing; embeddings; vector similarity; Bayesian calculation; regression; causal discovery; search; retrieval; ranking; experiment execution; UI; knowledge graph traversal; document rendering; workflow orchestration.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit Yes/No admission list for what belongs inside the Kernel: identity, admission, standing, transitions, revision relationships, constitutional rules, conflict preservation, historical integrity, representation-independent references and deterministic admissibility checks are IN; LLM inference, semantic parsing, embeddings, vector similarity, Bayesian calculation, regression, causal discovery, search, retrieval, ranking, experiment execution, UI, graph traversal, document rendering and workflow orchestration are OUT -- 'the Kernel protects the boundary; mechanisms perform cognition.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not build: 1. God Aggregate ... 2. Truth Oracle (Input -> Truth) ... 3. Bayesian Kernel ... 4. Semantic Kernel ... 5. Embedding Identity ... 6. AI Authority ... 7. Automatic Causal Discovery ... 8. Silent Revision ... 9. 'Confidence = Knowledge' ... 10. Full Epistemic OS Inside the Kernel.
b_rows_sample.statement: Ten explicit anti-patterns to avoid: God Aggregate, Truth Oracle, Bayesian Kernel, Semantic Kernel, Embedding Identity, AI Authority (LLM confidence cannot establish domain authority), Automatic Causal Discovery, Silent Revision, 'Confidence = Knowledge', and a Full Epistemic OS inside the Kernel -- the last explicitly noting formal epistemic machinery may still be valuable for AI reasoning *components* even though it should not become the organizational KnowledgeOS itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T1 - Distinction Preservation ... T15 - Deterministic Assurance. ... Preserve distinctions in the domain model; collapse representations only in mechanisms; collapse transactional boundaries only when an invariant requires atomicity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Fifteen-technique 'most optimized technique set' (Distinction Preservation, Evidence-First Reasoning, Assumption Ledger, Rival Hypothesis Analysis, Calibrated Uncertainty, Explicit Abstention, Residual Analysis, Search-Path Provenance, Value-of-Information Research, Designed Evidence, Append-Only Revision, Conflict Preservation, Representation-Independent Identity, Mechanism Independence, Deterministic Assurance), summarized by the sharpened final DDD principle: preserve distinctions in the domain model, collapse representations only in mechanisms, collapse transactional boundaries only when an invariant requires atomicity.

b_rows_sample.statement: Raises the DDD aggregate-boundary question ('what can change atomically?') and lists potential aggregates (Question, Observation, Assertion, Investigation, Conflict, Resolution, Decision) with references between them, explicitly rejecting a single giant KnowledgeOS aggregate; flags this as an architectural question still missing from the theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Does the UNDETERMINED BAND change the canonical K? If K's required components are identical for all 16 subsets ... then D-1 does NOT block construction of K -- it only affects the operation registry.
a_rows_sample.statement: Method: for the 14 forced operations (LOWER) and the 4-operation undetermined band {Transform, Merge, Split, Reintroduce}, enumerate the K-component (A, R, S, EL, Dt, PI, T, H) each operation NEEDS, compute the union of components required for every one of the 16 band subsets, and test whether that union ever differs from the 14-operation baseline; then, per component, test which operations (and how many are FORCED vs band-only) would break if that component were removed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: subsets of the undetermined band tested: 16 ... K-components IDENTICAL across all subsets? True ... band={Transform, Merge, Split, Reintroduce}       added components: NONE
a_rows_sample.statement: Executed result: across all 16 subsets of the undetermined operation band, the set of K-components required is identical (['A','Dt','EL','H','PI','R','S','T'], added components NONE in every case) to the 14-forced-operations baseline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: remove A   -> breaks 16 ops (12 of them FORCED)  => REQUIRED (forced ops break) ... remove H   -> breaks  1 ops (1 of them FORCED)  => REQUIRED (forced ops break)
a_rows_sample.statement: Per-component removal test: all eight components (A, Dt, EL, H, PI, R, S, T) are REQUIRED -- each breaks at least one FORCED (not merely band-only) operation if removed, ranging from A breaking 16 operations (12 forced) down to Dt and H each breaking exactly 1 forced operation (Add and Replay respectively).

a_rows_sample.anchor: EvidenceLinks required does NOT imply EvidenceLinks primitive. Likewise: Sigma required does not imply Sigma stored. It may be derived. This is one of the most important methodological safeguards of this step.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the semantic-necessity-vs-representation-necessity safeguard explicitly as one of Step 273's most important methodological rules -- later cited verbatim by the canonical-construction package (S1783) as the exact limit on its own derived K result.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Every component is load-bearing for at least one FORCED operation. Nothing is removable. ... K = (D_t, A, R, Sigma_c, E_L) with Pi and t carried inside each assertion; H external to K -- reachable only by Replay
a_rows_sample.statement: Executed removal test over the 14 forced operations: removing A breaks 16 ops (12 forced), S breaks 7 (6 forced), Pi breaks 6 (3 forced), R breaks 6 (3 forced), E_L breaks 5 (4 forced), T breaks 4 (2 forced), D_t breaks 1 (1 forced, Add), H breaks 1 (1 forced, Replay) -- every component load-bearing, none removable. Derived result: 𝒦=(K,H), K=(D_t, A, R, Sigma_c, E_L), with Pi (origin) and t (temporal) carried inside each assertion rather than as top-level K components, and H external, reachable only via Replay (a class-4 audit operation).

a_rows_sample.anchor: My removal test establishes SEMANTIC NECESSITY only. It shows each component must be expressible. It does not show it must be a stored top-level component. Sigma_c and E_L are exactly the two where this bites.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit self-limitation quoting Step 273 s273.31's semantic-vs-representation-necessity safeguard: the removal test shows each of the 8 components must be expressible (semantic necessity), not that each must be a stored top-level field (representation necessity); Sigma_c and E_L are flagged as exactly where this distinction matters, since Sigma is measured policy-relative (identical evidence yields Supported at min_support=2, Unknown at 3), creating an update-anomaly risk for a stored Sigma but an unrecoverable-commitment risk for a derived one -- explicitly deferred as D-4, not pre-empted here.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The terminal K = (A, R) is a representation claim presented as an ontology claim. That is why it could lose D_t without any test failing -- no test was quantified over the ontology.
a_rows_sample.statement: Diagnoses why the terminal model K=(A,R) could silently drop D_t (recognised dimensions) without any prior test detecting the loss: the terminal model conflated an ontology claim (what must be distinguishable) with a representation claim (how it is stored), and no prior test was ever quantified over the full ontology.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K = (A, R) | K = (D_t, A, R, Sigma_c, E_L), 𝒦=(K,H) | PROMOTION -- D_t is corpus (Zero lens); Sigma/E_L are corpus (Step 272/273) ... No INNOVATION was used.
a_rows_sample.statement: Characterises the change from the terminal K=(A,R) as: adding D_t and Sigma_c/E_L is a PROMOTION (already corpus-present, not invented), R's arity/field-count (n-ary 8-tuple vs the terminal 3-field triple) is an unresolved REPAIR blocked on D-5, and History being external is a confirmed REFINEMENT -- explicitly stating no innovation was used anywhere in the derivation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: non-collapse laws extracted (distinct) : 26 ... operations FORCED : 14 ... Two STRUCTURES are forced as a by-product, and neither is an operation: <D_t> ... <serialize>
a_rows_sample.statement: Derivation principle (o is mandatory iff removing it makes some corpus-stated non-collapse law inexpressible) applied to 26 distinct measured non-collapse laws: 14 operations forced (Authorize weight 45; Revise/Supersede 41; Promote 26; Qualify 20; Add 19; Determine 19; Derive 18; Replay 12; Assess/Validate 11; Remove/Withdraw/Reject weight 1 each), plus two non-operation structures forced as a by-product: <D_t> (recognised-dimension set, forced by UNKNOWN != ABSENT) and <serialize> (canonical form, forced by Expression != Meaning, the corpus's most-repeated law at 71 occurrences).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K-components IDENTICAL across all subsets? True ... D-1 IS K-INVARIANT. The open decision changes the operation REGISTRY. It does not change the knowledge STATE.
a_rows_sample.statement: Bandtest.py's executed result narrows D-1 from 'what is the operation universe' (foundational-sounding) to 'are these four specific operations mandatory or optional' (a bounded registry question), because K's required components are proven identical across all 16 possible resolutions of the undetermined band -- so K is constructible now, before D-1 is answered.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 𝒦 = (K, H) ... K = (D_t, 𝒜, ℛ, Σ_c, E_L) ... with H external, reachable only by Replay. DERIVED, not adopted. Four of its components' representations remain open (D-4, D-5) -- the ontology does not.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the smallest canonical model surviving all tests: 𝒦=(K,H), K=(D_t,A,R,Sigma_c,E_L), H external via Replay only, explicitly DERIVED not adopted, with the ontology settled but component REPRESENTATIONS (Sigma_c/E_L stored-vs-derived per D-4, R's arity per D-5) still open.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Semantically closed? NO ... Mathematically closed? NO ... Computationally closed? PARTIAL ... Empirically supported? PARTIAL ... Governance-closed? CLOSED at regime level, OPEN at act level ... These are five different numbers and must not be averaged.
a_rows_sample.statement: Five separately-stated closures paralleling (via so_exp06, cited directly) the second-order package's own five-closure result: semantic NO (5 G1 gaps; Context/Admissibility never typed; so_exp06 69%), mathematical NO (6 G2 gaps incl. an internal contradiction; ≡ unconstructed because ∀T∈T is indeterminate per s259.18), computational PARTIAL (closed above its oracles; Qualify/Authorize/delta-commit/Sigma.str have no bodies; 69%), empirical PARTIAL (14 experiments re-executed, all exit 0, but the strongest prior witness was a tautology; evidential 55%/implementation 52%), governance CLOSED at regime level / OPEN at act level (regress terminated twice, 132/132 humanActRef but free text/no identity, and GN-73's collision is live; 67%).

a_rows_sample.anchor: D-4 · Is Sigma stored or derived? ... Recommendation: DO NOT DECIDE -- let Step 273 finish. This is the one decision where the right act is to wait for work already in flight.
a_rows_sample.statement: D-4 (new): whether Sigma is stored (admits an update anomaly, demonstrated: identical evidence yields Supported at min_support=2, Unknown at 3) or derived (cannot carry an accepted commitment not recoverable from current evidence) -- explicitly recommends NOT deciding, since Step 273's own deletion/replacement tests (per s273.31) are the designated instrument and are still running.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D-5 · Is ℛ restored to the corpus 8-tuple? ... under the terminal model 'A1 contradicts A2' cannot be evidenced, dated, superseded or contested. ... v0.2 is AUTHORIZED and md5-pinned; ℛ is in its object inventory. Restoring it reopens a ratified artifact
a_rows_sample.statement: D-5 (new): whether the terminal 5-field relation triple ℛ⊆AxAxRelationType should be restored to the corpus's 8-tuple r=(E1,E2,T,R,Q,E,Sigma,tau); consequence constructed: under the terminal model a contradiction relation cannot be evidenced/dated/superseded/contested; blocked because v0.2 (which includes R in its object inventory) is authorized and md5-pinned, so restoration is a governance act, not a verification one, and the corpus's own Sigma-inside-r field is separately noted as ill-typed (policy-relative, no policy parameter) -- three options offered, (b) partial restoration (E, tau only) recommended but deferred to the human since it touches ratified architecture and depends on D-4.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = (A_t,R_t,E_t,Sigma_t,H_t,Z_t,L_t,T_t,G_t,C_t,M_t) ... with the conditional minimality result: K_minimal | O_core = (A,R,Sigma,E) ... Status: K: CLOSED
a_rows_sample.statement: Part 1 asserts (contradicting the more cautious canonical-construction package's own findings, S1783/S1784) that K is CLOSED with conditional minimality K_minimal|O_core=(A,R,Sigma,E), and that O_core is 'structurally closed' as a six-part union O_S∪O_E∪O_H∪O_G∪O_Q∪O_X, though O_G (governance operations) is 'not uniformly computationally demonstrated'.

a_rows_sample.statement: Part 2 downgrades Part 1's K_minimal=(A,R,Sigma,E) claim from CLOSED to a hypothesis pending the actual per-component deletion/replacement counterfactual experiment (remove x, check whether every mandatory distinction/operation is still representable) -- not yet completed at the time of writing.
