b_rows_sample.statement: Fifteen candidate concerns, each citing its supporting commission and what it waits on: K-1 dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model; K-2 the archetype set (strong: DOMAIN/PROCESS/CAPABILITY/KNOWLEDGE/ARTIFACT/RUNTIME ASSET/PROJECTION; weaker: CONTAINER; weakest: PURPOSE); K-3 the four partial orders (authority, production, realization, containment); K-4 11 invariant relationships vs 8 implementation choices; K-5 DP-n as capability anchor; K-6 Knowledge Space = declared boundary+owner+constitution; K-7 authority = provenance x standing, four progression kinds; K-8 the strategic domain set PD-1/2/3/5; K-9 viewpoints as presentation; K-10 decision-readiness as the platform's product; K-11 FREEZE/RETIRE as insufficiency evidence; K-12 PKS extends context-engineering with governance; K-13 the canon-track reference artifacts themselves; K-14 the mission is enacted via 8 artifacts; K-15 ownership splits (candidate-unowned=ladder working, operating-unowned=defect, sole instance Runtime Adapter).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 3. HYPOTHESIS — plausible, insufficient evidence (H-1..H-9)
b_rows_sample.statement: Nine hypotheses with evidence state: H-1 the space map is the platform's real ownership/context map (n=1, downgraded); H-2 GOVERNANCE as a fifth viewpoint (asset found, framing undecided); H-3 PURPOSE more fundamental than CONTAINER (n=0); H-4 KnowledgeOS as a 'Knowledge Architecture Platform' (n=1); H-5 'generates -> PKS', the loop's head edge and the platform's distinctive bet (n=0 inside and outside); H-6 capability may read across a space boundary, never own (n=1 capability); H-7 space nesting (unevidenced); H-8 DOMAIN's decision-silence is dormant not permanent (untestable at n=1); H-9 EVIDENCE-STATUS/OPERATIONAL-STATE as meta-model dimensions (proposed, undocketed).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ANNOTATED 2026-08-02 — THREE CORRECTIONS ... LEVEL MIXING — my third instance of that error class
b_rows_sample.statement: Three annotated corrections (recorded in KnowledgeOS_Relationship_Ontology.md): (1) section 2's six concepts are not siblings but four ontological layers (Purpose/Mission, Platform/Capability+Knowledge, Representation/Artifact, Application/PKS+Product) listed as one set — a third instance of level mixing; (2) PKS is a CONTAINER, not a layer below ARTIFACT — a PKS contains artifacts, and KNOWLEDGE SPACE is admitted as the container concept, defined by a declared boundary (scope.include), not a folder; (3) the document itself conflates two levels — section 1 (dimensions) is a meta-model, section 2 (concepts) is an ontology, both named rather than the whole renamed. The chain in section 2 is completed by naming DP-n (DESIGN POLICY) as the anchor stopping capabilities from floating, observable in the Capability Catalog's 1:1 CAP->DP binding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Concepts × kind × owner (C-1..C-13)
b_rows_sample.statement: Thirteen concepts classified by kind and owner: C-1 VISION (purpose, sponsor); C-2 MISSION (purpose, sponsor, enacted-unratified); C-3 ENGINEERING STRATEGY (purpose->governance bridge, ARB/sponsor); C-4 ENGINEERING PRINCIPLE (governance, DA/sponsor+ARB/platform depending on series); C-5 DESIGN POLICY DP-n (governance, DA via Catalog); C-6 ENGINEERING CAPABILITY (capability, its DP-n not a domain); C-7 ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE (knowledge, DA/sponsor+ARB); C-8 ENGINEERING ARTIFACT (representation, its owner field); C-9 KNOWLEDGE SPACE (container, the space's own owner); C-10 PKS (container, product team); C-11 PRODUCT (application, product team); C-12 RUNTIME ADAPTER (runtime element, no owner found); C-13 PROJECTION (projection, the generating space).

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-9 KNOWLEDGE SPACE — admitted, and the evidence is a boundary, not a folder ... A Knowledge Space is not a folder. It is a DECLARED SCOPE with an owner and a governing constitution
b_rows_sample.statement: KNOWLEDGE SPACE is admitted, evidenced by: knowledge-schema.yaml's declared scope.include; three registered documentation roots (knowledgeos, pks, publicdigit); ES-005.1's three concerns (Product, Platform, Runtime mount); the EKP having its own constitution and owner. A Knowledge Space is a declared scope with an owner and a governing constitution, not a folder — which is why the '13% coverage' question was a scope decision, not a bug.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The relationship model — the commission's seven questions ... contains = a container relation · references = a pointer · generates = produces a new instance · depends on = cannot be understood without
b_rows_sample.statement: A full relationship table across all thirteen concepts, using four typed relations (contains = container relation, references = a pointer, generates = produces a new instance, depends on = cannot be understood without). Notable entries: KNOWLEDGE SPACE may contain artifacts and other knowledge spaces, generates PROJECTIONS; PKS may contain product artifacts but never reusable Method, references Engineering Knowledge, generates Product Projections; ARTIFACT is a leaf (contains nothing) but depends on the Knowledge it represents; KNOWLEDGE generates nothing, being represented rather than generative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Missing concepts — recorded as hypotheses, not admitted (H-1..H-4)
b_rows_sample.statement: Four candidate concepts recorded as hypotheses, none admitted: H-1 'I-12', a Capability may read across a space boundary but never own what it reads (n=1 capability, needs a second cross-boundary reader); H-2 Engineering Domain as owner of Capabilities (no artifact binds a CAP to a PD; DP-n already fills the slot); H-3 Knowledge Space nesting, does the EKP contain the PKS or sit beside it (containment vs adjacency unevidenced); H-4 whether OPERATIONAL-STATE attaches to the Artifact or the Knowledge it carries (would change I-1's granularity).

b_rows_sample.anchor: RO-2 | Are Knowledge Spaces nested or adjacent?
b_rows_sample.statement: RO-2: are Knowledge Spaces nested or adjacent (H-3) — authority: ARB.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The three challenges — accepted, and one is settled by my own evidence rules ... CONTAINER demoted CONFIRMED → CANDIDATE ... my own admission rule decides it, not deference
b_rows_sample.statement: Three reviewer challenges: (1) 'Archetype' replaces 'nine kinds' until MM-1, since 'archetype' already exists in the corpus (RQ-002) so the rename mints nothing — a ubiquitous-language decision, decided with governance (MM-1), not unilaterally; (2) CONTAINER is demoted from CONFIRMED to CANDIDATE by the author's own admission rule: 'Containers generate Projections' is observed in exactly one space (the EKP's knowledge-graph.php), n=1, and nesting is unevidenced (H-3) — the settling test is a second generating space (confirms) or a capability-plus-scope reduction (refutes); (3) PURPOSE, possibly more fundamental than Container, is flagged not resolved, since the mission is enacted and unratified (D-5 pending), and deepening PURPOSE before ratification would model ahead of the domain expert — recorded as hypothesis U-ONT-2, n=0.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What exists instead ... FOUR DISTINCT PARTIAL ORDERS, one per relationship type: AUTHORITY · PRODUCTION · REALIZATION · CONTAINMENT
b_rows_sample.statement: Four evidenced partial orders replace the refuted single stack: AUTHORITY (who justifies whom) PURPOSE->STRATEGY->PRINCIPLE->DP-n->CAPABILITY; PRODUCTION (who produces whom) PROCESS->Knowledge/Artifacts/Evidence, CAPABILITY->Evidence, CONTAINER->Projection (n=1); REALIZATION (concept -> executable/persistent form) KNOWLEDGE->ARTIFACT (I-1), CAPABILITY->RUNTIME ASSET (R-7, SC-6 gap); CONTAINMENT (what moves together) CONTAINER contains Artifacts (contains other spaces? H-3 open). The intuition underneath the stack survives: relations are directional, with DOMAIN/KNOWLEDGE conceptual and RUNTIME/ARTIFACT realized; but 'which is above' is only answerable per relation, not for the stack as a whole.

a_aliases: Knowledge as a dynamic epistemic probability space

group_evidence.why_grouped: working_label token overlap Jaccard=0.50 (shared tokens: ['knowledge', 'space'])

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is the right next step because we now need to connect evidence aggregation with the question: When is acquiring another piece of evidence actually useful? This is the mathematical bridge between Evidence -> Zero -> Lord.
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 25C.3's purpose as the mathematical bridge Evidence→Zero→Lord: when is acquiring more evidence actually useful.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose KnowledgeOS currently has K_t and is considering an investigation action a ... The action may produce E_a. We need to calculate whether obtaining E_a is worthwhile. The first quantity is InformationGain(E_a|K_t) and eventually ValueOfInformation(a|K_t,G).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the two central quantities to be formalized: InformationGain(E_a|K_t) and ValueOfInformation(a|K_t,G) for an investigation action a.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose KnowledgeOS already knows E_1: NexusVersion=3.69. Now Lord proposes: Read the exact same inventory file again. The resulting evidence is E_2=E_1. The new information should be IG(E_2|E_1)=0. This is a very desirable property. It means KnowledgeOS can recognize: 'I am about to spend resources
a_rows_sample.statement: First experiment: duplicate-information retrieval must give IG(E2|E1)=0, letting KnowledgeOS recognize it is about to spend resources re-learning something already known.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For a hypothesis H, Shannon information is I(H)=-log P(H) ... IG(E;H)=Ent(H)-Ent(H|E) [renaming entropy Ent to avoid clash with hypothesis H].
a_rows_sample.statement: Adopts Shannon entropy-reduction as the formal InformationGain measure: IG(E;H)=Ent(H)-Ent(H|E), renaming entropy notation to avoid clashing with the hypothesis symbol H.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose P(H)=0.5. The uncertainty is Ent(H)=1 bit. Now an observation gives P(H|E)=0.9. The posterior entropy is lower. Therefore IG(E;H)>0. The observation has reduced uncertainty.
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked numerical example confirming IG(E;H)>0 when a posterior of 0.9 reduces entropy from the 1-bit prior.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose E_2=f(E_1). Then even though E_2 is technically another artifact: IG(E_2;H|E_1)=0 or approximately zero. Therefore the more useful quantity is IG(E_2;H|K_t). This asks: How much does this new evidence tell us that we do not already know?
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows a derived-copy artifact E2=f(E1) gives IG≈0 conditional on E1, motivating the conditional quantity IG(E2;H|K_t) as what KnowledgeOS actually needs (novel information relative to current knowledge, not raw artifact count).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose E_1 is one restore test. A second independently executed restore test E_2 can provide IG(E_2;H|E_1)>0. This is the mathematical explanation for why independent corroboration can be valuable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows independent corroborating evidence yields IG(E2;H|E1)>0 — the formal information-theoretic explanation for why independent corroboration is valuable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If E_2=f(E_1) then IG(E_2;H|E_1)≈0. This gives us a rigorous interpretation of the earlier qualitative rule: Don't count copied evidence twice. It isn't merely a governance convention. It has an information-theoretic interpretation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that the earlier 'don't count copied evidence twice' rule has a rigorous information-theoretic interpretation (IG≈0 for derived copies), not merely a governance convention.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The interesting case is 0 < IG(E_2;H|E_1) < IG(E_2;H). This means E_2 contains some new information, but part of its information was already contained in E_1. This is likely to be extremely common in KnowledgeOS. Vendor documentation -> Internal architecture document -> Human report -> LLM summary.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies partially-dependent evidence (0<IG(E2;H|E1)<IG(E2;H)) as the common case in practice, illustrated by a documentation-lineage chain (vendor doc→architecture doc→human report→LLM summary), none of which can be treated as fully independent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Define NovelInformation(E|K) as the information not already represented by the current knowledge state. Conceptually NovelInformation ≈ IG(E;Target|K). This should become one of the quantities available to Lord.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines NovelInformation(E|K) ≈ IG(E;Target|K) as a candidate quantity to be made available to Lord.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose Lord can run Action A: a five-second database query, expected information gain 0.1 bit. Action B: a two-week migration test, expected information gain 1.0 bit. Simply maximizing information would select B. That would be absurd. Therefore InformationGain != Value.
a_rows_sample.statement: Counterexample showing naive information-maximization would irrationally select a costly two-week test over a cheap query merely for higher bit-count, establishing InformationGain≠Value.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We need something like ValueOfInformation = ExpectedBenefitFromInformation - Cost. But there is another important term: Risk. Therefore a preliminary formulation is VOI(a) = ExpectedDecisionValueAfter(a) - CurrentDecisionValue - Cost(a) - Risk(a).
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a preliminary Value-of-Information equation VOI(a)=ExpectedDecisionValueAfter(a)-CurrentDecisionValue-Cost(a)-Risk(a).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Current best decision a* = argmax_{a in A} EU(a|K_t). Now consider information-gathering action q. After receiving evidence E_q: a*(E_q) = argmax_a EU(a|K_t,E_q). Then VOI(q) = E_{E_q}[max_a EU(a|K_t,E_q)] - max_a EU(a|K_t) - Cost(q). This is a much more rigorous definition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the rigorous decision-theoretic Value-of-Information formula VOI(q)=E_{E_q}[max_a EU(a|K_t,E_q)]-max_a EU(a|K_t)-Cost(q), the standard expected-utility VOI definition applied to Lord's action selection.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lord can now distinguish: Question A: Can I learn something? from Question B: Is learning it worth doing? The first is information theory. The second is decision theory. Thus Lord = InformationAcquisition + DecisionValue.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes 'can I learn something' (information theory) from 'is learning it worth doing' (decision theory), decomposing Lord = InformationAcquisition + DecisionValue.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose our goal is G: Determine whether Nexus rollback is safe. Lord considers: Search the company's office seating plan. It may contain enormous information. But IG(E;G)≈0. Therefore VOI≈0. Lord should reject the action. InformationQuantity != GoalRelevantInformation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsification test: irrelevant-but-information-rich evidence (office seating plan) has IG(E;G)≈0 against the actual goal, so VOI≈0 and Lord correctly rejects it — InformationQuantity≠GoalRelevantInformation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Now consider: Execute a restore test against the actual backup. Expected information gain about H: RollbackSafe=True is potentially very high. Therefore IG(E;H|K_t) >> 0. And if the result can change the migration decision: VOI(q) >> 0. This is exactly the type of action Lord should prioritize.
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsification test: a directly goal-relevant restore test yields IG>>0 and VOI(q)>>0, correctly prioritized by Lord.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose the migration has already been formally prohibited by governance. Even if we could learn whether Rollback=True the answer cannot change the current authorized decision. Then VOI(q)≈0. ... The same evidence can have HighInformationValue in one context and ZeroDecisionValue in another. Therefo
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsification test: information that cannot alter an already-governance-prohibited decision has VOI≈0 regardless of its Shannon information content, establishing VOI is goal- and decision-context dependent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose migration must happen tomorrow. A test requiring three weeks has potentially useful information. But operationally VOI_effective≈0 if the result arrives after the decision deadline. Therefore time is part of the value calculation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsification test: information arriving after the decision deadline has VOI_effective≈0, establishing time-to-delivery as part of the value calculation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose a test could reveal valuable information but requires risking production availability. Then InformationGain>0 but Risk>>0. Therefore Lord should potentially reject it. This gives SafeInformationAcquisition as a governance constraint.
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsification test: high-information but high-risk acquisition should potentially be rejected, giving SafeInformationAcquisition as a governance constraint on Lord.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose Lord can ask an infrastructure expert: Is port 8081 reachable from the target network? The answer could be highly informative. But HumanAnswer is itself evidence. Therefore Question -> HumanResponse -> Evidence -> Assessment. The human answer must not bypass the evidence model.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that a human answer to an information-gathering question is itself Evidence and must flow through Question→HumanResponse→Evidence→Assessment, never bypassing the evidence model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The fundamental distinction ... Evidence Strength \neq Information Gain \neq Decision Value ... How strongly does an evidence item support a proposition? ... How much does the evidence reduce uncertainty? ... How much does acquiring the evidence improve the decision?
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates three related-but-distinct quantities: Evidence Strength (support magnitude), Information Gain (uncertainty reduction), and Decision Value (improvement to the decision from acquiring the evidence).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can Nexus be migrated safely? ... Version = 3.69 ... Knowing the exact patch version may add little information. ... Is the production blob store backed up? ... may currently be completely unknown. A single answer could dramatically reduce the migration uncertainty. Highest Evidence Strength \neq Hi
b_rows_sample.statement: Illustrates with a migration-safety question that a strongly-evidenced fact (Nexus version) can add little new information, while an unknown backup-status question could dramatically reduce uncertainty with a single answer — Highest Evidence Strength ≠ Highest Information Gain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Information gain in information theory ... H(P) = -\sum_x P(x)\log P(x) ... P(P)=0.5 then H(P)=1 bit ... P(P\mid e)=0.95 and H(P\mid e)<H(P) ... IG(e;P) = H(P)-H(P\mid e). This is a mathematically rigorous definition of information gain.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines entropy-based information gain IG(e;P)=H(P)-H(P|e) using Shannon entropy H(P)=-Σ P(x)log P(x), worked with a 0.5→0.95 probability update as a rigorous but calculus-specific definition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: But this is not universal ... Entropy requires a probabilistic representation. ... unknown values; logical constraints; competing assertions; qualitative uncertainty; argument graphs; incomplete evidence. Therefore we should not define IG=EntropyReduction as a universal KnowledgeOS law. InformationG
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the previous entropy definition's universality: entropy requires a probabilistic representation, which KnowledgeOS often lacks (unknown values, logical constraints, argument graphs), so IG=EntropyReduction must not be a universal law — InformationGain_ρ is policy-specific.

b_rows_sample.anchor: General definition ... discrepancy function D(S,I,P) ... IG_D(e) = D(S_t,I_t,P) - D(S_{t+1}^{(e)},I_t,P) ... Information gain can be measured as reduction in discrepancy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes information gain beyond entropy: IG_D(e)=D(S_t,I_t,P)-D(S_{t+1}^(e),I_t,P), i.e. information gain measured as reduction in a discrepancy function relative to the Ideal State.

b_rows_sample.anchor: But there is an important complication ... We usually don't know in advance what evidence e will reveal. ... Yes; No; Unknown; "Backups exist but have never been tested." Therefore we need expected information gain. ... EIG(e) = \sum_{o\in O_e} Pr(o\mid e,K_t)[D(K_t,I_t,P)-D(K_{t+1}^{o},I_t,P)]
b_rows_sample.statement: Notes evidence outcomes are unknown in advance (e.g. a yes/no/unknown/qualified backup-status answer), requiring Expected Information Gain EIG(e)=Σ_o Pr(o|e,K_t)[D(K_t,I_t,P)-D(K_{t+1}^o,I_t,P)] over possible outcomes o.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Expected discrepancy reduction ... EDR(e) = \mathbb E[D(K_t,I_t,P)-D(K_{t+1},I_t,P)\mid e] ... This does not require us to call it information theory. It can be used with deterministic gap counts; probabilistic uncertainty; belief functions; argumentation; domain-specific discrepancy measures.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Expected Discrepancy Reduction EDR(e)=E[D(K_t,I_t,P)-D(K_{t+1},I_t,P)|e], deliberately framework-neutral so it can be instantiated with deterministic gap counts, probability, belief functions, argumentation, or other domain-specific discrepancy measures.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is probably more fundamental for KnowledgeOS ... ExpectedDiscrepancyReduction more fundamental than EntropyReduction ... KnowledgeOS is not merely trying to reduce uncertainty. It is trying to move K_t toward I_t. Therefore the natural objective is K_t\rightarrow I_t and not merely H(K_t)\right
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues ExpectedDiscrepancyReduction is more fundamental to KnowledgeOS than EntropyReduction, since KnowledgeOS's real objective is moving K_t toward I_t, not merely driving entropy to zero.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A critical counterexample ... P(A)=0.5 and P(B)=0.5 ... A is irrelevant to the current decision. Then IG(A)>0 but EDR(A)\approx0. Meanwhile evidence about B might directly resolve a Critical Gap. InformationGain\neq PurposeValue. This is why purpose P must remain in the equation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a counterexample where entropy-reducing evidence about an irrelevant proposition A has high IG but near-zero EDR, while evidence about a decision-relevant proposition B would resolve a critical gap — InformationGain ≠ PurposeValue, so purpose must remain in the equation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Value of Evidence ... VOE_\rho(e\mid K_t,I_t,P,C) ... the expected value of acquiring evidence e ... VOE(e) = ExpectedDiscrepancyReduction(e) \times DecisionImpact(e) ... this multiplication is not a universal law. It is one possible policy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Value of Evidence VOE_ρ(e|K_t,I_t,P,C) as the expected value of acquiring e, offering EDR(e)×DecisionImpact(e) as one possible (non-universal) policy decomposition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Cost must also be included ... Evidence A ... 0.9 ... €10,000 ... Evidence B ... 0.7 ... €10 ... Clearly, "maximum information gain" alone is insufficient. We need Cost(e) and potentially Time(e), Risk(e), Effort(e)
b_rows_sample.statement: Shows via a cost/benefit contrast (Evidence A: EDR 0.9 at €10,000 vs Evidence B: EDR 0.7 at €10) that maximizing information gain alone is insufficient — Cost, Time, Risk, and Effort must also enter the evaluation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Utility of evidence ... U_\rho(e) = Benefit_\rho(e) - Cost_\rho(e) ... U(e) = \alpha EDR(e) + \beta DecisionImpact(e) - \gamma Cost(e) - \delta Time(e) ... the coefficients \alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta are policy parameters. They are not mathematical truths.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines evidence utility U_ρ(e)=Benefit_ρ(e)-Cost_ρ(e), with a worked linear form U(e)=αEDR(e)+βDecisionImpact(e)-γCost(e)-δTime(e) whose coefficients are explicitly labeled policy parameters, not mathematical truths.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The evidence acquisition problem ... \mathcal Q ... Q1 = inspect filesystem ... Q8 = ask LLM to extract information ... q^* = \arg\max_{q\in\mathcal Q} U_\rho(q\mid K_t,I_t,P) ... This is potentially one of the most important equations in the whole KnowledgeOS theory.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Lord's core problem as q*=argmax_{q∈Q} U_ρ(q|K_t,I_t,P) over a candidate acquisition-action set Q (inspect filesystem, query API, read document, ask engineer, inspect backup config, run test, search internet, ask LLM) — called potentially one of the most important equations in the whole theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Lord's role becomes precise ... Lord(K_t,I_t,P,\rho) \rightarrow RankedCandidateAcquisitions ... Candidate 1 Inspect production backup configuration Expected discrepancy reduction: High Cost: Low Risk: Low
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Lord as Lord(K_t,I_t,P,ρ)→RankedCandidateAcquisitions, illustrated with a ranked candidate list (inspect backup config / ask infra owner / search internet) each carrying EDR/Cost/Risk estimates.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sarathi then chooses or guides ... Lord generates the candidate space. Sārathi considers current constraints; available capabilities; urgency; policy; safety; dependencies; human authority. Sārathi : Candidates \rightarrow NextAction ... Lord = option generation/ranking ... Sārathi = action guidance
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Lord (option generation/ranking) from Sārathi (Candidates→NextAction, factoring in constraints/urgency/policy/safety/dependencies/human authority) as separate roles.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero has a different role ... Zero(K_t,I_t) \rightarrow \Delta_t ... Lord(\Delta_t) \rightarrow Q ... Sārathi(Q,constraints) \rightarrow a_t ... This gives us a very elegant cycle: Knowledge K_t → Zero → Δ_t → Lord → candidates → Sārathi → action → Evidence Acquisition → New Knowledge K_t+1 → Zero
b_rows_sample.statement: Assembles the full Zero→Lord→Sārathi cycle: Zero(K_t,I_t)→Δ_t, Lord(Δ_t)→Q (candidates), Sārathi(Q,constraints)→a_t (action), producing new evidence and K_{t+1}, feeding back into Zero.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is much more than RAG ... Question \rightarrow Retrieve \rightarrow Generate ... Purpose \rightarrow IdealState \rightarrow Discrepancy \rightarrow EvidenceValue \rightarrow AcquisitionPlan \rightarrow Evidence \rightarrow Assessment \rightarrow KnowledgeState. That is a fundamentally different
b_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts traditional RAG's Question→Retrieve→Generate pipeline with KnowledgeOS's Purpose→IdealState→Discrepancy→EvidenceValue→AcquisitionPlan→Evidence→Assessment→KnowledgeState pipeline as a fundamentally different architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Human research fits naturally ... q=HumanInquiry ... HumanResponse\rightarrow Evidence ... Acquisition=Reported ... Source=Human ... The human's statement does not automatically become truth. It enters exactly the same evidence machinery.
b_rows_sample.statement: Shows human inquiry fits the same acquisition/evidence machinery (q=HumanInquiry → HumanResponse→Evidence with Acquisition=Reported, Source=Human), with the human's statement not automatically becoming truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LLM output also fits ... LLM(D)\rightarrow e ... Acquisition=Inferred ... Parent=D ... LLMOutput\neq GroundTruth ... LLMOutput\neq IndependentEvidence when it derives from existing evidence. This is one of the major architectural strengths of the model.
b_rows_sample.statement: Shows LLM output fits the same graph (LLM(D)→e with Acquisition=Inferred, Parent=D), reaffirming LLMOutput ≠ GroundTruth and LLMOutput ≠ IndependentEvidence when derived from existing evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experimental evidence ... Hypothesis: Nexus backup can be restored. Experiment: Restore backup to isolated environment. Observation: Restore succeeded. Evidence: e_exp ... Acquisition(e)=Observed with provenance Experiment\rightarrow Observation. This can have much higher relevance to a migration de
b_rows_sample.statement: Models experimental evidence (Hypothesis/Experiment/Observation/Evidence, e.g. restoring a backup to an isolated environment) with Acquisition=Observed and provenance Experiment→Observation, noted as potentially higher relevance than a textual claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Logical omniscience: The system believes all logical consequences ... computationally intractable and cognitively unrealistic. ... four-valued situations: True only, False only, Both, Neither. ... Beliefs are not closed under implication. ... {Bp,B(p\supset q),
eg Bq} ... {Bp,B
eg p,
eg Bq} inconsistent beliefs without omniscience
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the B (explicit belief) operator using four-valued situations (true-only/false-only/both/neither) to avoid logical omniscience -- beliefs are not closed under implication or consequence, exemplified by satisfiable sets {Bp,B(p⊃q),¬Bq} and inconsistent-without-explosion {Bp,B¬p,¬Bq}; a first-order variant interprets existential quantification constructively, making existential generalization fail (not |= B(P(a)∨P(b))⊃B∃xP(x)); complexity results range from co-NP-complete (propositional) to undecidable (first-order with existential generalization).

type_signature.domain: formula phi, epistemic state e, situation s

a_rows_sample.anchor: EOC = Explicit Only-knowing with Complete introspection ... Mark terms that appear within modal operators with triangle. Teach(father(tom),sara)\land\neg B Teach(father(tom)^\triangle,sara) ... Decidability: first-order with unrestricted equality Undecidable.
a_rows_sample.statement: EOC logic extends B with nested beliefs, only-knowing, and equality, introducing a triangle-marking device to solve quantifying-in with explicit belief (marking terms evaluated at substitution time versus modal-operator time); catalogues decidability results ranging from O(nm) propositional to undecidable first-order-with-unrestricted-equality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation: Integrate the book's findings into KnowledgeOS Theory v1.2, particularly: 1. The TELL/ASK framework -> Core operations 2. The Representation Theorem -> Sat semantics 3. Only-knowing -> Zero definition 4. Explicit belief (B) -> Tractable reasoning 5. Successor state axioms -> delta semantics 6. The triangle operator -> Quantifying-in with explicit belief
a_rows_sample.statement: Final unhedged recommendation to integrate six findings directly into Theory v1.2 (TELL/ASK->core operations, Representation Theorem->Sat semantics, Only-knowing->Zero definition, Explicit belief B->tractable reasoning, successor-state axioms->delta semantics, triangle operator->quantifying-in), without the [PROP]/[OPEN] hedging used by the more disciplined reviews elsewhere in this batch (e.g. S2520-S2524, S2526-S2528).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contr: Four-valued semantics handles contradiction without collapse. We should mark this SUPPORTING EVIDENCE ONLY. ... our own KR-CONTR-FDE experiments already showed FDE is insufficient by itself. ... Four-valued belief \neq Contr and B/N \neq Zero remain intact.
a_rows_sample.statement: Directly contradicts S2532's claim that four-valued semantics 'handles contradiction without collapse' for Contr, citing the project's own prior KR-CONTR-FDE experiment result that FDE's four values cannot distinguish all required boundary reasons (whereas Standing x Boundary x Context x Provenance did); concludes Four-valued belief != Contr and B/N != Zero remain intact -- the book independently strengthens motivation for non-classical/bounded belief representation but does not resolve Contr semantics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Part 3: What Must Be Corrected ... ASK -> Sat(K_t,r) Reject ... TELL -> Adding requirements to R_t Reject ... Only-Knowing = Zero Reject ... Four-valued semantics solves Contr Reject ... Successor-state axioms define delta Reject ... Levesque & Lakemeyer = KnowledgeOS theory Reject
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the six overclaim-rejections scattered across S2534 into one authoritative correction table: ASK!=Sat(K_t,r), TELL!=requirements-addition, Only-Knowing!=Zero, four-valued-semantics-does-not-solve-Contr, successor-state-axioms-do-not-define-delta, Levesque&Lakemeyer!=KnowledgeOS-theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: TELL(KB, alpha) -> KB' ; ASK(KB, alpha) -> {YES, NO, UNKNOWN}
b_rows_sample.statement: TELL/ASK proposed as a candidate KnowledgeOS operation family O_knowledge ⊇ {TELL, ASK}: TELL(K,alpha)->K' for knowledge acquisition, ASK(K,r,Gamma)->Eval_c for knowledge inquiry, explicitly replacing the source's {YES,NO,UNKNOWN} return type with the richer structured Eval_c because contradiction research already showed the three-valued return is insufficient. Status: very strong candidate for Theory v1.3, no kernel promotion yet.

type_signature.domain: K x alpha (TELL); K x r x Gamma (ASK)

b_rows_sample.anchor: Table: what I would actually add to KnowledgeOS Theory v1.3 (T1-T5) vs What I would NOT adopt
b_rows_sample.statement: Recorded editorial recommendation: five candidate theoretical commitments (T1 explicit/implicit knowledge, T2 reasoning is semantics-dependent Cn_S(K), T3 evaluation may consume implicit knowledge Eval_c(Cn_S(K),r,Gamma), T4 state transition needs persistence semantics Succ_S, T5 explanation is not determination) proposed for Theory v1.3 as strong candidates, none yet kernel-promoted; explicitly rejects Sat=FOL-entailment, Zero=CWA, Zero=Delta=empty universally, Boundary=frame axioms, delta=situation calculus, Identity=unique-names+domain-closure, DL=Boundary-taxonomy, mandatory default reasoning, FOL-as-representation-language, and YES/NO/UNKNOWN-sufficiency.

b_rows_sample.anchor: TELL does not mean TELL \Rightarrow Truth ... ASK=TRUE does not automatically mean Truth
b_rows_sample.statement: TELL(K,alpha)->K' and ASK(K,r,Gamma)->Eval_c are candidate fundamental operations, grounded in the classical KR&R TELL/ASK pattern (systems that can be told facts and adjust behaviour); explicit KnowledgeOS restriction: TELL does not imply Truth (only that content entered the governed representation per applicable authority/admission rules), and ASK=TRUE does not automatically mean Truth (only that the applicable evaluation semantics returned that result).

type_signature.domain: K x alpha (TELL); K x r x Gamma (ASK)

b_rows_sample.anchor: TELL(K, alpha) -> K' — Add knowledge to the KB ; ASK(K, alpha) -> Answer — Query the KB ... TELL — Adding requirements or observations ; ASK — Determining Sat(K_t, r)
b_rows_sample.statement: TELL/ASK interface restated from the DL handbook and mapped: TELL for adding requirements or observations, ASK for determining Sat(K_t,r) — a less hedged version of the TELL/ASK candidate than the one in S2520/S2521 (no restriction noted here that TELL does not imply Truth).

b_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge base represents what is explicitly believed; what is implicitly believed is what follows from it. ... Tell(KB,\alpha)\rightarrow KB' ... Ask(KB,\alpha)\rightarrow \{Yes,No,Unknown\} ... Only-Knowing — A formal logic for "all I know" — exactly what you need for Zero
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends Levesque & Lakemeyer's Logic of Knowledge Bases as second priority, proposing its TELL/ASK interface (with the unhedged three-valued ASK return type later replaced by Eval_c in S2520/S2521) and its 'Only-Knowing' formal logic for 'all I know' as directly relevant to the open Zero TODO and the Closed-World-Assumption question.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ASK[alpha,e] = YES if e|=Kalpha; NO otherwise ... TELL[alpha,e]=e \cap \{w\mid e,w\models\alpha\} ... e,w\models K\alpha \iff for every w'\in e, e,w'\models\alpha
b_rows_sample.statement: Formal semantics for ASK[alpha,e] (YES iff e|=K-alpha, else NO) and TELL[alpha,e] (intersect e with the worlds satisfying alpha), and the K operator (K-alpha true at w iff alpha holds in every world w' in the epistemic state e) -- the precise formal machinery underlying the TELL/ASK candidate used loosely elsewhere in this batch.

b_rows_sample.anchor: (\alpha\supset K\alpha) FALSE ... (K\alpha\supset\alpha) FALSE ... If \models\alpha then \models K\alpha TRUE ... For any subjective sentence sigma: \models(\sigma\supset K\sigma) [positive introspection] ... logical omniscience
b_rows_sample.statement: Catalogues formal properties of K: truth does not imply knownness and knowledge need not be accurate (K models belief, not factive knowledge, in this framework) while valid sentences are always known; complete positive introspection holds for subjective sentences; and the K operator suffers logical omniscience (knows all logical consequences of what it knows) -- a limitation later addressed by the B operator.

b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects S2532's closing claim that Levesque & Lakemeyer provides 'the definitive formal foundation for KnowledgeOS's core architecture' as too strong: reclassifies the book as formal KR/epistemic-reasoning EVIDENCE, since KnowledgeOS additionally includes attribution, evidence, provenance, determination, governance, authority, assurance, temporal state, decisions, action, verification and lifecycle not covered by the book.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NEXT-ACTOR-ORCHESTRATION-001 / AST-018 (SEPARATE, EXISTING, UNCHANGED) ... KOS-OPERATING-MODEL-001 (NEW — this recording) ... The new slice CONSUMES AST-018 as the existing canonical mechanism for next-actor orchestration. It does not modify, re-implement, re-open, or await the adoption of AST-018.
a_rows_sample.statement: PO/ARB's Option-B decision explicitly creates a separate governed slice (the operating model) that consumes, rather than modifies or waits on, the existing AST-018 slice; AST-018's own STOP→verification→adoption path continues unaffected in parallel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Responsibilities, not services/positions ... Neither name enters the declared workflow role vocabulary consumed by AST-015/AST-017/AST-018 ... without an explicit governed decision
a_rows_sample.statement: Five recorded review constraints bind the coming implementation: Governance Engineer/Communication Engineer must remain operating responsibilities (never platform services or organizational positions, per the adopted six-role non-equivalence); neither name may silently enter the workflow role vocabulary; REVIEW_INDEPENDENCE_POLICY stays a placeholder; layer scope needs explicit PO/ARB confirmation; and the AST-018 slice's own obligations are not displaced by the new work item.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Governance Engineer is the dedicated human-facing governance role ... The Communication Engineer is NOT a permanent person. It is a TRANSFERABLE OPERATIONAL RESPONSIBILITY. Any currently authorized actor/session may perform the Communication Engineer responsibility for routine coordination.
a_rows_sample.statement: The operating model defines two human-facing responsibilities: a dedicated Governance Engineer (business/authority/exception handling, adoption presentation) and a transferable Communication Engineer (routine session-lifecycle coordination performable by any currently authorized actor), with the rule BUSINESS/AUTHORITY/EXCEPTION→Governance, ROUTINE/OPERATIONAL/SESSION-COORDINATION→Communication, HUMAN AUTHORITY→Human/PO-ARB.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This produces exactly one business-level outcome: CONTINUE, PERMISSION_REQUIRED, FRESH_SESSION_REQUIRED, GOVERNANCE_DECISION_REQUIRED, STOP. ... Do NOT create a second workflow-state vocabulary.
a_rows_sample.statement: Every working session's local governance/communication capability at completion must classify its situation into exactly one of five business-level outcomes (CONTINUE / PERMISSION_REQUIRED / FRESH_SESSION_REQUIRED / GOVERNANCE_DECISION_REQUIRED / STOP), explicitly forbidden from becoming a second, competing workflow-state vocabulary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A process identity is: DISCOVERED FROM THE RUNTIME. It is not: invented by the human; copied from another session; inferred from prompt text; chosen from a human-entered UUID. ... Therefore: role ≠ process identity; identity ≠ eligibility; eligibility ≠ appointment; appointment ≠ activation; activation ≠ authorization.
a_rows_sample.statement: The Process Identity Rule: the human always chooses business intent/role, and the runtime always supplies concrete process identity — never the reverse — yielding a five-term non-equivalence chain (role≠identity≠eligibility≠appointment≠activation≠authorization) that must never collapse.

a_rows_sample.anchor: MATCH ... 'This is the assigned session. You may continue.' ... MISMATCH ... 'This is not the session assigned to this work.' Then: 1. Open the assigned session 2. Prepare the exact prompt for the assigned session 3. Stop.
a_rows_sample.statement: When an actor is already appointed, a fresh session's runtime identity is compared against the expected actor to produce exactly ACTOR_MATCH or ACTOR_MISMATCH; on mismatch the system must never create a second appointment, replace or impersonate the appointed actor, self-register, or treat the mismatch itself as authorization — it only offers a business-language recovery path.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not hard-code in this implementation whether every review must be: same session, subagent, independent OS session. Treat review independence as a separate policy. The implementation must support the concept: REVIEW_INDEPENDENCE_POLICY but must not invent final policy rules.
a_rows_sample.statement: The degree of review independence required (same session / subagent / independent OS session) is deliberately left as an unresolved, named policy placeholder (REVIEW_INDEPENDENCE_POLICY) rather than hard-coded, so the implementation supports the concept without inventing the final rule.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not treat verification as adoption. Do not treat review PASS as adoption.
a_rows_sample.statement: Final adoption requires an explicit human decision (Accept/Adopt, Return, or Stop) presented by the Governance Engineer after review PASS; review passing and independent verification are each explicitly insufficient on their own to constitute adoption.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The human must never need to: provide a session UUID; choose runtime process identity; determine mutationOwner; determine predecessor; construct REGISTER; construct HANDOFF; construct START; edit workflow JSON; invoke workflow-state.php; inspect workflow records to route the work; diagnose INV-B; diagnose G-3; understand token/tokenRef; manually calculate authorization.
a_rows_sample.statement: A fourteen-item hard acceptance criterion enumerates everything the human must never be required to do; if the human is forced to perform any of these in a normal workflow, the implementation is declared to have failed the human-facing contract.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Explicitly distinguish: IMPLEMENTED from: ADOPTED and: AUTHORIZED for future use. Do not collapse them.
a_rows_sample.statement: Every completion report produced under this operating model must keep IMPLEMENTED, VERIFIED, ADOPTED and AUTHORIZED as four distinct, never-collapsed states — a rule enforced verbatim through every subsequent artifact in the batch (implementation, AMENDMENT-001, and their completion reports).

a_rows_sample.anchor: the capability layer is minimal. The operating model is the primary deliverable; it consumes the existing AST-018 commands and does not re-implement, enlarge, or re-open them. Any new software produced under this commission is minimal support for the operating model — never a second workflow engine
a_rows_sample.statement: PO/ARB authorizes all three delivery layers (operating model document, minimal supporting capability, verification/acceptance) but clarifies 'minimal supporting capability' to mean the new software must consume AST-018's existing commands rather than re-implement or enlarge them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: test_om_37 proves all four canonical assets byte-unchanged vs HEAD. PO/ARB's two corrected semantics pinned in tests: FRESH_SESSION_REQUIRED = paste-prompt-not-appointment (+ no UUID asked); session candidate status never inferred from UNRESOLVED + NEXT_ACTOR_REQUIRED.
a_rows_sample.statement: The completed implementation records two specific PO/ARB-corrected semantic pins in its test suite: FRESH_SESSION_REQUIRED means presenting a paste-ready prompt, not an appointment act, and never asking for a UUID; and a session's candidate status must never be silently inferred merely from an UNRESOLVED bootstrap plus a NEXT_ACTOR_REQUIRED result.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The work item is STOPPED (seq 4) — an explicit CONTINUATION (recordedBy governance/human) must precede any REGISTER(verification); this prompt creates no activation.
a_rows_sample.statement: The candidate-declaration prompt for a fresh verifier explicitly states that STOPPED is sticky and that an explicit, human-recorded CONTINUATION must occur before any REGISTER(verification) can be written, listing nine barred prior participants including the implementing session itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The producer's completion report §38 was itself a verification object — its four-state separation (IMPLEMENTED ≠ VERIFIED ≠ ADOPTED ≠ AUTHORIZED) had to be accurate in content, not just in label.
a_rows_sample.statement: Independent verification treats a completion report's own claimed status-separation as itself a falsifiable object, not merely a label to trust — confirming the producer's IMPLEMENTED/NOT-VERIFIED/NOT-ADOPTED/NOT-AUTHORIZED claims held true in substance, not only in wording.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If the verifier also performed the adoption review, VERIFIED and ADOPTED-review would collapse into one actor — the exact collapse the operating model forbids.
a_rows_sample.statement: The verifier itself refuses to perform the Governance adoption review, extending the producer-bar/separation-of-duties chain a further step: a verifier acting as its own adoption reviewer would collapse two of the operating model's four distinct states (VERIFIED, ADOPTED) into a single actor's judgement, which §38 explicitly forbids.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Human ↔ Governance ↔ KnowledgeOS ↔ Agent ↔ Engineering ↔ Runtime
b_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 125 (KnowledgeOS Operating Model), stating the principal-actor chain Human<->Governance<->KnowledgeOS<->Agent<->Engineering<->Runtime and posing the question 'who does what, who is allowed to decide what, and where does evidence flow?' across Domain Architect, Architecture Board, engineers, deterministic assurance, KnowledgeOS, Claude, Codex, and runtime systems.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Business/Product Authority, Domain Architect, Architecture Board/Governance, Engineering Team, Deterministic Assurance, AI Agent, Runtime/Operational Systems
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies seven principal actor classes and states KnowledgeOS itself is not an organizational actor but 'the system of record and coordination substrate through which these actors exchange governed knowledge and evidence.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: BusinessIntent ... Why are we doing this?
b_rows_sample.statement: Assigns responsibilities per actor: Business/Product Authority establishes BusinessIntent (objectives, regulatory/customer requirements, strategic priorities, risk acceptance) answering 'why,' without determining technical architecture; Domain Architect translates business/technical concerns into architectural reasoning (analysis, bounded-context decisions, principles, alternatives, impact analysis, recommendations, governance prep) under ArchitecturalRecommendation ≠ GovernanceDecision; Architecture Board consumes Evidence+Recommendation+Impact+Alternatives to produce Analysis->BoardDecision rather than performing every technical analysis itself; Engineering transforms authorized intent into implementation (Decision->Implementation) owning code/config/deployment/tests/technical remediation/operational changes within delegation; Deterministic Assurance answers machine-testable conformance questions (Assurance->Evidence, not Assurance->OrganizationalAuthority); AI Agent participates in retrieval/analysis/reasoning/inspection/tool execution/checks/recommendations/delegated execution but Agent ≠ GovernanceAuthority; Runtime/Operations is the source of observed reality answering 'what is actually happening'; KnowledgeOS holds Knowledge+Evidence+Provenance+Authority+TemporalValidity+Traceability+Feedback as the semantic continuity layer between decisions and reality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Responsible ... Authorized.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Responsible from Authorized (an engineer can be responsible for implementing a decision without authority to change it; an architect can recommend without authority to approve; an agent can execute a delegated action without authority to redefine policy), and argues a conventional RACI matrix is insufficient — KnowledgeOS needs Actor+Capability+Authority+Scope+EvidenceResponsibility.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Authority = Actor × Action × Resource × Scope × Validity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Authority = Actor x Action x Resource x Scope x Validity (e.g. Engineering Team/deploy/Service X/Staging/current may be authorized while the same tuple in production may require different authority); for agents, AgentAuthority = DelegatedAuthority ∩ Policy, so an agent cannot inherit all authority of the human whose credentials it uses — e.g. being authorized to 'run tests and create a PR' gives AgentCapability={read,test,createPR} which does not imply merge or deployProduction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | Actor | Primary responsibility | Can recommend? | Can decide? | Can execute? | Produces evidence? |
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents a first-approximation operating-model matrix (Business Authority, Domain Architect, Architecture Board, Engineering, Assurance, AI Agent, Runtime rows) recording each actor's recommend/decide/execute/evidence capacities, explicitly labeled a working model, not yet a finalized organizational RACI.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Business Intent → Architecture → Governance Decision → Engineering → Runtime → Observation → Evidence → KnowledgeOS → Governance
b_rows_sample.statement: Diagrams the evidence-flow loop, and separately the decision-flow Question->Analysis->Recommendation->Decision->Authorization->Action (agent participates heavily in the first three, authority governs the fourth/fifth, engineering executes the sixth); warns evidence flow and decision flow must not be confused — Evidence->Recommendation is possible, but Evidence->Decision is not automatically valid without an intervening governance mechanism.

b_rows_sample.anchor: GovernanceDecision → Knowledge → AgentContext → EngineeringAction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the bottom-up half (Runtime->Observation->Evidence->Finding->GovernanceInput) and the reverse top-down half (GovernanceDecision->Knowledge->AgentContext->EngineeringAction), together making KnowledgeOS the semantic bridge Governance <-> EngineeringReality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Architect = Classification/Assessment; GovernancePolicy = DefinesDecisionAuthority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Answers 'is the Domain Architect the person who decides whether something requires governance?' — generally no: the architect performs Classification/Assessment while GovernancePolicy defines decision authority; the architect may apply governance rules but should not be sole authority source unless explicitly assigned; worked with a Nexus-upgrade example flow (change -> engineering/project -> business+architecture assessment -> governance classification -> required path -> decision -> implementation) where authority belongs to the organizational governance framework, not automatically to whoever performed the assessment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: BusinessImpact, ArchitectureImpact, SecurityImpact, OperationalImpact, RegulatoryImpact, TechnologyRisk.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes governance should be triggered by change characteristics, not personal judgment alone, listing six trigger dimensions; defines a classification engine Change->Classification with results Standard/Governed/ArchitectureRelevant/SecurityRelevant/HighRisk, automatable for simple cases but policy-defined in meaning; an agent may gather affected components/dependencies/decisions/runtime impact/historical changes/similar cases and recommend a classification, but Recommendation ≠ FinalClassification unless delegated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Governance Package ├── Change ... └── Recommendation
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a Governance Package KnowledgeOS should assemble (Change, Business Intent, Affected Systems, Architecture Context, Existing Decisions, Runtime Evidence, Security Evidence, Risk, Agent Analysis, Deterministic Checks, Recommendation) so the human decision-maker receives a decision-ready evidence package rather than a pile of documents — framed as where KnowledgeOS provides real value, an 'engineering decision-support system' able to answer what changed/expected/deployed/governing-decisions/evidence/risks/governance-path/agent-conclusion/checks-passed/remaining-uncertainty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Task → RelevantContext.
b_rows_sample.statement: States agent context construction should be task-scoped (Task->RelevantContext = AuthoritativeKnowledge+RelevantEvidence+CurrentState+ApplicablePolicy) rather than the entire knowledge universe; every context element should retain SourceID so the agent can cite provenance ('this comes from ADR-042, effective since June 2026') rather than an unattributed 'the system told me this.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Constitutional rules ... 9. Historical context
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a nine-level context precedence hierarchy (constitutional rules, applicable governance policies, current authoritative decisions, current architecture, verified implementation state, runtime observations, approved exceptions, agent inference, historical context), noting actual precedence must be formally defined rather than assumed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rule + Exception → EffectiveState.
b_rows_sample.statement: Models exception handling as Rule+Exception->EffectiveState rather than the exception destroying the rule (e.g. Rule: UseArchitectureA; Exception: ServiceX may use B until T; Effective(ServiceX,t<T)=B while Effective(OtherService,t)=A); requires an agent to retrieve both Rule and ApplicableExceptions since ignoring an exception creates false findings — Conformance = ExpectedRule + ExceptionContext.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Business → Domain Architect → Architecture Board → KnowledgeOS → {Claude, Codex} → Engineering → Runtime → Evidence → KnowledgeOS
b_rows_sample.statement: Diagrams the complete, deliberately circular actor-interaction chain and states KnowledgeOS is 'the continuity layer' preventing the fragmentation that would otherwise occur when BusinessDecision, Architecture, Code, Runtime, Evidence, and AgentContext each live in separate, disconnected systems.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agents can participate in governance workflows; they do not automatically possess governance authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 125 verdict: the operating model Business->Architecture->Governance->KnowledgeOS->Agent->Engineering->Runtime->Evidence->KnowledgeOS with explicit Knowledge/Classification/Authorization/Assurance/Closure gates, and the central organizational principle that agents can participate in governance workflows without automatically possessing governance authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The KnowledgeOS Kernel should not be understood as the whole of knowledge. It is the epistemic mechanism through which a bounded knower processes a changing knowledge state while being unable to directly contain the whole knowledge space.
b_rows_sample.statement: Strongest Chapter 11 finding: the KnowledgeOS Kernel is not the whole of knowledge but the epistemic mechanism through which a bounded knower processes a changing knowledge state while unable to directly contain the whole knowledge space K. Formalized as Kernel observes/processes a projection of K: O_t = Omega(K_t, K, context), connecting to the previously-established Sanjaya/Omega hypothesis. Chapter 11 corroborates rather than derives this (Step 286 discipline).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown \neq Non-existent
b_rows_sample.statement: x not-in O_t does not imply x not-in K (the knowledge space): 'not observed' must not be equated with 'does not exist'. Proposed as a potentially fundamental KnowledgeOS principle: Unknown != Non-existent. Prevents the dangerous kernel behavior chain 'not observed -> not represented -> false'; the correct chain is 'not observed -> not currently known -> epistemic gap'.

Ten labeled research findings (explicitly not architecture decisions): H11-1 Observation is perspective-bound (O_t != K); H11-2 Expanded observation != complete knowledge (O_t-up does not imply K_t=K); H11-3 Knowledge state changes through time (K_t != K_{t+1}); H11-4 State and process must remain distinguishable (Event != State); H11-5 Seeing does not equal understanding (Observation != Knowledge); H11-6 Knowledge requires discrimination (O_t --Buddhi--> D_t); H11-7 A larger observation can expose rather than eliminate uncertainty; H11-8 Different projections may describe different aspects of a larger state (R_1=pi_1(K), R_2=pi_2(K)); H11-9 Persistence must be distinguished from state identity (Kernel continuity != K_t identity); H11-10 The Kernel must not mistake its representation for reality (Model of Knowledge != Knowledge Space itself).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Buddhi is a critical control point
b_rows_sample.statement: The kernel/mind 'enemy' danger is not only bad data but can arise from: (1) incomplete observation, (2) overwhelming observation, (3) incorrect interpretation, (4) defective discrimination, (5) incorrect decision, (6) state transition based on that decision -- pipeline O_t -> B_t -> D_t -> K_{t+1}. Hence Buddhi is a critical control point in the kernel architecture. Observation != Understanding and Understanding != Discrimination.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Bounded Context \neq \text{Whole Reality}
b_rows_sample.statement: DDD consequence: a bounded context may be only a local projection of a larger reality; this does not invalidate bounded contexts but makes the boundary explicit (Bounded Context != Whole Reality), preventing the Kernel from confusing its represented world with the world itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 11 does **not** establish ... that KnowledgeOS Kernel = mind; that Buddhi is a KnowledgeOS primitive; that \Omega = Sa\~njaya
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit list of what Chapter 11 does NOT establish, maintaining methodological discipline: not that KnowledgeOS Kernel = mind; not that Buddhi is a KnowledgeOS primitive; not that Omega = Sanjaya; not that K (knowledge space) is equivalent to the universal form; not that Moksha = complete knowledge; not that Time should become a Kernel primitive; not that a universal-view operation should exist; not that a particular architecture is mandated. Required chain: Gita observation -> philosophical interpretation -> KnowledgeOS hypothesis -> independent derivation -> falsification -> architecture only if justified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal K \overset{\Omega}{\longrightarrow} O_t \overset{\mathcal B}{\longrightarrow} D_t \overset{\delta}{\longrightarrow} K_{t+1}
b_rows_sample.statement: The central kernel question evolves from 'what operations does the Kernel perform?' to 'what can a bounded KnowledgeOS Kernel legitimately know, observe, discriminate, and conclude about a knowledge space larger than its current state?'. Final research-model pipeline: K (Knowledge Space) --Omega (observation/projection)--> O_t (observation) --B (Buddhi/discrimination)--> D_t (discrimination result) --delta (state transition)--> K_{t+1} (new Knowledge State). Explicitly not yet canonical architecture; identifies convergence of existing open questions about Observation, Proposition, State, Event, Buddhi, Qualify, delta, and the five-axis Sigma.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A Zero does not necessarily mean "Nothing exists." It may mean "Nothing is represented in the currently observed projection."
b_rows_sample.statement: From Chapter 11's Visvarupa (universal form): a kernel may see only a local projection pi_X(K) while the theoretical whole is K, giving local knowledge != knowledge space as a whole. Reinterprets Zero accordingly: rather than meaning 'nothing exists', a Zero detection may mean 'nothing is represented in the currently observed projection' -- proposed as a much stronger formal interpretation, potentially important for the Zero theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Integrity(K_t) = Virtue(K_t) ∧ ¬Vice(K_t) ... Virtue(K_t) = All 26 divine qualities present ... Vice(K_t) = Any demonic quality present
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Integrity(K_t) as conjunction of Virtue(K_t) (all divine qualities present) and negation of Vice(K_t) (no demonic quality present); later refined (Part 4.4) to a difference Integrity(K_t)=Virtue(K_t)-Vice(K_t) with Virtue/Vice as sums of per-quality indicator terms and SystemCharacter(K_t) case-split into Daivi/Asuri/Mixed by the sign of Integrity(K_t).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Twenty-six qualities define epistemic virtue ... | Fearlessness | Willingness to confront gaps, errors | ... (table lists 15 rows)
a_rows_sample.statement: Internal inconsistency: the document asserts 26 divine qualities (matching the Gita's traditional count) but its own enumeration table (Section 1.2 and Section 4.1) lists only 15 named quality-to-KnowledgeOS-measure mappings, not 26 — the claimed count and the delivered mapping are mismatched within the same document.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DemonicCycle(K_t) = Attachment(K_t) > 0 ∧ Confidence(K_t) > Evidence(K_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a formal failure condition for epistemic 'demonic cycle': Attachment(K_t)>0 AND Confidence(K_t)>Evidence(K_t), i.e. miscalibration where stated confidence exceeds the evidence that supports it, mapped to the Gita's cycle of greed/pride/dissatisfaction (16.13-15).

a_rows_sample.anchor: GatesToHell = {Lust, Greed, Anger} ... EpistemicFailure(K_t) = Lust(K_t) ∨ Greed(K_t) ∨ Anger(K_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines three 'gates' to epistemic failure mapped from Gita 16.21-22: Lust=attachment to EC=TRUE, Greed=evidence hoarding (acquisition without evaluation), Anger=defensiveness/hostility to challenge; EpistemicFailure(K_t) is their disjunction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Liberation(K_t) = Authority(K_t) ∧ Understanding(K_t) ∧ Action(K_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes liberation/epistemic success as requiring the conjunction of Authority (ratified epistemic standards), Understanding (epistemic maturity), and Action (Decision Readiness), derived from Gita 16.23-24's injunction to let scripture be authority.
