a_rows_sample.anchor: Human first has/conceives an Ideal State ... IDEAL STATE -> EXPECTATIONS/CRITERIA -> OBSERVATION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT/KNOWLEDGE. That is a substantially different model from the one I was using before.
a_rows_sample.statement: Major reorientation: humans do not build up an ideal state from arbitrary observations; instead a human first has/conceives an Ideal State and then evaluates reality against it, giving the pipeline IDEAL STATE -> EXPECTATIONS/CRITERIA -> OBSERVATION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT/KNOWLEDGE, substantially reversing the previously-used observation-first model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ideal state ... The complete state of what is supposed to be known/true/valid for the thing at that point in time. ... all applicable rules; all required participants; ... I_t = Ideal Knowledge State at t ... O_t -- comparison with I_t --> K_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the ideal state I_t broadly as the complete state of what is supposed to be known/true/valid for a thing at time t; for an election system this would include all applicable rules, required participants, required conditions, valid relationships, required evidence, expected states, constraints, applicable laws, and known principles; every new piece of observed information O_t is evaluated against I_t, giving the extraction problem O_t --comparison with I_t--> K_t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Information that correctly describes some aspect of the ideal state is Knowledge. ... K_t subset I_t ... The ideal state itself may be unknown to us. ... I_t -- the theoretical ideal state, and hat-I_t -- our current extracted/estimated representation of it. Then: hat-I_t != I_t in general. That may actually explain your earlier statement: "We try our best but never achieve the best."
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines 'information on the ideal state is knowledge' to 'information that correctly describes some aspect of the ideal state is Knowledge', giving K_t subset-or-equal I_t as the established/identified portion of the ideal state -- but the ideal state I_t itself may be unknown to us, so we must distinguish the theoretical ideal state I_t from our current extracted/estimated representation hat-I_t, with hat-I_t != I_t in general, explaining 'we try our best but never achieve the best'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(x|O_{<=t},I_t^known) ... Probability is involved in extracting the ideal state from imperfect observations. Not: Knowledge=Probability. Instead: Probability models the uncertainty of our extraction of the ideal state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Locates probability's role: for an ideal-state element x, given incomplete and overlapping observations O_1..O_n we estimate P(x|O_{<=t},I_t^known); probability is involved in extracting the ideal state from imperfect observations, not in defining Knowledge -- probability models the uncertainty of our extraction of the ideal state, not Knowledge itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: System must have backup capability ... backup configuration exists ... If the applicable reasoning rules determine that the observation satisfies the criterion, we establish: F_t: "System has backup capability." ... the fact is not produced merely from the observation. It is produced by: Observation + Ideal State + Comparison Criteria + Reasoning.
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example of fact production: ideal state I_t requires 'system must have backup capability', observation O_t is 'backup configuration exists'; comparing O_t against I_t via applicable reasoning rules establishes fact F_t='System has backup capability' -- a fact is produced not merely from observation but from Observation + Ideal State + Comparison Criteria + Reasoning together.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Logic = mechanism for comparing/deriving consequences from the ideal state and observed state. ... I_t: A and B and C. Observed: O_t: A,B,not-C. Logic gives: O_t does not entail I_t. Therefore the determination might be: F_t: "Current state does not satisfy the ideal state."
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines logic's role as the mechanism for comparing/deriving consequences from the ideal state and observed state: given ideal state I_t=(A and B and C) and observed O_t=(A,B,not-C), logic determines O_t does not entail I_t, yielding determination F_t='Current state does not satisfy the ideal state'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(A)=1, P(B)=0.9, P(C)=0.6, P(D)=0.2. Then our extracted representation of the ideal/current relationship is uncertain. The probability is therefore attached to the extraction/determination, not necessarily to the underlying ideal state itself. That gives: I_t -> hat-I_t where hat-I_t is probabilistically estimated from available information.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explains the origin of graded 0-to-1 values: if the ideal state requires A,B,C,D but observations only partially resolve them (P(A)=1,P(B)=0.9,P(C)=0.6,P(D)=0.2), the extracted representation of the ideal/current relationship is uncertain -- this probability attaches to the extraction/determination I_t -> hat-I_t, not to the underlying ideal state itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Where does the Ideal State come from? ... A. Given by reality I_t=Reality_t B. Given by human knowledge I_t=HumanModel_t C. Given by rules/laws/principles I_t=NormativeModel_t D. Given by the domain model I_t=DomainModel_t E. An ideal mathematical state I_t=I* F. Some combination I_t=f(Reality,Rules,Principles,Domain,HumanKnowledge). We should not assume which one it is.
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses 'Where does the Ideal State come from?' as, in the author's opinion, the most important unresolved problem, with six unassumed candidate sources: given by reality (I_t=Reality_t), given by human knowledge (I_t=HumanModel_t), given by rules/laws/principles (I_t=NormativeModel_t), given by the domain model (I_t=DomainModel_t), an ideal mathematical state (I_t=I*), or some combination I_t=f(Reality,Rules,Principles,Domain,HumanKnowledge) -- explicitly: we should not assume which one it is.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge = identified elements/relationships of an ideal state. And the current Knowledge state is K_t while the ideal state is I_t. The goal of knowledge extraction could therefore be: K_t -> I_t or more realistically: K_t approx I_t with the difference I_t - K_t representing what remains unknown, uncertain, or unextracted.
a_rows_sample.statement: Resolves 'is Knowledge a collection of facts?' into a richer formulation: Knowledge = identified elements/relationships of an ideal state; with current knowledge state K_t and ideal state I_t, knowledge extraction aims at K_t -> I_t or more realistically K_t approx I_t, with the residual I_t - K_t representing what remains unknown, uncertain, or unextracted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "Every information on the ideal state of anything is knowledge." I would change "every information" to "every correctly determined proposition about the ideal state". ... "I believe the ideal state contains X." That is information about someone's belief, not necessarily Knowledge about the ideal state. ... "The document says X." ... Information about an ideal state != Knowledge of the ideal state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Challenges the overbroad claim 'every information on the ideal state of anything is knowledge', proposing instead 'every correctly determined proposition about the ideal state'; example: 'I believe the ideal state contains X' is information about someone's belief, not Knowledge about the ideal state, and 'the document says X' is knowledge that the document says X, not knowledge that X is true. Preserves the distinction: Information about an ideal state != Knowledge of the ideal state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: IDEAL STATE -> (defines expected/relevant structure) -> OBSERVED REALITY -> INFORMATION -> EXTRACTION -> (evidence/uncertainty) -> COMPARISON (ideal <-> observed) -> LOGIC -> DETERMINATION -> FACTS -> KNOWLEDGE STATE -> update over time. ... Probability primarily helps with the extraction from imperfect information, while Logic helps determine consequences and relationships.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the full revised pipeline diagram: IDEAL STATE (defines expected/relevant structure) -> OBSERVED REALITY -> INFORMATION -> EXTRACTION (branching into evidence and uncertainty) -> COMPARISON (ideal<->observed) -> LOGIC -> DETERMINATION -> FACTS -> KNOWLEDGE STATE -> update over time; probability primarily helps with extraction from imperfect information, logic helps determine consequences and relationships.

a_rows_sample.anchor: before determination, we now need to investigate: What is the Ideal State? Because determination is: D_t = Compare(Observed_t, Ideal_t) and if we don't understand Ideal_t, we don't fully understand D_t. ... IDEAL STATE -> OBSERVATION -> EXTRACTION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT -> KNOWLEDGE
a_rows_sample.statement: Revises the research direction: before determination can be understood, 'What is the Ideal State?' must be investigated, since determination is formalized as D_t=Compare(Observed_t,Ideal_t) and understanding D_t requires understanding Ideal_t; sets the research sequence as IDEAL STATE -> OBSERVATION -> EXTRACTION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT -> KNOWLEDGE, with Probability->uncertain extraction and Logic->comparison and consequence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the fundamental question for KnowledgeOS is not "How do we store Knowledge?" and not even "How do we extract Knowledge?" It may be: "How is an ideal state of Knowledge defined, and how does a system continuously determine its current relationship to that ideal state?" ... Knowledge becomes the currently justified representation of the relationship between them. I would now research Ideal State / normative state / complete state / target state / possible-world state / domain model / epistemic idealization across mathematics, epistemology, AI, systems theory, DDD, and philosophy before we touch the Kernel again.
a_rows_sample.statement: States what may be 'the biggest discovery so far': the fundamental KnowledgeOS question may be neither 'how do we store Knowledge' nor 'how do we extract Knowledge' but 'how is an ideal state of Knowledge defined, and how does a system continuously determine its current relationship to that ideal state?'; Knowledge becomes the currently justified representation of the relationship between Ideal State and Observed State. Proposes researching Ideal State / normative state / complete state / target state / possible-world state / domain model / epistemic idealization across mathematics, epistemology, AI, systems theory, DDD, and philosophy before returning to Kernel definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "Every information" you mean all possible information about the thing, not merely "some information." So your proposition is: I_t = the totality of all possible information about the object/domain at time t. And I_t may be infinite.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets 'every information' as meaning ALL possible information about a thing, not merely some information: I_t is redefined as the totality of all possible information about the object/domain at time t, and I_t may be infinite -- a much stronger interpretation than given previously.

a_rows_sample.anchor: O_t subset I_t or, more realistically, imperfect projections of I_t. The extraction process is therefore: I_t -> observable information -> extracted knowledge, with the extraction being imperfect because the underlying elements can overlap and the observation process cannot completely distinguish them.
a_rows_sample.statement: A human/system cannot access all of the (possibly infinite) I_t, only observations O_t subset I_t or imperfect projections of it; extraction is I_t -> observable information -> extracted knowledge, imperfect because underlying elements can overlap and observation cannot completely distinguish them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K = the space of all possible information/knowledge elements ... I_t subset K is the complete/ideal information state relevant at that time. Then an observer A has only an extracted state: K_t^A subset I_t ... K_t^A != I_t in general.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens 'Knowledge is a state and subset of elements of the infinite Knowledge Space' into: K-script (the space of all possible information/knowledge elements), with I_t subset K-script being the complete/ideal information state relevant at time t; an observer A has only an extracted state K_t^A subset I_t (or a representation/projection of it), and because extraction is imperfect, K_t^A != I_t in general.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(x in I_t | O_{<=t}^A). So probability describes the extraction uncertainty. ... Knowledge itself is not probability. Rather: Probability can describe the imperfect extraction of Knowledge from the ideal information state.
a_rows_sample.statement: For an ideal-state element x in I_t that an observer cannot directly verify, the observer estimates P(x in I_t | O_{<=t}^A) given its observations -- probability describes extraction uncertainty, consistent with 'the elements overlap and only probability can extract them as separately as possible' (still to be tested as the right mathematical mechanism, but a coherent hypothesis). Knowledge itself is not probability; probability describes the imperfect extraction of Knowledge from the ideal information state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If I_t means all possible information, then we need to distinguish: possible information from true information and knowable information. ... whether your I_t means: 1. all logically possible information, or 2. all information that is actually true about the thing at t, or 3. all information that could in principle be known about the thing at t. I think this distinction is now the next critical question.
a_rows_sample.statement: Raises the next critical question: since not every possible description of a system is true, I_t must be disambiguated among three readings -- (1) all logically possible information, (2) all information that is actually true about the thing at t, or (3) all information that could in principle be known about the thing at t; this distinction will determine the meaning of the 'infinite Knowledge Space' and what KnowledgeOS is trying to extract from it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I_t = the potentially infinite space of all relevant states/propositions/relationships at time t ... K_t (script) = Infinite Knowledge Space at t and I_t subset K_t (script) could represent an ideal state/configuration of the domain. But even I_t may itself be infinite. ... K_t = Pi_t(I_t) where Pi_t is the extraction/projection available to the observer.
a_rows_sample.statement: If I_t can be infinite, it should not be modeled as a finite list of facts but as the potentially infinite space of all relevant states/propositions/relationships at t; introduces K-script_t (infinite Knowledge Space at t) with I_t subset K-script_t as an ideal state/configuration of the domain (itself possibly infinite), and the observer's actual accessible/extracted knowledge as K_t subset I_t or, more generally, K_t=Pi_t(I_t) where Pi_t is the observer's extraction/projection function.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I_t={x_1,x_2,x_3,...}. We cannot observe all of them. ... construct an estimate hat-I_t from the observations. For an element x: P(x in I_t | O_{<=t},C_t) can express our uncertainty ... probability is increasingly looking like a mathematics of extraction from an incompletely observable/infinite state, rather than a definition of Knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: With an infinite ideal state I_t={x_1,x_2,...} that cannot be fully observed, an estimate hat-I_t is constructed from observations O_{<=t}, and for an element x, P(x in I_t | O_{<=t},C_t) expresses uncertainty about membership; probability is increasingly a mathematics of extraction from an incompletely observable/infinite state, not a definition of Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Ideal State is the Knower's current model of what the Knowledge State should be ... I_t = (D_I, V_I, R_I, Sigma_I, C_I, P_I) ... Ideal State \neq Knowledge State ... Ideal State \neq Truth
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Ideal State as the Knower's model of desired dimensions/values/relationships/epistemic-state/constraints/purpose, explicitly distinct from both the current Knowledge State and Truth, and shown to be dynamic (I_{t+1}=Revision(I_t,K_t,U_t)) and both purpose-dependent (I_t(P)!=I_t(P')) and Knower-dependent (I_t(N)!=I_t(N')).

b_rows_sample.anchor: I^K_t \neq I^U_t \neq I^D_t ... I^K: what should be known ... I^U: how the knowledge should be understood/held ... I^D: what the domain reality should become
b_rows_sample.statement: Splits the single Ideal State into three distinguishable forms -- Ideal Knowledge State I^K (what should be known), Ideal Understanding State I^U (how knowledge should be understood/interpreted/applied for decision purposes), and Ideal Domain State I^D (what domain reality should become) -- resolving an ambiguity where 'ideal' had conflated epistemic target with normative/domain target.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Arjuna could possess facts such as Bhishma=grandfather without yet understanding what those facts mean for his decision. Knowledge \neq Understanding.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues via the Arjuna case that Knowledge != Understanding: possessing a fact does not entail grasping its decision-relevant implications, motivating the separate Ideal Understanding State I^U and the corresponding Understanding-comparison operation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I^D_t \Rightarrow Requirements(I^K_t) ... I^K_t \Rightarrow Requirements(I^U_t) ... these are requirements/derivations, not identities. We must not write I^D=I^K or I^K=I^U.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that the three Ideal forms are not independent (a desired domain state generates knowledge requirements, which generate understanding requirements) but must never be treated as identical, preventing collapse of domain/knowledge/understanding targets into one object.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K uparrow and Certainty downarrow ... Q_{t+1} \neq Q_t. The Knower discovers that the original question was inadequate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates via the Arjuna case that increased knowledge can accompany decreased certainty because the ideal knowledge target I^K itself grows (I^K_0 -> I^K_1) once new dimensions are discovered, sometimes producing a revised question Q_{t+1} != Q_t rather than a direct answer to Q_t.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D_E(K_t,I^K_t) \rightarrow 0 \not\Rightarrow Journey Complete ... I^K_2 \neq I^K_0 ... Knowledge acquisition can move the Ideal State. KnowledgeOS is not solving a static optimization problem. It is solving a dynamic epistemic navigation problem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Shows via the Arjuna example that measured distance reaching zero (D_E(K_2,I^K_0)=0) does not mean the epistemic journey is complete, because the Ideal State itself evolved in step (I^K_2 != I^K_0); reframes KnowledgeOS's problem as dynamic epistemic navigation rather than static optimization against a fixed target.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If the Ideal State is allowed to adapt freely to the Current Knowledge State, the system can make its own epistemic deficit disappear ... Current Knowledge must not silently redefine its own target ... Declared Ideal / Derived Ideal / Exploratory Horizon
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a critical safety failure mode: since the Ideal State is defined as dynamically revisable (I_{t+1}=Revision(I_t,K_t,...)), nothing prevents it from being set equal to current knowledge (I_t:=K_t), silently erasing all epistemic deficit even though the Knower remains ignorant; introduces the invariant 'current knowledge must not silently redefine its own target' and splits Ideal State into Declared Ideal (what the Knower explicitly requires), Derived Ideal (what KnowledgeOS derives from purpose/context/domain), and Exploratory Horizon (what Lord proposes might matter) to prevent this collapse.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not use 'all understanding' as an Ideal State; use purpose-relative sufficiency ... I^U(P) = Decision-relevant understanding sufficient for P, not I^U = Complete understanding. Adequacy \neq Completeness.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the Ideal Understanding State from an impossible 'all implications understood' target to a purpose-relative sufficiency criterion (decision-relevant implications identified and sufficiently understood for the given purpose P), consistent with the earlier Adequacy != Completeness distinction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I_{t+1} = Revision(I_t, K_t, U_t, X_t, N_t) ... The Knower is the ultimate authority over the Ideal State. KnowledgeOS != I_t; KnowledgeOS -> Suggestions for I_t; Knower -> I_t.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Ideal State evolution as a deterministic Revision function of prior ideal, current knowledge/understanding/domain state and the Knower, with six sources of change (knowledge-driven, understanding-driven, domain-driven, purpose-driven, context-driven, Knower-driven), most modelled as monotonic union-additions to the ideal, and states the Knower as sole ultimate authority over I_t.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knower Intent != Ideal State Authority... The Knower cannot simply redefine a mandatory regulatory requirement... IdealState = KnowerIntent + ApplicableNorms + Constraints + Purpose, not simply IdealState=KnowerPreference.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the absolute claim that the Knower alone owns/controls the Ideal State: real Ideal States are also constrained by law, organizational policy, domain rules, contractual obligations, safety constraints, architecture governance and regulatory requirements the Knower cannot unilaterally override -- IdealState is composed of KnowerIntent plus ApplicableNorms plus Constraints plus Purpose, never reducible to KnowerPreference alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I strongly recommend introducing: I-hat_t = Candidate Ideal State and I_t = Approved Ideal State ... KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1} (proposal); Authorize(I-hat_{t+1}) -> I_{t+1}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a Candidate Ideal State (I-hat) vs Approved Ideal State (I) split mirroring the Q17 recommendation/authorization boundary: KnowledgeOS may only ever produce a candidate revision proposal, and only an explicit Authorize step (by the Knower/governance authority under applicable norms) produces the actually approved I_{t+1}; KnowledgeOS != I_{t+1} but KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Given the same inputs, there is one correct Ideal State. That is not true... several legitimate responses: increase security requirement; change the purpose; accept the risk; change the architecture; defer the decision. RevisionCandidates: S_t -> P(I).
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects modelling Ideal-State Revision as a deterministic function returning one correct new ideal, since the same discovered deficiency (e.g. insufficient security) admits multiple legitimate responses (strengthen requirement, change purpose, accept risk, change architecture, defer); replaces it with RevisionCandidates producing a power-set of possible ideal states, from which Authorize selects the approved one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the union equations are too strong ... this assumes Ideal State evolution is monotonic expansion. But later you correctly allow Remove Dimension, Revise Value, Revise Constraint. I_{t+1}=Revision(I_t,Delta_t,Authority_t) with Add | Remove | Modify | Relax | Strengthen | Replace.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the union-based Ideal-State evolution equations (I^K_{t+1}=I^K_t union NewRequiredDimensions(K_t)) as an inconsistent general law -- since removal/modification operations were also defined elsewhere -- replacing them with a general revision admitting Add/Remove/Modify/Relax/Strengthen/Replace operations, with the union form retained only as one example instance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q18 should distinguish discovery from revision... Discovery -> Proposal -> Evaluation -> Authorization -> Revision ... Ideal State itself should have history: H^I_t, I_t=Replay(I_0,H^I_t,Pi_I). Ideal-State revision should itself be an event: I_{t+1}=delta_I(I_t,r_t).
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes symmetry between Knowledge-State and Ideal-State evolution: Ideal-State revisions must go through the same Discovery->Proposal->Evaluation->Authorization->Revision sequence as knowledge events, be recorded as an authorized IdealStateRevisionAuthorized event r_t, accumulate in an append-only Ideal-State history H^I_t, and be reconstructible via I_t=Replay(I_0,H^I_t,Pi_I) -- giving the Ideal State the same provenance/auditability the Knowledge State already has.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS cannot formally encode 'Dharma transcends personal duty' as an objective fact merely because Sarathi/Lord/Krishna proposed it. It must be represented as Proposition + Source + EpistemicStatus + Context. Observation != Interpretation != Guidance != Truth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the Arjuna worked example: 'Krishna's guidance' that dharma transcends personal duty cannot be encoded as an objective fact simply because a guidance capability proposed it; it must remain a Proposition tagged with Source, EpistemicStatus, and Context like any other assertion, preserving Observation != Interpretation != Guidance != Truth even for guidance content originating from the most authoritative-seeming source in the corpus's own narrative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ideal State Does Not Automatically Evolve... The system should not autonomously revise the Ideal State merely because new knowledge appears... Discovery may motivate Ideal revision but Discovery not=> Ideal revision.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the deterministic Ideal-State evolution equation I_{t+1}=Revision(I_t,K_t,U_t,X_t,N_t) as too permissive at the system-state level (it would let the system autonomously mutate its own evaluation target from new knowledge alone); replaces it with I_{t+1}=ReviseIdeal(I_t,r_t) requiring an explicitly authorized revision event r_t -- Discovery may motivate but never automatically implies an Ideal-State revision.

a_notations: IDEAL STATE -> OBSERVATION -> EXTRACTION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT -> KNOWLEDGE

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'ideal-state-formalization' POSSIBLY relates to 'ideal-state-comparison-model' (batch B0019). Note: This batch's own re-derivation of the Ideal State as the Knower's target model against which Knowledge/Understanding/Domain-reality are each compared, split into I^K/I^U/I^D forms; flagged as possibly related to the pre-existing ideal-state-comparison-model (B0017) but developed independently within this phase_measure_theory thread without citing it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Human first has/conceives an Ideal State ... IDEAL STATE -> EXPECTATIONS/CRITERIA -> OBSERVATION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT/KNOWLEDGE. That is a substantially different model from the one I was using before.
a_rows_sample.statement: Major reorientation: humans do not build up an ideal state from arbitrary observations; instead a human first has/conceives an Ideal State and then evaluates reality against it, giving the pipeline IDEAL STATE -> EXPECTATIONS/CRITERIA -> OBSERVATION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT/KNOWLEDGE, substantially reversing the previously-used observation-first model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ideal state ... The complete state of what is supposed to be known/true/valid for the thing at that point in time. ... all applicable rules; all required participants; ... I_t = Ideal Knowledge State at t ... O_t -- comparison with I_t --> K_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the ideal state I_t broadly as the complete state of what is supposed to be known/true/valid for a thing at time t; for an election system this would include all applicable rules, required participants, required conditions, valid relationships, required evidence, expected states, constraints, applicable laws, and known principles; every new piece of observed information O_t is evaluated against I_t, giving the extraction problem O_t --comparison with I_t--> K_t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Information that correctly describes some aspect of the ideal state is Knowledge. ... K_t subset I_t ... The ideal state itself may be unknown to us. ... I_t -- the theoretical ideal state, and hat-I_t -- our current extracted/estimated representation of it. Then: hat-I_t != I_t in general. That may actually explain your earlier statement: "We try our best but never achieve the best."
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines 'information on the ideal state is knowledge' to 'information that correctly describes some aspect of the ideal state is Knowledge', giving K_t subset-or-equal I_t as the established/identified portion of the ideal state -- but the ideal state I_t itself may be unknown to us, so we must distinguish the theoretical ideal state I_t from our current extracted/estimated representation hat-I_t, with hat-I_t != I_t in general, explaining 'we try our best but never achieve the best'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(x|O_{<=t},I_t^known) ... Probability is involved in extracting the ideal state from imperfect observations. Not: Knowledge=Probability. Instead: Probability models the uncertainty of our extraction of the ideal state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Locates probability's role: for an ideal-state element x, given incomplete and overlapping observations O_1..O_n we estimate P(x|O_{<=t},I_t^known); probability is involved in extracting the ideal state from imperfect observations, not in defining Knowledge -- probability models the uncertainty of our extraction of the ideal state, not Knowledge itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: System must have backup capability ... backup configuration exists ... If the applicable reasoning rules determine that the observation satisfies the criterion, we establish: F_t: "System has backup capability." ... the fact is not produced merely from the observation. It is produced by: Observation + Ideal State + Comparison Criteria + Reasoning.
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example of fact production: ideal state I_t requires 'system must have backup capability', observation O_t is 'backup configuration exists'; comparing O_t against I_t via applicable reasoning rules establishes fact F_t='System has backup capability' -- a fact is produced not merely from observation but from Observation + Ideal State + Comparison Criteria + Reasoning together.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Logic = mechanism for comparing/deriving consequences from the ideal state and observed state. ... I_t: A and B and C. Observed: O_t: A,B,not-C. Logic gives: O_t does not entail I_t. Therefore the determination might be: F_t: "Current state does not satisfy the ideal state."
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines logic's role as the mechanism for comparing/deriving consequences from the ideal state and observed state: given ideal state I_t=(A and B and C) and observed O_t=(A,B,not-C), logic determines O_t does not entail I_t, yielding determination F_t='Current state does not satisfy the ideal state'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(A)=1, P(B)=0.9, P(C)=0.6, P(D)=0.2. Then our extracted representation of the ideal/current relationship is uncertain. The probability is therefore attached to the extraction/determination, not necessarily to the underlying ideal state itself. That gives: I_t -> hat-I_t where hat-I_t is probabilistically estimated from available information.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explains the origin of graded 0-to-1 values: if the ideal state requires A,B,C,D but observations only partially resolve them (P(A)=1,P(B)=0.9,P(C)=0.6,P(D)=0.2), the extracted representation of the ideal/current relationship is uncertain -- this probability attaches to the extraction/determination I_t -> hat-I_t, not to the underlying ideal state itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Where does the Ideal State come from? ... A. Given by reality I_t=Reality_t B. Given by human knowledge I_t=HumanModel_t C. Given by rules/laws/principles I_t=NormativeModel_t D. Given by the domain model I_t=DomainModel_t E. An ideal mathematical state I_t=I* F. Some combination I_t=f(Reality,Rules,Principles,Domain,HumanKnowledge). We should not assume which one it is.
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses 'Where does the Ideal State come from?' as, in the author's opinion, the most important unresolved problem, with six unassumed candidate sources: given by reality (I_t=Reality_t), given by human knowledge (I_t=HumanModel_t), given by rules/laws/principles (I_t=NormativeModel_t), given by the domain model (I_t=DomainModel_t), an ideal mathematical state (I_t=I*), or some combination I_t=f(Reality,Rules,Principles,Domain,HumanKnowledge) -- explicitly: we should not assume which one it is.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge = identified elements/relationships of an ideal state. And the current Knowledge state is K_t while the ideal state is I_t. The goal of knowledge extraction could therefore be: K_t -> I_t or more realistically: K_t approx I_t with the difference I_t - K_t representing what remains unknown, uncertain, or unextracted.
a_rows_sample.statement: Resolves 'is Knowledge a collection of facts?' into a richer formulation: Knowledge = identified elements/relationships of an ideal state; with current knowledge state K_t and ideal state I_t, knowledge extraction aims at K_t -> I_t or more realistically K_t approx I_t, with the residual I_t - K_t representing what remains unknown, uncertain, or unextracted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "Every information on the ideal state of anything is knowledge." I would change "every information" to "every correctly determined proposition about the ideal state". ... "I believe the ideal state contains X." That is information about someone's belief, not necessarily Knowledge about the ideal state. ... "The document says X." ... Information about an ideal state != Knowledge of the ideal state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Challenges the overbroad claim 'every information on the ideal state of anything is knowledge', proposing instead 'every correctly determined proposition about the ideal state'; example: 'I believe the ideal state contains X' is information about someone's belief, not Knowledge about the ideal state, and 'the document says X' is knowledge that the document says X, not knowledge that X is true. Preserves the distinction: Information about an ideal state != Knowledge of the ideal state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: IDEAL STATE -> (defines expected/relevant structure) -> OBSERVED REALITY -> INFORMATION -> EXTRACTION -> (evidence/uncertainty) -> COMPARISON (ideal <-> observed) -> LOGIC -> DETERMINATION -> FACTS -> KNOWLEDGE STATE -> update over time. ... Probability primarily helps with the extraction from imperfect information, while Logic helps determine consequences and relationships.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the full revised pipeline diagram: IDEAL STATE (defines expected/relevant structure) -> OBSERVED REALITY -> INFORMATION -> EXTRACTION (branching into evidence and uncertainty) -> COMPARISON (ideal<->observed) -> LOGIC -> DETERMINATION -> FACTS -> KNOWLEDGE STATE -> update over time; probability primarily helps with extraction from imperfect information, logic helps determine consequences and relationships.

a_rows_sample.anchor: before determination, we now need to investigate: What is the Ideal State? Because determination is: D_t = Compare(Observed_t, Ideal_t) and if we don't understand Ideal_t, we don't fully understand D_t. ... IDEAL STATE -> OBSERVATION -> EXTRACTION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT -> KNOWLEDGE
a_rows_sample.statement: Revises the research direction: before determination can be understood, 'What is the Ideal State?' must be investigated, since determination is formalized as D_t=Compare(Observed_t,Ideal_t) and understanding D_t requires understanding Ideal_t; sets the research sequence as IDEAL STATE -> OBSERVATION -> EXTRACTION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT -> KNOWLEDGE, with Probability->uncertain extraction and Logic->comparison and consequence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the fundamental question for KnowledgeOS is not "How do we store Knowledge?" and not even "How do we extract Knowledge?" It may be: "How is an ideal state of Knowledge defined, and how does a system continuously determine its current relationship to that ideal state?" ... Knowledge becomes the currently justified representation of the relationship between them. I would now research Ideal State / normative state / complete state / target state / possible-world state / domain model / epistemic idealization across mathematics, epistemology, AI, systems theory, DDD, and philosophy before we touch the Kernel again.
a_rows_sample.statement: States what may be 'the biggest discovery so far': the fundamental KnowledgeOS question may be neither 'how do we store Knowledge' nor 'how do we extract Knowledge' but 'how is an ideal state of Knowledge defined, and how does a system continuously determine its current relationship to that ideal state?'; Knowledge becomes the currently justified representation of the relationship between Ideal State and Observed State. Proposes researching Ideal State / normative state / complete state / target state / possible-world state / domain model / epistemic idealization across mathematics, epistemology, AI, systems theory, DDD, and philosophy before returning to Kernel definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "Every information" you mean all possible information about the thing, not merely "some information." So your proposition is: I_t = the totality of all possible information about the object/domain at time t. And I_t may be infinite.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets 'every information' as meaning ALL possible information about a thing, not merely some information: I_t is redefined as the totality of all possible information about the object/domain at time t, and I_t may be infinite -- a much stronger interpretation than given previously.

a_rows_sample.anchor: O_t subset I_t or, more realistically, imperfect projections of I_t. The extraction process is therefore: I_t -> observable information -> extracted knowledge, with the extraction being imperfect because the underlying elements can overlap and the observation process cannot completely distinguish them.
a_rows_sample.statement: A human/system cannot access all of the (possibly infinite) I_t, only observations O_t subset I_t or imperfect projections of it; extraction is I_t -> observable information -> extracted knowledge, imperfect because underlying elements can overlap and observation cannot completely distinguish them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K = the space of all possible information/knowledge elements ... I_t subset K is the complete/ideal information state relevant at that time. Then an observer A has only an extracted state: K_t^A subset I_t ... K_t^A != I_t in general.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens 'Knowledge is a state and subset of elements of the infinite Knowledge Space' into: K-script (the space of all possible information/knowledge elements), with I_t subset K-script being the complete/ideal information state relevant at time t; an observer A has only an extracted state K_t^A subset I_t (or a representation/projection of it), and because extraction is imperfect, K_t^A != I_t in general.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(x in I_t | O_{<=t}^A). So probability describes the extraction uncertainty. ... Knowledge itself is not probability. Rather: Probability can describe the imperfect extraction of Knowledge from the ideal information state.
a_rows_sample.statement: For an ideal-state element x in I_t that an observer cannot directly verify, the observer estimates P(x in I_t | O_{<=t}^A) given its observations -- probability describes extraction uncertainty, consistent with 'the elements overlap and only probability can extract them as separately as possible' (still to be tested as the right mathematical mechanism, but a coherent hypothesis). Knowledge itself is not probability; probability describes the imperfect extraction of Knowledge from the ideal information state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If I_t means all possible information, then we need to distinguish: possible information from true information and knowable information. ... whether your I_t means: 1. all logically possible information, or 2. all information that is actually true about the thing at t, or 3. all information that could in principle be known about the thing at t. I think this distinction is now the next critical question.
a_rows_sample.statement: Raises the next critical question: since not every possible description of a system is true, I_t must be disambiguated among three readings -- (1) all logically possible information, (2) all information that is actually true about the thing at t, or (3) all information that could in principle be known about the thing at t; this distinction will determine the meaning of the 'infinite Knowledge Space' and what KnowledgeOS is trying to extract from it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I_t = the potentially infinite space of all relevant states/propositions/relationships at time t ... K_t (script) = Infinite Knowledge Space at t and I_t subset K_t (script) could represent an ideal state/configuration of the domain. But even I_t may itself be infinite. ... K_t = Pi_t(I_t) where Pi_t is the extraction/projection available to the observer.
a_rows_sample.statement: If I_t can be infinite, it should not be modeled as a finite list of facts but as the potentially infinite space of all relevant states/propositions/relationships at t; introduces K-script_t (infinite Knowledge Space at t) with I_t subset K-script_t as an ideal state/configuration of the domain (itself possibly infinite), and the observer's actual accessible/extracted knowledge as K_t subset I_t or, more generally, K_t=Pi_t(I_t) where Pi_t is the observer's extraction/projection function.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I_t={x_1,x_2,x_3,...}. We cannot observe all of them. ... construct an estimate hat-I_t from the observations. For an element x: P(x in I_t | O_{<=t},C_t) can express our uncertainty ... probability is increasingly looking like a mathematics of extraction from an incompletely observable/infinite state, rather than a definition of Knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: With an infinite ideal state I_t={x_1,x_2,...} that cannot be fully observed, an estimate hat-I_t is constructed from observations O_{<=t}, and for an element x, P(x in I_t | O_{<=t},C_t) expresses uncertainty about membership; probability is increasingly a mathematics of extraction from an incompletely observable/infinite state, not a definition of Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1} = Learn( K_t, Observations_t, Events_t, Policies_t, Outcomes_t )... the source states the decision and world equations (A_t = Decision(K_t, S_t, Policy_t); S_{t+1} = F(S_t, A_t, U_t)), keeping three evolutions -- of knowledge, of choices, of the world -- as three different functions.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the knowledge state's time-indexed dynamics as three separate evolution functions: K_{t+1}=Learn(K_t, Observations_t, Events_t, Policies_t, Outcomes_t) for knowledge, A_t=Decision(K_t, S_t, Policy_t) for choices, and S_{t+1}=F(S_t, A_t, U_t) for the world -- kept as three distinct functions, with time-indexing meaning there is no bare "the knowledge," only knowledge-as-of-t.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CORE: Entity, State, Event, Observation / EPISTEMIC: Evidence, Claim, Uncertainty / SEMANTIC:... / RELATIONAL:... / GOVERNANCE:... / OPERATIONAL:... / EVOLUTION:... Then, family by family, the source interrogates each concept -- is this primitive, or constructible? -- and most collapse... What survives... K = (E, S, T, O, P, R, Pi, A)
b_rows_sample.statement: Reproduces the source's reduction derivation from an initial seven-family stratification (Core/Epistemic/Semantic/Relational/Governance/Operational/Evolution) to the frozen eight-tuple candidate kernel K=(E,S,T,O,P,R,Pi,A) -- entities, states, temporal/event structure, observations, propositions, typed relations, policies, actions -- by showing most non-core concepts (Evidence, Claim, Identity, Provenance, Causality/Dependency, Uncertainty, Authority/Decision, Outcome, Learning/Revision/Drift) individually reduce to typed structure over the four cores plus the four surviving structure-carriers (Proposition, Relation, Policy, Action).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence = QualifiedObservation... Claim = Proposition... Identity = EntityIdentityRelation... Uncertainty = epistemic annotation U(C) (probabilistic OR not -- 49.10's Probability != EpistemicConfidence)... Authority = governance structure over decisions (Authority(actor, d))... resist inventing primitives -- the reduction's whole yield is that richer notions are TYPED STRUCTURE
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists the derived-structure layer -- the equations by which richer concepts are expressed as typed structure over the eight primitives rather than as new primitives themselves (Evidence=QualifiedObservation; Claim=Proposition; Identity=EntityIdentityRelation; Provenance=TypedDependencyRelation; Uncertainty=epistemic annotation U(C), explicitly not assumed probabilistic -- Probability != EpistemicConfidence; Authority=governance structure over decisions; Decision=structure over K,S,Policy with Proposal kept distinct from AuthorizedDecision; Outcome=observed consequence of Action; Learning/Revision/Drift=evolution structure) and states the modelling discipline this yields: resist inventing new primitives, since typed structure can be checked/queried/governed in ways ad-hoc primitives cannot.

b_rows_sample.anchor: stress-tested by twelve falsification experiments (49.78-49.89... What the argument does not and cannot claim, and the source itself refuses to claim: completeness... minimality... and uniqueness... The source's own word is the governing one: a candidate mathematical kernel.
b_rows_sample.statement: Teaches PF-2 in place at its exact strength: the eight-primitive reduction argument is RECONSTRUCTABLE, stress-tested by twelve falsification experiments (each attempting to express a rich concept in Structure(primitives) and failing the kernel if it cannot be done) plus Step 050's fifty-attack consistency audit; but completeness (no needed concept will ever fail to reduce), minimality (no seven-element basis would suffice -- the source concedes Entity is "arguably" Identity+State, kept for DDD-pragmatic reasons), and uniqueness (no alternative basis exists) remain explicitly NOT ESTABLISHED, matching the source's own characterization of it as a "candidate" kernel and a design result, not a theorem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Collapse the typed relation set into a single generic RelatedTo(A, B) and semantics die: an AI consumer, seeing RelatedTo everywhere, infers RelatedTo => Causes -- recreating "one of the fundamental problems we eliminated in Step 43." b_rows_sample.statement: Reproduces the source's own worked failure case for mis-typing the Relation primitive: collapsing the seven typed relations (Supports, DependsOn, Causes, Identifies, MapsTo, Contradicts, Precedes) into a single generic RelatedTo(A,B) edge causes an AI consumer to infer RelatedTo implies Causes, recreating a causal-hallucination failure mode the architecture had previously eliminated; extended to the election running example (DerivedFrom(wireSummary,wireReport) and Supports blurred into RelatedTo would let a derived summary quietly become a second independent witness) as the same dependency failure seen at the primitive-typing layer.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Headline structural findings
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven headline findings: (1) AIP is a registry-first, session-based engineering operating platform, not a product domain; (2) the implemented core is the workflow/authority engine plus guard surfaces, with knowledge/review components deferred/not built and verification under construction; (3) the invariant asymmetry is the load-bearing structural property; (4) the authority record lives in an ignored runtime directory (the durability inversion), decided-but-not-executed; (5) the D1/D2 decision state is contradictory across the corpus, surfaced not reconciled; (6) four unowned capabilities form one control loop with C-10/C-14 existence UNDECIDED; (7) AIP self-records four capability failures (EKS-01..04) -- the platform observing its own uneven assurance.

b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a safety gate as Gate(d,K,t)=InvariantSatisfied(d,K,t), with the rule that for critical invariants False => Block. For the case Invariant=Unknown, argues the default should generally be Block for safety-critical decisions -- 'a very strong architectural default' framed as a policy decision, formalized as Unknown safety condition != Safe.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Open-world versus closed-world interpretation
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes open-world semantics (absence of evidence for A does not imply not-A) from closed-world semantics (system may treat unknown A as False). Argues KnowledgeOS should not adopt one universal assumption; the applicable domain policy must specify which semantics apply. For a safety gate, Unknown->Block is usually appropriate; for exploratory analytics, Unknown->ContinueWithWarning may be appropriate; Policy_decision determines the treatment of unknowns.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Invariant taxonomy: structural, temporal, numerical, referential, governance, security
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes six invariant kinds with examples: Structural (Entity must have exactly one owner), Temporal (Approval must precede deployment), Numerical (Amount>=0), Referential (EveryClaim -> ValidEvidence), Governance (ProductionChange -> RequiredApproval), Security (Credential must not be exposed).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Invariant ownership and DDD aggregate boundaries
b_rows_sample.statement: In DDD, invariants often belong to an aggregate boundary (Aggregate must guarantee Invariant(AggregateState)); KnowledgeOS should respect that ownership and not arbitrarily redefine an aggregate's invariants. Every invariant should have an OwnerContext (e.g. Invariant_1 -> BC_Voting, Invariant_2 -> BC_Governance). This prevents KnowledgeOS from becoming the owner of every business invariant: instead KnowledgeOS represents, evaluates and traces governed invariants while the domain remains authoritative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HardInvariant versus PolicyConstraint versus AdvisoryCondition
b_rows_sample.statement: First proposes InvariantType in {Hard, Soft, Advisory} (Hard: violation blocks action; Soft: violation requires explicit justification; Advisory: violation produces warning), then self-corrects: strictly speaking a property that CAN be violated is not an invariant in the mathematical sense, so the vocabulary should instead be HardInvariant versus PolicyConstraint versus AdvisoryCondition -- flagged explicitly as 'a useful correction in our formal vocabulary'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Formal invariant I(s)=True over reachable states; inductive invariant reasoning
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a true invariant as I(s)=True for every reachable valid state s, established inductively: base case I(s_0)=True, inductive step I(s) and ValidTransition(s,s') => I(s'), concluding I holds for all reachable states -- noted as powerful for software verification. Applies it to a governed workflow Requested->Reviewed->Approved->Provisioned with the invariant Provisioned=>Approved, requiring it be impossible for a valid transition to produce Provisioned & not-Approved.

b_rows_sample.anchor: State transition system S, T subset SxS, safety requirement
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines S as the set of system states, T subset of SxS as valid transitions, and an invariant I:S->{True,False}; the safety requirement is (s,s') in T and I(s) => I(s'). Connects this directly to event-driven architecture: an event such as ApprovalGranted must follow the domain's event semantics, and KnowledgeOS can reconstruct State_t from Events_<=t -- but an event itself may be invalid, so EventValid(e,K,t) must be checked (an invalid event must not silently establish a valid state). Each state transition should ideally be traceable end to end: Event -> Actor -> Evidence -> Authorization, giving complete decision lineage.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Temporal invariant and temporal validity window
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes ordering invariants as t_approval < t_deployment (violated if t_deployment <= t_approval), and separately temporal validity: a fact can be true but stale -- e.g. SecurityApproved(t_1) is used at decision time t_2, requiring t_2 in ValidityWindow(SecurityApproval). Composes multiple temporal conditions into TemporalSufficiency(d,t) = ApprovalValid(t) and SecurityValid(t) and TestValid(t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Twelve falsification experiments for Step 42 (all PASS)
b_rows_sample.statement: Runs twelve falsification tests against the Step 42 model, all recorded PASS: (1) epistemic requirements pass but authorization fails => Admissible=False; (2) authorization passes but a hard invariant fails => Block; (3) all conditions known except a safety-critical invariant => Block/Unknown per policy, never automatic authorization; (4) a valid transition from a valid state preserves the invariant; (5) a transition that would violate a domain invariant is rejected; (6) a required approval expires before execution => decision becomes inadmissible; (7) evidence used by a decision is revoked => dependency closure identifies affected assurance and decisions; (8) an AI proposes an action violating a governance rule => proposal may be recorded but execution is blocked; (9) new evidence disproves an earlier assumption => existing assurance can be downgraded/revoked; (10) a decision is evaluated without execution => dry-run result has no side effect; (11) an invariant belongs to bounded context BC_A => KnowledgeOS does not silently redefine it from BC_B; (12) a decision passes technical assurance but lacks governance authorization => TechnicallySupported=True, Authorized=False, therefore Execute=False.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 42 verdict and seven closing principles
b_rows_sample.statement: Declares STEP 42 -- PASS and restates seven principles as the step's headline results: (1) Sufficient Knowledge != Valid Decision; (2) Valid Decision != Authorized Action; (3) Unknown safety state must not silently become safe; (4) Hard invariants are non-negotiable; (5) AI proposal != authorized execution; (6) Every consequential decision should have an explicit contract; (7) Evidence invalidation must propagate through decision dependencies.

a_rows_sample.statement: Temptation map (mapped, not resolved) of seven recurring pressures: T-1 Enlarge the aggregate (3 arrivals: 110248->111730->113243); T-2 Add an eighth epistemic state (5 arrivals, three names: AMBIGUOUS -> catuskoti B/N -> 8-way UNKNOWN); T-3 Make Knowledge the Kernel primitive (5 arrivals, both directions); T-4 Make identity derived/relational (2 opposed); T-5 Merge plurality into contradiction (2: 103542 §19 does it, 110525 avoids it); T-6 Use a lens before defining it (Zero Lens, ~17h lag); T-7 Let research become architecture (3: 232146, 111317, 131125, affecting all formal questions). Framed as: 'the corpus is a record of where human and AI reasoning repeatedly want to expand the Kernel' — valuable as future adversarial corpus, dangerous as synthesis input.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The kernel corpus is **not** a subset of the root corpus — they are disjoint sets of files.
a_rows_sample.statement: The brainstorming corpus has three disjoint locations: root (99 docs, the pre-kernel programme: lenses, EKS/PKS baselines, governance, semantic compiler, epistemic core), kernel/ (151 docs, the kernel-discovery corpus), _misc/ (7 docs, earliest material 2026-08-19 to 08-21 including one .png), total 257. The kernel corpus is not a subset of the root corpus — disjoint file sets.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Root corpus spans **2026-08-01 → 08-24**; kernel corpus **08-22 → 08-25**. The overlap is narrow: the root corpus is largely **antecedent** to the kernel work, which makes it the more likely home of original project thinking
a_rows_sample.statement: Chronology by day: 2026-08-01->08-18 (4 docs, scattered origins), 08-19 (12, roles/DDD verification/product architecture), 08-20 (3), 08-21 (9, EKS->KnowledgeOS transition thinking), 08-22 (60, the single heaviest day in the entire programme), 08-23 (8, lens consolidation, handover into kernel/), 08-24 (2, one a cross-folder duplicate). Root corpus (08-01 to 08-24) is largely antecedent to and more likely the home of original project thinking than the kernel corpus, which found only 6 such documents. The 60-documents-in-one-day rate is flagged as capture-driven and warranting its own provenance caution, given the kernel corpus's 8.5% duplicate rate under similar conditions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: formal adjudication already depends on root-corpus documents, which until now had no census at all. That dependency is the strongest argument for this index existing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Five cross-location findings: F-1 the _misc/ folder was never censused and contains a kernel/OS analogy document (20260819-224159, 33KB) predating the entire kernel corpus and not referenced by it, plus the corpus's only image; F-2 two dating conventions coexist at root (31 files YYYYMMDD-HHMM, 66 YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS, one underscore form), not corrected since adding seconds would fabricate false precision; F-3 one confirmed cross-folder duplicate (root 20260824-145631 byte-identical to kernel/20260824-151311, the topological Åström extraction); F-4 the kernel/ handover point is visible at root (20260823-103255/104148/104251/105200) and these are precisely the four documents the adjudication workbook cites as evidence for W:F-CM-1a (the AMBIGUOUS state question) — formal adjudication already depends on previously-uncensused root-corpus documents, the strongest argument for this index existing; F-5 the lens system (39 of 99 root documents) is a root-corpus asset that the kernel corpus uses but does not define, so kernel-corpus conclusions drawn 'through a lens' trace to a document outside that corpus. a_rows_sample.anchor: the entire 257-document corpus this programme reconstructs is priority-7 evidence by the project's oldest stated rule.
a_rows_sample.statement: DOC-1 (20260801-1231 §3) establishes the project's own eight-tier evidence hierarchy: (1) implementation/source code highest, (2) executable tests/enforced invariants very high, (3) persistence/durable records very high, (4) accepted ADRs/governance decisions high, (5) architecture documentation medium-high, (6) C4/diagrams medium, (7) proposals and brainstorming low, (8) historical contextual knowledge lowest — with the rule 'a documented architecture that is not implemented is not current architecture.' DOC-1 §61 also excludes 'future KnowledgeOS kernel concepts' from current EKS, and §44 states historical EKS architecture and the later KnowledgeOS target architecture are not interchangeable — the corpus's oldest document already forbids the retrospective attribution this programme guards against.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Nine redundant copies. **Eight in-folder pairs** plus one cross-folder pair. ... **12 redundant copies. Effective distinct documents: 130.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Duplicate register verified by md5 (nothing deleted): 12 redundant copies against 142 documents, giving 130 effective distinct documents (8.5% duplicate rate). Includes one cross-folder pair (kernel/20260824-151311 = ../20260824-145631) and one lossy (not identical) pair (20260825-130514 critique vs 20260825-130339 scrollback subset). Three additional identical re-saves arrived during Phase A (20260825-101801/145948, 20260824-162039/20260825-150010, 20260825-140251/145918).

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **T-1** | **The over-large aggregate** | ... **rediscovered three times, independently.** The strongest signal in the corpus |
a_rows_sample.statement: Recurring-temptation register T-1..T-7 (each the same idea arriving repeatedly by independent routes, treated as evidence about the corpus not the domain): T-1 the over-large aggregate (rediscovered three times independently: 110248 god-object -> 111730 'too large' -> 113243 don't-freeze-AssertionAggregate — the strongest signal in the corpus); T-2 an eighth epistemic state (five arrivals, three names: AMBIGUOUS -> catuskoti B/N -> 8-way UNKNOWN, recurring after F-CM-1a was deferred); T-3 Knowledge as the Kernel primitive (direct internal contradiction, both sides K3); T-4 identity derived-or-primitive (unreconciled, both K3/K4); T-5 plurality conflated with contradiction (the live F-CM-1a drift, inside the corpus itself); T-6 definition lagging use (Zero Lens used ~17h before being defined); T-7 research->architecture leakage (three documents most at risk of a hypothesis becoming law by being well written: 232146 ADR draft, 111317 'proposed target model', 131125 proposed architecture).

a_rows_sample.anchor: **K4 — Kernel-adversarial (10):** ... **K3 — direct Kernel evidence (29):** ... **39 documents — 30 % of the corpus.** Deduplicated and excluding the scrollback partial: **38**.
a_rows_sample.statement: Phase C candidate subset: 10 K4 (Kernel-adversarial) documents and 29 K3 (direct Kernel evidence) documents, 39 total (30% of corpus), deduplicated and excluding the lossy scrollback partial to 38 documents; the remaining ~89 are K0-K2 (real research, not Kernel evidence). Explicit deliverable boundary: no merit ranking, no synthesis, no contradiction resolution, no promotion of any hypothesis, no Zero pass, nothing written to KnowledgeOS law — T-1..T-7 are registered, not adjudicated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **Ruled by the HPA, 2026-08-25.** ... A reclassification edits **this census** — never a document's name or location.
a_rows_sample.statement: HPA ruling (2026-08-25): classification is metadata, not filesystem — a filename carries identity/chronology/provenance only, never a category code; cluster membership is recorded in the census, not the path (a document may belong to several clusters, a path cannot express that without arbitrary choice); a reclassification edits the census, never a document's name/location; directory names express artifact function, never subject or authority; not one source document was moved. Separately ruled: renaming kernel/ to corpus/ was considered and rejected (the semantic hazard is mitigated by rule, not layout); every directory is kept but the two levels (brainstorming/ coordination vs brainstorming/kernel/ working) must differ rather than mirror, since mirroring identical trees created ambiguity about which to use.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge is **not** merely stored information. It potentially involves: relationship · knower / participant · object / subject · evidence · justification · reasoning · context · conclusion · state · change / evolution · time.
b_rows_sample.statement: Inherited starting model K-M0 (not created here): Knowledge is not merely stored information; it potentially involves relationship, knower/participant, object/subject, evidence, justification, reasoning, context, conclusion, state, change/evolution, time. Phase 1 original thinking: 'Knowledge is the relationship' and 'justified state evolution.' Competing models exist; none assumed correct.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation ──► Recommendation ──► Decision ──► Outcome ──► Assessment ──► KNOWLEDGE ... Knowledge = durable understanding derived from accumulated decisions and outcomes — and explicitly NOT an observation
b_rows_sample.statement: Model K-M1 (change type M2 EXTEND, triggered by 20260801-1231 EKS current architecture baseline, the corpus's oldest document): adds a generative pathway K-M0 lacked entirely — Observation -> Recommendation -> Decision -> Outcome -> Assessment -> KNOWLEDGE, with Knowledge = durable understanding derived from accumulated decisions and outcomes, explicitly NOT an observation. Evidence: '§9.1 Knowledge is durable engineering understanding, differs from raw observation'; 'LCOM4=29 is an observation; acceptance-under-certain-circumstances is knowledge, derived from multiple decisions and outcomes'; '§9.4 these concepts must not collapse into one object'; '§10 the most significant current conceptual chain: Recommendation->Decision->Outcome->Assessment->Effectiveness/Evidence.' Explicitly does NOT mean adding Decision/Outcome/Assessment to the Kernel or KnowledgeAggregate, does not mean the pathway is an invariant, and does not promote anything to architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### C-K1 · Is knowledge *understanding* or *a relationship*? ... *understanding* is **participant-internal and non-inspectable**; a *relationship* is **structural and inspectable**.
b_rows_sample.statement: Contradiction C-K1, recorded not resolved: Position A — knowledge is durable engineering understanding, a cognitive achievement (20260801-1231 §9.1, dated 2026-08-01); Position B — knowledge is the relationship among knower/object/evidence/reasoning/context/conclusion (20260822-0135/0225/0249/0302/1057, five arrivals in one day, 2026-08-22). Both ORIGINAL_PROJECT. Why they conflict: understanding is participant-internal and non-inspectable while a relationship is structural and inspectable — a system can record a relationship but not an understanding, so the two genera imply different answers to 'what is preserved.' A possible reconciliation (understanding as the human-side effect of a recorded relationship) is explicitly NOT accepted since no document proposes it — adopting it would be the extractor's own inference, not the corpus's position. Noted as evolution within the project's own thinking (three weeks apart), not project-versus-import.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the entire 257-document corpus this programme reconstructs is priority-7 evidence by the project's oldest stated rule.
b_rows_sample.statement: DOC-1 (20260801-1231 §3) establishes the project's own eight-tier evidence hierarchy: (1) implementation/source code highest, (2) executable tests/enforced invariants very high, (3) persistence/durable records very high, (4) accepted ADRs/governance decisions high, (5) architecture documentation medium-high, (6) C4/diagrams medium, (7) proposals and brainstorming low, (8) historical contextual knowledge lowest — with the rule 'a documented architecture that is not implemented is not current architecture.' Applied reflexively: the entire 257-document brainstorming corpus this programme reconstructs is itself only priority-7 evidence by the project's own oldest stated rule, meaning the reconstruction's output can only ever be candidate pressure on the formal model, never a competing authority. DOC-1 §61 also excludes 'future KnowledgeOS kernel concepts' from current EKS, and §44 states historical EKS architecture and the later KnowledgeOS target architecture are not interchangeable — the corpus's oldest document already forbids the retrospective attribution this programme guards against.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Session 1 correctly classified this as: **M2 — EXTEND** rather than pretending that the new material was already contained in K-M0. That is exactly the behavior we wanted.
b_rows_sample.statement: Endorses Session 1's K-M0->K-M1 transition as exactly the desired behavior: M2-EXTEND was applied honestly rather than absorbing new material (Observation->Recommendation->Decision->Outcome->Assessment->Knowledge) into the prior K-M0 relational model without acknowledgment. Frames the first real research question this raises: 'Is Knowledge fundamentally a relationship, or an accumulated durable understanding produced through a decision/assessment lifecycle — or are these two descriptions of different dimensions of the same thing?' — more valuable than immediately deciding one model is right.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Research model → potential domain concept → potential architectural implication → formal adjudication → possibly Kernel. We are currently only at the first two levels.
b_rows_sample.statement: Five-stage escalation ladder for research findings: research model -> potential domain concept -> potential architectural implication -> formal adjudication -> possibly Kernel; explicitly notes the current work is only at the first two levels, and praises Session 1 for not concluding 'therefore Decision, Outcome and Assessment belong in the Kernel.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: If Knowledge is durable but knowledge can evolve, what exactly persists? Possibilities include: identity, relationship, proposition, historical record, justification, understanding, knowledge object. But **we should not choose one yet**.
b_rows_sample.statement: Flags that 'durable' (from K-M1's 'durable engineering understanding') is not yet a temporal model, raising a future question: if knowledge is durable but knowledge can evolve, what exactly persists — identity, relationship, proposition, historical record, justification, understanding, or knowledge object — deliberately not choosing one, and noting this may eventually connect to the separate claim that 'knowledge is associated with time', pending further document evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If it materially changes the model: create K-M2 and STOP. If it only confirms existing concepts: record confirmation and continue. If it introduces a contradiction: record it without resolving it and STOP. If it adds no material conceptual information: record M0 and continue.
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues an explicit four-branch continuation protocol for each subsequent document: materially changes the model -> create next K-Mn and STOP; only confirms existing concepts -> record confirmation and continue; introduces a contradiction -> record it without resolving it and STOP; adds no material conceptual information -> record 'M0' (no-change) and continue. Instructs Session 1 to preserve K-M0/K-M1/C-K1 before reading the next document, maintain strict provenance tagging (source-derived / project-original / interpretation / hypothesis / architectural implication), and never promote any research finding into KnowledgeOS law. Also reaffirms the meta-rule that 'the research corpus can discover possibilities without becoming architectural authority' (Research corpus ≠ Current architecture ≠ Constitutional authority).

b_rows_sample.anchor: stop for human attention when the finding **changes the research model** or creates a **significant unresolved contradiction** — not merely because another candidate appears
b_rows_sample.statement: M-2: the extraction stop criterion is narrowed by HPA direction from 'stop whenever a document introduces a potentially Kernel-relevant finding' (superseded, produced excessive stops on a corpus containing many Kernel candidates) to stopping only when a finding changes the research model or creates a significant unresolved contradiction; a new Kernel candidate is simply recorded in the Kernel candidate matrix and extraction continues without interrupt.

b_rows_sample.anchor: All 26 declare `authoritative: false`.
b_rows_sample.statement: 26 of the 256 in-scope documents (P1 root 21/98, _misc 5/6, P2 kernel 0/157) carry YAML front-matter declaring provenance/classification, and all 26 self-declare authoritative:false -- corpus-side confirmation of the standing non-authority discipline, not an externally imposed rule; the convention existed early (declared type values include analysis, architecture-proposal, brainstorm, noise, duplicate, Decision, enum, PRIOR_ABSENCE, POSTERIOR_ABSENCE) and was abandoned before Phase 2 P2-kernel documents, which carry zero such front-matter. front-matter also self-rates timestamp_confidence: medium, corroborating three chronology inversions recorded separately in the dependency-map.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the intersection of the two earliest Phase 1 Kernel member-lists is `{Evidence, Provenance}` only
b_rows_sample.statement: Opens a Kernel candidate matrix (section 10) tabulating candidate/source/why-proposed/counter-evidence/alternative-location/status for: Authority mechanics (RESEARCH_CANDIDATE, contested -- absent from list B), Evidence mechanics (RESEARCH_CANDIDATE, counter-evidence that the kernel must not own typed Assessments), Lifecycle/provenance (RESEARCH_CANDIDATE), KnowledgeProduct (CHALLENGED as too large in its own source document), KnowledgeElement (RESEARCH_CANDIDATE), UNKNOWN-applicability distinction (OPEN, different altitude from v1.1's epistemic UNKNOWN per VC-1), R-CONFLICT as domain invariant (OBSERVED), ChangeSet (RESEARCH_CANDIDATE, implemented so higher evidence class), Rule Port (RESEARCH_CANDIDATE, CONSISTENT with Verification Port), and the Observation/Assessment/Result/Rule-evaluation pipeline (OPEN). No row may reach FORMALLY_ACCEPTED in this ledger -- only the formal architecture can produce that status.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the future KnowledgeOS kernel probably will not be a mathematical engine
b_rows_sample.statement: Concept register KCON-001..025 accumulates, including: KCON-006/007/008/009 (Rule as standing authoritative obligation; Rule≠Decision≠Recommendation≠Permission, ruled; UNKNOWN≠DOES-NOT-APPLY≠EMPTY-SCOPE as a candidate invariant from 20260816-204714, the earliest UNKNOWN non-collapse in the corpus, six days before v1.1; supersession as a Rule component); KCON-010/011/012 (KnowledgeProduct and KnowledgeElement as a third genus for Knowledge -- a product with members -- with KCON-012, aggregate validity = atomically-maintained invariants not relatedness, rated strong on 4 independent arrivals); KCON-015/016/017 (kernel as deterministic runtime; kernel is not database/API/plugin-system/AI-runtime/knowledge-graph, agreeing with v1.1 §17; Artifact existence≠Authority, Record existence≠Authority establishment); KCON-018 (no authority manufacture -- a checker may emit CONFLICT DETECTED, never INDEPENDENCE=TRUE); KCON-019..025 (no established knowledge-kernel research category; trustworthy core = epistemic accountability over time; knowledge-graph-as-kernel evidence Weak; kernel protects the rules, mathematics describes the behavior, anticipating the Phase 2 verdict by ~4 days; kernel as formal semantic operating system with primitives Identity/Evidence/Authority/State/Transition/Provenance/Time/Invariant, a third member list; method rule to discover invariants before choosing a mathematical model).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Same endpoints, **different middle terms and different order**
b_rows_sample.statement: Three unresolved contradictions recorded: C-K1, Knowledge as durable understanding (20260801) vs a product with members (20260819) vs a relationship (20260822 +4), all P1, classified DIFFERENT LEVEL (candidate) since understanding is participant-internal/non-inspectable, relationship is structural/inspectable, and product is an artefact with membership/lifecycle -- but no document proposes the altitude reading, so status stays UNRESOLVED. C-K2, two different Phase-1 knowledge-production chains (Observation->Recommendation->Decision->Outcome->Assessment vs Observation->Evidence->Assessment->Verdict->Decision), classified DIFFERENT CONTEXT (candidate), UNRESOLVED. C-K3, the kernel-determinism contradiction (see S1-F004), UNRESOLVED, reconciliation not adopted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: and make research of only kernel" — **two readings, materially different work**
b_rows_sample.statement: An HPA scope-narrowing instruction on 2026-08-25 is recorded as AMBIGUOUS between (a) folder scope (extract only brainstorming/kernel/, 158 docs, dropping the 98 Phase 1 root documents) and (b) concept scope (keep both locations, extract only Kernel-relevant content); reading (a) would discard the origin of KCON-012 (the corpus's most durable finding) and the three earliest Knowledge definitions, all Phase 1 root. Acted on the intersection of both readings -- Kernel-focused extraction with kernel/ prioritised -- and paused (not discarded) Phase 1 root extraction at 14 of 98 done, awaiting confirmation.
