group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 2 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: We now consolidate the previous experiments. The objective is to identify the smallest set of invariants whose violation would fundamentally change the nature of KnowledgeOS. Provenance+Authority+EpistemicStatus+TemporalValidity+DeterministicVerification+Traceability+Feedback.
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 120's objective: identifying the smallest invariant set whose violation would fundamentally change KnowledgeOS, starting from a seven-part candidate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.1 — What makes an invariant constitutional? A constitutional invariant says: if this property is violated, the system no longer has the intended semantic character. ConstitutionalInvariant≠CodingConvention. 'Use PostgreSQL' is not necessarily constitutional. 'Authoritative knowledge must have id
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines ConstitutionalInvariant≠CodingConvention: a constitutional invariant's violation changes the system's intended semantic character, illustrated by contrasting a technology preference with a provenance requirement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.2 — Invariant K1: Provenance ... Every authoritative knowledge object MUST have provenance. Provenance should answer where did it originate, when, through which process, who/what produced it, from which source material.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K1: every authoritative knowledge object must have provenance answering five questions (origin/when/process/producer/source material).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.3 — Why provenance is constitutional ... Without provenance, Knowledge becomes indistinguishable from GeneratedText. That destroys the ability to answer: Why should I trust this?
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues without provenance, Knowledge becomes indistinguishable from GeneratedText, destroying trust justification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.4 — Experiment K1.1 ... KnowledgeOS contains 'The architecture requires rootless containers.' No source, author, decision, timestamp or provenance exists. Can the system establish that it is authoritative? No. Verdict: K1 VIOLATED
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K1.1: a sourceless/authorless/timestampless architecture statement cannot be established as authoritative; verdict K1 VIOLATED.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.5 — Provenance does not equal source URL ... SourceURL does not tell us WhoApproved or WhenDidItBecomeValid. Source≠CompleteProvenance.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Source≠CompleteProvenance: a URL alone does not establish approval or validity onset.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.6 — Invariant K2: Authority ... Every authoritative governance change MUST have identifiable authority. Decision→Authority.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K2: every authoritative governance change must have identifiable authority (Decision->Authority).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.7 — Why authority is constitutional ... Without authority, Recommendation can silently become Decision. And AgentOutput can silently become OrganizationalTruth. That is unacceptable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues without authority, Recommendation can silently become Decision and AgentOutput can silently become OrganizationalTruth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.8 — Experiment K2.1 ... Agent generates 'Architecture standard changed to X.' No authorized decision exists. Expected: Status=Proposed. Not Status=Authoritative. Verdict: K2 VIOLATION if promoted
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K2.1: an unauthorized agent-declared standard change must remain Status=Proposed; K2 VIOLATION if promoted to Authoritative.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.9 — Authority is not identity ... Actor≠Authority. Credential≠Authority. Role≠Authority unless the governance model explicitly establishes the mapping.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Actor≠Authority, Credential≠Authority, Role≠Authority unless the governance model explicitly maps them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.10 — Invariant K3: Epistemic status ... KnowledgeOS MUST distinguish observed, verified, inferred, proposed and authoritative information. This is perhaps the most important AI-specific invariant.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K3, called perhaps the most important AI-specific invariant: distinguishing observed/verified/inferred/proposed/authoritative information.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.11 — Why epistemic status matters ... 'The service probably owns this database' versus 'The Architecture Board decided that this service owns this database.' The textual similarity may be high. Their epistemic status is radically different.
a_rows_sample.statement: Illustrates why epistemic status matters via a textually-similar but epistemically-radically-different sentence pair.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.12 — Experiment K3.1 ... LLM generates Inference(X). System stores it identically to AuthoritativeDecision(X). Expected: K3 VIOLATION
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K3.1: storing an LLM inference identically to an authoritative decision is K3 VIOLATION.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.13 — Candidate epistemic states ... Observed, Imported, Asserted, Inferred, Proposed, Verified, Approved, Superseded. But we should only implement states that have real semantic value.
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists an eight-value candidate epistemic vocabulary, cautioning only states with real semantic value should be implemented.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.14 — Invariant K4: Temporal validity ... Authoritative knowledge MUST have determinable temporal validity. At minimum Current versus Superseded.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K4: authoritative knowledge must have determinable temporal validity, at minimum Current vs Superseded.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.15 — Why time is constitutional ... An architecture decision from 2024 may not represent the current architecture in 2026. Therefore HistoricalTruth≠CurrentTruth.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues HistoricalTruth≠CurrentTruth, illustrated by a 2024 decision potentially not representing 2026's current architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.16 — Experiment K4.1 ... Two decisions exist: D1 use architecture A, D2 use architecture B. No relationship identifies which supersedes which. Expected: agent cannot safely determine current architecture. Verdict: K4 VIOLATION
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K4.1: two competing, unlinked decisions leave an agent unable to safely determine current architecture; verdict K4 VIOLATION.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.17 — Creation time versus validity ... We must explicitly distinguish CreatedAt from ValidFrom. And potentially ValidUntil.
a_rows_sample.statement: States CreatedAt must be distinguished from ValidFrom (and potentially ValidUntil).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.18 — Experiment K4.2 ... Decision created 2026-08-01 but effective 2026-09-01. If the system only knows created_at, it cannot correctly answer is this decision currently effective. Verdict: K4 PARTIAL
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K4.2: a decision created before its effective date cannot be correctly evaluated by a created_at-only system; verdict K4 PARTIAL.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.19 — Invariant K5: Deterministic verification ... Where a claim is deterministically testable, authoritative assurance MUST be based on reproducible verification evidence. This does not eliminate human judgment. It prevents LLMConfidence from becoming Verification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K5: deterministically testable claims must be assured via reproducible evidence, preventing LLMConfidence from becoming Verification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-SV-01 ... SV1=Provenance ... SV7=Feedback.
b_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 123 (Self-Verification of KnowledgeOS): instead of manually applying the EEP to KnowledgeOS, defines how KnowledgeOS can verify its own constitutional invariants via a first self-verification suite KOS-SV-01 with seven test families mapped to the C1-C7 constitution (SV1 Provenance, SV2 Authority, SV3 EpistemicStatus, SV4 TemporalValidity, SV5 DeterministicAssurance, SV6 Traceability, SV7 Feedback); poses the decisive experiment 'can KnowledgeOS produce machine-verifiable evidence that its own constitutional rules are currently satisfied?' and states that a yes-answer crosses the boundary KnowledgeOS -> Self-Knowledge -> Self-Verification -> Self-Governance, framed as the foundation for KnowledgeOS as a self-assuring engineering system rather than merely a governed knowledge platform.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS → SelfObservation → SelfVerification
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the question from 'can KnowledgeOS govern engineering?' to 'can KnowledgeOS prove that it itself conforms to the principles it imposes on engineering?' — the start of 'self-assuring architecture'; states the self-verification principle that the same Evidence Execution Protocol used on an engineering system (EEP(KnowledgeOS)) must be applicable to KnowledgeOS itself, making the platform both Subject and Verifier.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS → DeterministicChecks → Evidence → Verdict.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the important boundary that self-verification does not mean KnowledgeOS declares itself correct (circular); it must instead run independently reproducible deterministic checks producing evidence and a verdict.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SV-01 Provenance ... SV-07 Feedback
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates KOS-SV as a table mapping SV-01..SV-07 one-to-one onto constitutional invariants C1-C7 (Provenance, Authority, Epistemic status, Temporal validity, Deterministic assurance, Traceability, Feedback).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q1 = {k | k.authoritative=True ∧ k.provenance=null}; |Q1|=0
b_rows_sample.statement: SV-01 Provenance integrity test: query for authoritative knowledge objects with null provenance, expect zero results (else C1=FAIL); further distinguishes Valid(Provenance) from Present(Provenance) — e.g. source="unknown" is technically populated but semantically useless — and defines a five-level SV-01 assurance ladder: L1 field exists, L2 source identifiable, L3 origin process identifiable, L4 provenance immutable/auditable, L5 lineage traversable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Promotion(Proposed→Authoritative) with Authority=null → Reject
b_rows_sample.statement: SV-02 Authority integrity: attempts promotion to authoritative status without valid authority, expecting rejection; introduces the negative-authorization-test principle — a positive test (authorized actors can approve) does not prove unauthorized actors cannot approve, so every governance control needs both a positive test (authorized_actor -> approve -> ALLOW) and a negative test (unauthorized_actor -> approve -> DENY); AuthorizationIntegrity = Positive + Negative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Inference → Authoritative without validation → DENY
b_rows_sample.statement: SV-03 Epistemic integrity: attempting to promote an Inference directly to Authoritative without validation should DENY (worked as SV-03.1: Inference I-42 attempting status=Authoritative expects DENY); specifies the intended promotion pipeline Inference -> Candidate -> Evidence -> Verification -> Governance -> Authority -> Authoritative where no step should silently disappear; also flags the reverse failure mode 'epistemic downgrade' — a verified fact silently becoming an unsupported inference via a serialization/transformation error — requiring any Verified->Inferred transition to be explicit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K1 supersededBy K2; CurrentKnowledge = K2, not K1
b_rows_sample.statement: SV-04 Temporal integrity: after K1 is superseded by K2, querying CurrentKnowledge must return K2 not K1; also requires preserving KnowledgeAt(t) for historical reconstruction (KnowledgeAt(2025) != CurrentKnowledge), worked as SV-04.1: D1 valid from January, D2 supersedes from June, Current(D)=D2 and At(March)=D1, expected PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: V = f(Rule, Input, Version); V1 = V2
b_rows_sample.statement: SV-05 Assurance integrity: a deterministic verification result V=f(Rule,Input,Version) run twice with identical inputs must reproduce (V1=V2; worked as SV-05.1: architecture-check --rule R17 run twice with same versioned inputs, expected PASS both times, else the verification mechanism itself needs investigation); requires a verification record to preserve RuleVersion, InputVersion, CheckerVersion, ExecutionContext for reproducibility.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Action → Decision → Authority; untracked Action A82 → GovernanceFinding
b_rows_sample.statement: SV-06 Traceability integrity: a positive test (Decision D42 -> Action A81) expects TraceExists=True; a negative test (untracked Action A82 with no decision) expects the system to actively recognize the missing relationship and raise a GovernanceFinding — stronger than merely failing a lookup query.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation → Finding → Classification → Governance → Decision → Action → Verification → Updated Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: SV-07 Feedback integrity, 'the most ambitious test': injects a synthetic ObservedDeviation and traces the full closed loop through six sub-tests (SV-07.1 Observation->FindingCreated; SV-07.2 Finding classified->GovernancePathAssigned; SV-07.3 Governance decision created (Finding->Decision); SV-07.4 remediation occurs (Decision->Action); SV-07.5 post-remediation observation matches expected, Finding->Verified->Closed; SV-07.6 knowledge state updates to contain the verified current state), assembled into one complete synthetic self-verification scenario diagram.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SyntheticVerification ≠ UniversalCorrectness
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues synthetic tests matter because historical production events may be incomplete, letting the suite deliberately exercise failure/authorization/correction/closure/feedback paths even without a historical incident (SyntheticEvidence can prove a mechanism exists); but limits this — synthetic verification proves the mechanism works under the tested scenario, not that every real-world scenario works (SyntheticVerification != UniversalCorrectness).

b_rows_sample.anchor: TestID, Rule, Input, Expected, Actual, Evidence, Execution, Version, Timestamp, Verdict
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a self-verification result record schema (TestID/Rule/Input/Expected/Actual/Evidence/Execution/Version/Timestamp/Verdict) that itself becomes an evidence object; notes the recursive property that the SVResult is itself Evidence, so KnowledgeOS -> Evidence -> KnowledgeOS (the system records evidence about its own conformance).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Verifier_A ≠ System_A
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that self-verification must not be the sole evidence of correctness (needs multiple layers: Static + Test + Runtime + IndependentReview) and states the independent-verifier principle: for high-value constitutional controls, the verifier should be a different system/process than the system under test (e.g. CI independently querying the DB for ProvenanceCompleteness) to reduce self-reporting risk.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS API reports 'all authoritative decisions have provenance'; independent SQL check returns 17 records without provenance
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: KnowledgeOS's own API claims full provenance coverage while an independent SQL check finds 17 records without provenance (APIClaim != Reality), verdict 'self-reporting failure' — presented as precisely why independent verification matters.

b_rows_sample.anchor: S1 Self-reported ... S5 Independent governance review
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a five-level constitutional-evidence-tier hierarchy (S1 self-reported, S2 internal deterministic check, S3 external deterministic verifier, S4 runtime observation, S5 independent governance review), explicitly as a hierarchy of evidence strength rather than a requirement that every control reach S5.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SV01 → Finding(C1Violation)
b_rows_sample.statement: States a failed constitutional check should itself create a ConstitutionalFinding (e.g. SV01 -> Finding(C1Violation)) which then flows through the same governance loop, giving a recursive control cycle Constitution -> Check -> Finding -> Governance -> Remediation -> Check.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is not a ratification of Theory v1.3. It is a reviewed, consolidated theory draft / research synthesis ... Theory v1.2 remains frozen ... KNOWLEDGEOS-INFORMATION-TRANSFORMATION-THEORY-CONSOLIDATED-DRAFT-2026-09 ... use it as the adjudication baseline against which the existing Theory v1.2, KR-Z
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes this document explicitly as a research synthesis / candidate theory draft (KNOWLEDGEOS-INFORMATION-TRANSFORMATION-THEORY-CONSOLIDATED-DRAFT-2026-09), not a ratification of Theory v1.3, with Theory v1.2 remaining the frozen baseline; the draft is to be used as an adjudication baseline against which Theory v1.2 and the KR-ZERO, KR-REP-REDUCTION, and KR-BRIDGE-01 artifacts are compared, rather than replacing them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Pattern -> Candidate representation/operator -> Preservation test -> Algebraic-law test. A candidate becomes part of the theory only if it survives explicit experimentation and audit.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the theory's scientific workflow as Pattern -> Candidate representation/operator -> Preservation test -> Algebraic-law test, with a candidate entering the theory only once it survives explicit experimentation and audit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Representation: D -> R ... Transformation: T: D -> R ... Observation: Pi: R -> O, or Q: D -> Y ... Preservation: a preservation requirement specifies what the transformation is required to retain ... C = (Q,Pi,R,...) rather than being an intrinsic property of a representation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines the theory's four fundamental layers that must not be collapsed prematurely: Representation (D->R, how information is encoded), Transformation (T:D->R, what operation changes the representation), Observation (Pi:R->O or Q:D->Y, what aspect we care about), and Preservation (a contract C=(Q,Pi,R,...) specifying what must remain unchanged, rather than an intrinsic representation property).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A representation is adequate only relative to a defined inquiry and preservation requirement. ... Information matters relative to a specified purpose.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the theory's central principle: a representation is adequate only relative to a defined inquiry and preservation requirement, so information should never be described as mattering absolutely but only relative to a specified purpose -- the basis of the contract-relative view of information.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H(Q(D)|T(D))=0 ... H(T(D)|Q(D)) ... H(T(D)) = H(Q(D)) + H(T(D)|Q(D)) ... A representation can therefore be adequate but large, adequate and reduced, inadequate but compact, or highly detailed yet still unsuitable for the required inquiry.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes representation adequacy as H(Q(D)|T(D))=0 and a second quantity H(T(D)|Q(D)) measuring information beyond what the inquiry determines, related by the decomposition H(T(D))=H(Q(D))+H(T(D)|Q(D)) hence H(T(D))>=H(Q(D)); notes these are different dimensions, so a representation can be adequate-but-large, adequate-and-reduced, inadequate-but-compact, or detailed-yet-unsuitable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(x|D1) != Zero(x|D2) ... Question: Does the same information behave differently in different contexts? ... Can Zero(S) be derived from Zero-status of proper subsets? These are different questions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates and formalizes the two separate dimensions of Zero (Dimension A: context dependence, Zero(x|D1)!=Zero(x|D2); Dimension B: determination order, whether Zero(S) can be derived from proper-subset Zero-status) as genuinely different questions whose relationship (whether contextual Zero causes higher-order Zero) remains open.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An invariant describes something that remains unchanged under transformation: Inv_T(D) = Inv_T(T(D)). Zero asks a different question: Pi(T(D)) = Pi(T(E_S(D))). The first asks: What survives transformation? The second asks: What can be eliminated without changing the observation? Invariant != Zero.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a new formal distinction between an invariant (Inv_T(D)=Inv_T(T(D)), asking what survives transformation) and Zero (Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))), asking what can be eliminated without changing the observation), concluding Invariant != Zero even though the two may interact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: E_S(D) removes S. It should not automatically be called a projection. A projection normally carries algebraic properties such as idempotence: P(P(D))=P(D). Unless those properties are established, the safer terminology is: elimination operator rather than projection.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a new terminological discipline: the elimination operator E_S(D) should not automatically be called a 'projection' since projections normally carry algebraic properties such as idempotence (P(P(D))=P(D)) that have not been established for E_S, so the safer term 'elimination operator' should be used instead.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Redundancy Zero: Information can be removed because equivalent information remains. Contextual Zero: Information is Zero in one context but not another. Cancellation Zero: A group becomes Zero because its combined effect cancels, even though individual members are not Zero. These should currently be
a_rows_sample.statement: Names three descriptive Zero-mechanism categories -- Redundancy Zero (removal because equivalent information remains), Contextual Zero (Zero(x|D1)!=Zero(x|D2)), and Cancellation Zero (a group becomes Zero via combined-effect cancellation despite individual members not being Zero) -- explicitly warning these are descriptive categories/hypotheses, not established ontological kinds, and that the ~90% singleton-determined empirical result does not prove all such cases are 'Redundancy Zero'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero was neither necessary nor sufficient for adequacy in the tested regime. The four cells were populated: Z+A, Z+I, NZ+A, NZ+I. ... Zero !=> Adequacy and Adequacy !=> Zero. This is one of the strongest current separations in the theory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the KR-BRIDGE-01 result into a canonical theory statement: Zero was neither necessary nor sufficient for adequacy in the tested regime (all four cells Z+A, Z+I, NZ+A, NZ+I were populated), giving Zero!=>Adequacy and Adequacy!=>Zero as one of the strongest current separations in the theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Within the tested deduplication regime, redundancy behaved as a common structural factor associated with both Zero occurrence and loss of adequacy. ... Observed correlation != established mechanism. ... an AI system must not convert an observed correlation into a knowledge rule without controlling f
a_rows_sample.statement: Draws the general methodological principle 'observed correlation != established mechanism' from the BRIDGE redundancy finding, arguing this is directly relevant to KnowledgeOS because an AI system must not convert an observed correlation into a knowledge rule without controlling for structural factors.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Only one redundancy stratum was genuinely informative for the direct within-transformation association. Other strata were structurally uninformative because adequacy or Zero was saturated. ... The natural imbalance should not simply be 'fixed' after the fact because that would alter the experimental
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the single-informative-stratum limitation of KR-BRIDGE-01 as a general experimental-design lesson: a natural stratum imbalance (other strata structurally uninformative due to saturation) should not be 'fixed' after the fact, since doing so would alter the experimental design rather than genuinely address the limitation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO _|_ KR-REP-REDUCTION. Here _|_ means: analytically separated / not unified by current evidence. This does not mean the two areas can never interact. It means: We currently have no sufficient evidence to define a single common reduction operator or common algebra containing both.
a_rows_sample.statement: Clarifies precisely what the KR-ZERO _|_ KR-REP-REDUCTION governance conclusion means: analytically separated / not unified by current evidence, i.e. there is currently no sufficient evidence to define a single common reduction operator or algebra containing both -- explicitly not a claim that the two areas can never interact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: T_R(D) = Inv_T(D) oplus Delta_R(D) oplus Rem_T(D). This should not be retained as a universal law. There is insufficient evidence for the direct-sum structure, the algebraic carrier, or the semantics of each component. A safer representation is a tuple: T_R(D) |-> (Inv_T(D), Delta_T(D), Rem_T(D)). E
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly rejects an earlier proposed universal decomposition T_R(D)=Inv_T(D) oplus Delta_R(D) oplus Rem_T(D) as a universal law, citing insufficient evidence for the direct-sum structure, algebraic carrier, or component semantics, replacing it with a safer tuple T_R(D) |-> (Inv_T(D), Delta_T(D), Rem_T(D)) whose entries remain candidate observables rather than established algebraic components.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Delta_R(D) = D - R should not be assumed. The difference between source and representation may require a typed operator: Delta_T(D,R). The representation may not even live in the same algebraic space as the source. Difference requires a defined type and operation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects assuming the difference between source and representation is simple subtraction (Delta_R(D)=D-R), requiring instead a typed operator Delta_T(D,R) since the representation may not live in the same algebraic space as the source, establishing the general principle that difference requires a defined type and operation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Vedic transformations provide examples of systematic representation changes that can be formalized and empirically tested. ... Historical pattern -> formal candidate -> controlled experiment -> audit -> possible theory. Historical interpretation and mathematical validation therefore remain separate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates Vedic Mathematics's role as a generator of candidate transformation patterns (never proof of the theory), formalizing the research architecture Historical pattern -> formal candidate -> controlled experiment -> audit -> possible theory, keeping historical interpretation and mathematical validation strictly separate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: encode_B(K) = (B, delta_K) ... We do not assume that K = B - delta_K. ... Q(decode(B,delta_K)) === Q(K). The base-selection rule must be predeclared. Otherwise dynamic optimization can overfit the test data. ... f(a otimes_A b) = f(a) otimes_B f(b). If this fails, define a homomorphic defect ... P(x
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates four candidate Vedic-inspired operators into formal notation: reference-relative encoding encode_B(K)=(B,delta_K) with predeclared base-selection to avoid overfitting and correctness condition Q(decode(B,delta_K))=Q(K); structure-preserving composition f(a otimes_A b)=f(a) otimes_B f(b), with a 'homomorphic defect' quantity defined when it fails rather than assuming structure preservation; guarded specialized rewrite operators P(x)=>O_special(x)===O_general(x); and local transformation T(D)=Reconstruct(T(W_1(D)),...,T(W_n(D))) testing whether no information crosses locality boundaries.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim + not-Claim = 0 [rejected as a simplistic rule]. Cancellation is valid only when an appropriate inverse or observational cancellation structure has been demonstrated. ... Cancellation is a specialized emergent property, not a universal primitive.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms that cancellation must remain conservative: the simplistic rule Claim+notClaim=0 is rejected, cancellation being valid only once an appropriate inverse or observational cancellation structure is demonstrated, establishing cancellation as a specialized emergent property rather than a universal primitive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An attractive interpretation must yield to an audit finding. ... the representation-reduction audit found: the bootstrap confidence interval procedure was invalid for the sparse conditional-entropy estimator; the rank invertibility claim failed because of tie handling. Those failures did not invalid
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports that the representation-reduction audit found two specific problems -- the bootstrap confidence-interval procedure was invalid for the sparse conditional-entropy estimator, and the rank-invertibility claim failed due to tie handling (matching the desc=(n+1)-asc falsification) -- neither of which invalidated the main structural conclusions (which rested on exact violation counts and train/test agreement), but both of which forced withdrawal of the affected claims, establishing the principle that an attractive interpretation must yield to an audit finding, essential if KnowledgeOS is to govern AI-generated knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Ascending and descending rank are merely invertible recodings.' The audit showed that deterministic tie-breaking makes this claim false in the implemented experiment.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally records the rejection of the claim that ascending and descending rank encodings are merely invertible recodings, since the audit showed deterministic tie-breaking makes this false in the implemented experiment -- the theory-level record of the desc=(n+1)-asc falsification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: we should distinguish definitions, mathematical propositions/theorems, empirical findings, conjectures, and research heuristics. In particular, some equations that appeared earlier as if they were empirical results are actually mathematical consequences of the definitions under explicit assumptions.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the governing improvement of this pass over the prior consolidated draft: strictly distinguish definitions, proven mathematical propositions/theorems, empirical findings, conjectures, and research heuristics, since some equations previously presented as empirical results are actually mathematical consequences of the definitions under explicit assumptions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Theorem 1 -- Functional recoverability criterion. Let D be a random variable, R=T(D), and Q=Q(D) ... H(Q|R)=0 if and only if Q is almost surely a deterministic function of R. Proof: H(Q|R) = sum_r P(R=r) H(Q|R=r) ... Q=g(R) almost surely.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proves Theorem 1 (functional recoverability criterion): for discrete finite-valued random variables, H(Q|R)=0 if and only if Q is almost surely a deterministic function of R, with a complete proof via the decomposition H(Q|R)=sum_r P(R=r)H(Q|R=r) and the observation that each conditional distribution with positive probability must be degenerate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: N_viol=0 => empirical adequacy on the tested sample. This does not imply population adequacy. That distinction is fundamental.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the finite-sample operational adequacy criterion: a deterministic empirical decoder exists iff every representation value corresponds to at most one inquiry value in the test set (equivalently N_viol=0), which implies only empirical adequacy on the tested sample, never population adequacy.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H(R) = H(Q) + H(R|Q) - H(Q|R) ... If the representation is adequate, H(Q|R)=0. Therefore H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q). Hence H(R)>=H(Q). Equality occurs iff H(R|Q)=0. Therefore H(R)=H(Q) iff H(Q|R)=0 and H(R|Q)=0.
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives the general chain-rule identity H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q)-H(Q|R), specializing under adequacy (H(Q|R)=0) to H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q), hence H(R)>=H(Q) with equality iff H(R|Q)=0 as well -- the mathematically precise form of the earlier informal 'no representational excess' idea.

b_rows_sample.anchor: NoExcess(R,Q) iff H(R|Q)=0. ... Adequacy: H(Q|R)=0. No excess: H(R|Q)=0. These are logically independent conditions in general. ... Adequate with excess: H(Q|R)=0, H(R|Q)>0. Inadequate: H(Q|R)>0. ... Sufficiency != Minimality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines NoExcess(R,Q) iff H(R|Q)=0 and formally establishes that adequacy (H(Q|R)=0) and no-excess (H(R|Q)=0) are logically independent conditions in general -- a representation can be 'adequate with excess' (H(Q|R)=0 but H(R|Q)>0) or inadequate (H(Q|R)>0) -- yielding the new distinction Sufficiency != Minimality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R1 ~_Q R2 when Q(decode(R1)) = Q(decode(R2)). However, the theory should not call this Q-isomorphism. ... equality of inquiry outcomes does not establish structural isomorphism. Q-equivalent != Q-isomorphic. The latter requires additional structural conditions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Q-equivalence between representations (R1 ~_Q R2 iff Q(decode(R1))=Q(decode(R2))) and explicitly distinguishes it from 'Q-isomorphism', since equality of inquiry outcomes does not establish structural isomorphism, which requires additional structural conditions not implied by Q-equivalence alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Theorem 2 -- Conditional entropy monotonicity under deterministic reduction. Let Q -> R_n -> R_{n-1} form a Markov chain, with R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n) deterministically. Then H(Q|R_{n-1}) >= H(Q|R_n). Proof: data-processing inequality gives I(Q;R_{n-1}) <= I(Q;R_n) ... cancel H(Q) ... QED.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proves Theorem 2 (conditional entropy monotonicity under deterministic reduction): for a Markov chain Q->R_n->R_{n-1} with R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n) deterministic, H(Q|R_{n-1})>=H(Q|R_n), derived rigorously from the data-processing inequality I(Q;R_{n-1})<=I(Q;R_n) via I(Q;R)=H(Q)-H(Q|R); the corollary chain H(Q|R5)<=H(Q|R4)<=H(Q|R3)<=H(Q|R2) shows information sufficiency cannot spontaneously reappear once lost.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_n = 1{H(Q|R_n)=0}. Then, under exact population adequacy and deterministic degradation: A_n=1 => A_{n-1}<=A_n. Equivalently, adequacy can transition 1->0 but cannot transition 0->1. Thus a preservation boundary can be defined as the first transition: R_k adequate, R_{k-1} inadequate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the preservation boundary using an adequacy indicator A_n=1{H(Q|R_n)=0}: under deterministic sequential degradation, adequacy can only transition from 1 to 0, never from 0 to 1, so the preservation boundary is precisely defined as the first transition point R_k adequate, R_{k-1} inadequate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: min_{T in T} C(T(D)) subject to H(Q(D)|T(D))=0. ... C(R) = w1 bytes(R) + w2 latency(R) + w3 storage(R) + ... but the weights must be business-defined. Reduction is an optimization problem subject to preservation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes reduction as a constrained optimization problem: minimize a business-defined representation-cost functional C(T(D)) (e.g. weighted bytes, latency, storage) subject to the adequacy constraint H(Q(D)|T(D))=0, explicitly marked as a candidate mathematical formulation, not yet an established KnowledgeOS law.

b_rows_sample.anchor: desc != (n+1)-asc [for D with ties, e.g. D=[23000,46000,46000]] ... The implemented ascending/descending rank transformations were not proven to be simple invertible recodings. ... A representational convention can carry operational consequences. But the pure 'decoder-only effect' attribution was to
b_rows_sample.statement: Records the formal audit correction that the ascending/descending rank transformations were not proven to be simple invertible recodings, since deterministic tie-breaking on data with repeated values (e.g. D=[23000,46000,46000]) makes desc != (n+1)-asc; the broader lesson survives (a representational convention can carry operational consequences) but the pure 'decoder-only effect' attribution was too strong and had to be corrected after audit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: f(a otimes_A b) = f(a) otimes_B f(b) [homomorphism]. If this equality fails, define the defect: Delta_f(a,b) = f(a otimes_A b) - f(a) otimes_B f(b) only when an appropriate difference operation exists. Otherwise define a typed defect relation: Def_f(a,b). The theory must not assume homomorphism. It
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the homomorphic-defect quantity for structure-preserving transformations: when f(a otimes_A b) != f(a) otimes_B f(b), define Delta_f(a,b)=f(a otimes_A b) - f(a) otimes_B f(b) if a difference operation exists in the target space, otherwise a typed defect relation Def_f(a,b) when it does not, establishing that homomorphism must be measured, never assumed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A specific decoder is: O: R -> Y. Realization requires: O(R) = Q(D). A representation can therefore contain sufficient information while a particular decoder fails to recover it. Adequacy != Realization. ... Decoder theorem: if Q is recoverable from R, then there exists an ideal decoder g* such that
b_rows_sample.statement: Proves the decoder theorem: if Q is recoverable from R there exists an ideal decoder g* with g*(R)=Q, but an arbitrary decoder O need not equal g*, so H(Q|R)=0 does not imply O(R)=Q without additional conditions on O -- formally separating representation sufficiency (adequacy) from implementation realization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q(D1)=Q(D2) ... This relation IS an equivalence relation because equality is reflexive, symmetric, transitive. Therefore Q partitions the source space: D/~_Q. A representation T is adequate for Q precisely when it distinguishes enough classes to recover the Q-class. Q(D1)!=Q(D2) => T(D1)!=T(D2).
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that the relation D1~D2 iff Q(D1)=Q(D2) is a genuine equivalence relation (equality being reflexive, symmetric, transitive), partitioning the source space into D/~_Q classes, with T adequate for Q precisely when it distinguishes enough classes to recover the Q-class, equivalently Q(D1)!=Q(D2) implies T(D1)!=T(D2).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Theorem 3. For deterministic T, the following are equivalent on a domain D0: 1. H(Q|T(D))=0. 2. There exists g such that Q=g.T. 3. Whenever T(D1)=T(D2), then Q(D1)=Q(D2). Proof: 1<=>2 follows from Theorem 1. 2=>3 ... 3=>2: define g(r)=Q(D) for any D with T(D)=r; well-defined by condition 3. QED. Thi
b_rows_sample.statement: Proves Theorem 3, establishing the equivalence, for deterministic T, of (1) H(Q|T(D))=0, (2) existence of g with Q=g.T, and (3) T(D1)=T(D2) implies Q(D1)=Q(D2), with a complete proof; judged extremely useful for KnowledgeOS because it converts semantic preservation into a concrete fiber-separation condition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T^{-1}(r) = {D: T(D)=r}. Adequacy means: Q is constant on every fiber of T. ... Representation reduction is safe iff every representation fiber is Q-homogeneous.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the fiber T^{-1}(r)={D:T(D)=r} of a representation and characterizes adequacy as Q being constant on every fiber of T, giving the clean formulation that representation reduction is safe if and only if every representation fiber is Q-homogeneous -- judged a stronger conceptual formulation than merely 'information was preserved'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A reduction transformation T1 -> T2 crosses a preservation boundary precisely when T2 creates at least one Q-heterogeneous fiber: exists D1,D2: T2(D1)=T2(D2) but Q(D1)!=Q(D2). Boundary iff first occurrence of a Q-heterogeneous representation fiber. This gives a very concrete mathematical interpretat
b_rows_sample.statement: Characterizes a preservation-boundary crossing as the first occurrence of a Q-heterogeneous representation fiber (T2 collapsing two source states D1,D2 with T2(D1)=T2(D2) but Q(D1)!=Q(D2)), giving a concrete mathematical interpretation of the experimental N_viol statistic as counting such fiber collisions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Hhat(Q|R)=0 does not establish H(Q|R)=0 in the population. It establishes only a sample-level result under the estimator and observed support. Hhat=0 !=> H=0 without additional statistical assumptions. This distinction is mandatory.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates the population-vs-sample distinction as a formal requirement: the empirical estimator result Hhat(Q|R)=0 establishes only a sample-level result under the given estimator and observed support, never the population-level H(Q|R)=0, without additional statistical assumptions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the representation-reduction audit discovered that a proposed bootstrap confidence interval for conditional entropy was invalid because sparse resampling changed the support structure. ... define the estimator, establish its assumptions, evaluate finite-sample bias, use appropriate corrections, vali
b_rows_sample.statement: Details the specific audit finding that a proposed bootstrap confidence interval for conditional entropy was invalid because sparse resampling changed the support structure, listing six required remedial steps (define estimator, establish assumptions, evaluate finite-sample bias, apply corrections, validate bootstrap conditions, distinguish empirical from population support), while noting the main preservation conclusion survived since it rested on exact violation counts and train/test agreement rather than the invalid confidence interval.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Level 1 -- Observed: Hhat(Q|R) or N_viol. Level 2 -- Experimental conclusion: within the tested sample and design, preservation was/was not observed. Level 3 -- Statistical generalization: requires sampling assumptions, estimator validity, uncertainty quantification, population model. Level 4 -- Mat
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a formal four-level statistical-generalization hierarchy that must never be collapsed: Level 1 Observed (Hhat(Q|R) or N_viol), Level 2 Experimental conclusion (within the tested sample/design), Level 3 Statistical generalization (requiring sampling assumptions, estimator validity, uncertainty quantification, population model), Level 4 Mathematical theorem (requiring proof).

This is a candidate meta-structure. It is not yet an algebra.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a seven-element candidate meta-structure K=(D,R,T,Q,Pi,E,O) -- source domain, representation space, transformations, inquiries, preservation observations/contracts, elimination operators, and realization/decoder operators -- explicitly marked as only a candidate meta-structure, distinct from the five-element K=(R,T,O,P,E) proposed in the prior consolidated draft.

a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes this document explicitly as a research synthesis / candidate theory draft (KNOWLEDGEOS-INFORMATION-TRANSFORMATION-THEORY-CONSOLIDATED-DRAFT-2026-09), not a ratification of Theory v1.3, with Theory v1.2 remaining the frozen baseline; the draft is to be used as an adjudication baseline against which Theory v1.2 and the KR-ZERO, KR-REP-REDUCTION, and KR-BRIDGE-01 artifacts are compared, rather than replacing them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Pattern -> Candidate representation/operator -> Preservation test -> Algebraic-law test. A candidate becomes part of the theory only if it survives explicit experimentation and audit.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the theory's scientific workflow as Pattern -> Candidate representation/operator -> Preservation test -> Algebraic-law test, with a candidate entering the theory only once it survives explicit experimentation and audit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Representation: D -> R ... Transformation: T: D -> R ... Observation: Pi: R -> O, or Q: D -> Y ... Preservation: a preservation requirement specifies what the transformation is required to retain ... C = (Q,Pi,R,...) rather than being an intrinsic property of a representation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines the theory's four fundamental layers that must not be collapsed prematurely: Representation (D->R, how information is encoded), Transformation (T:D->R, what operation changes the representation), Observation (Pi:R->O or Q:D->Y, what aspect we care about), and Preservation (a contract C=(Q,Pi,R,...) specifying what must remain unchanged, rather than an intrinsic representation property).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A representation is adequate only relative to a defined inquiry and preservation requirement. ... Information matters relative to a specified purpose.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the theory's central principle: a representation is adequate only relative to a defined inquiry and preservation requirement, so information should never be described as mattering absolutely but only relative to a specified purpose -- the basis of the contract-relative view of information.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H(Q(D)|T(D))=0 ... H(T(D)|Q(D)) ... H(T(D)) = H(Q(D)) + H(T(D)|Q(D)) ... A representation can therefore be adequate but large, adequate and reduced, inadequate but compact, or highly detailed yet still unsuitable for the required inquiry.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes representation adequacy as H(Q(D)|T(D))=0 and a second quantity H(T(D)|Q(D)) measuring information beyond what the inquiry determines, related by the decomposition H(T(D))=H(Q(D))+H(T(D)|Q(D)) hence H(T(D))>=H(Q(D)); notes these are different dimensions, so a representation can be adequate-but-large, adequate-and-reduced, inadequate-but-compact, or detailed-yet-unsuitable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(x|D1) != Zero(x|D2) ... Question: Does the same information behave differently in different contexts? ... Can Zero(S) be derived from Zero-status of proper subsets? These are different questions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates and formalizes the two separate dimensions of Zero (Dimension A: context dependence, Zero(x|D1)!=Zero(x|D2); Dimension B: determination order, whether Zero(S) can be derived from proper-subset Zero-status) as genuinely different questions whose relationship (whether contextual Zero causes higher-order Zero) remains open.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An invariant describes something that remains unchanged under transformation: Inv_T(D) = Inv_T(T(D)). Zero asks a different question: Pi(T(D)) = Pi(T(E_S(D))). The first asks: What survives transformation? The second asks: What can be eliminated without changing the observation? Invariant != Zero.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a new formal distinction between an invariant (Inv_T(D)=Inv_T(T(D)), asking what survives transformation) and Zero (Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))), asking what can be eliminated without changing the observation), concluding Invariant != Zero even though the two may interact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: E_S(D) removes S. It should not automatically be called a projection. A projection normally carries algebraic properties such as idempotence: P(P(D))=P(D). Unless those properties are established, the safer terminology is: elimination operator rather than projection.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a new terminological discipline: the elimination operator E_S(D) should not automatically be called a 'projection' since projections normally carry algebraic properties such as idempotence (P(P(D))=P(D)) that have not been established for E_S, so the safer term 'elimination operator' should be used instead.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Redundancy Zero: Information can be removed because equivalent information remains. Contextual Zero: Information is Zero in one context but not another. Cancellation Zero: A group becomes Zero because its combined effect cancels, even though individual members are not Zero. These should currently be
a_rows_sample.statement: Names three descriptive Zero-mechanism categories -- Redundancy Zero (removal because equivalent information remains), Contextual Zero (Zero(x|D1)!=Zero(x|D2)), and Cancellation Zero (a group becomes Zero via combined-effect cancellation despite individual members not being Zero) -- explicitly warning these are descriptive categories/hypotheses, not established ontological kinds, and that the ~90% singleton-determined empirical result does not prove all such cases are 'Redundancy Zero'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero was neither necessary nor sufficient for adequacy in the tested regime. The four cells were populated: Z+A, Z+I, NZ+A, NZ+I. ... Zero !=> Adequacy and Adequacy !=> Zero. This is one of the strongest current separations in the theory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the KR-BRIDGE-01 result into a canonical theory statement: Zero was neither necessary nor sufficient for adequacy in the tested regime (all four cells Z+A, Z+I, NZ+A, NZ+I were populated), giving Zero!=>Adequacy and Adequacy!=>Zero as one of the strongest current separations in the theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Within the tested deduplication regime, redundancy behaved as a common structural factor associated with both Zero occurrence and loss of adequacy. ... Observed correlation != established mechanism. ... an AI system must not convert an observed correlation into a knowledge rule without controlling f
a_rows_sample.statement: Draws the general methodological principle 'observed correlation != established mechanism' from the BRIDGE redundancy finding, arguing this is directly relevant to KnowledgeOS because an AI system must not convert an observed correlation into a knowledge rule without controlling for structural factors.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Only one redundancy stratum was genuinely informative for the direct within-transformation association. Other strata were structurally uninformative because adequacy or Zero was saturated. ... The natural imbalance should not simply be 'fixed' after the fact because that would alter the experimental
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the single-informative-stratum limitation of KR-BRIDGE-01 as a general experimental-design lesson: a natural stratum imbalance (other strata structurally uninformative due to saturation) should not be 'fixed' after the fact, since doing so would alter the experimental design rather than genuinely address the limitation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO _|_ KR-REP-REDUCTION. Here _|_ means: analytically separated / not unified by current evidence. This does not mean the two areas can never interact. It means: We currently have no sufficient evidence to define a single common reduction operator or common algebra containing both.
a_rows_sample.statement: Clarifies precisely what the KR-ZERO _|_ KR-REP-REDUCTION governance conclusion means: analytically separated / not unified by current evidence, i.e. there is currently no sufficient evidence to define a single common reduction operator or algebra containing both -- explicitly not a claim that the two areas can never interact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: T_R(D) = Inv_T(D) oplus Delta_R(D) oplus Rem_T(D). This should not be retained as a universal law. There is insufficient evidence for the direct-sum structure, the algebraic carrier, or the semantics of each component. A safer representation is a tuple: T_R(D) |-> (Inv_T(D), Delta_T(D), Rem_T(D)). E
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly rejects an earlier proposed universal decomposition T_R(D)=Inv_T(D) oplus Delta_R(D) oplus Rem_T(D) as a universal law, citing insufficient evidence for the direct-sum structure, algebraic carrier, or component semantics, replacing it with a safer tuple T_R(D) |-> (Inv_T(D), Delta_T(D), Rem_T(D)) whose entries remain candidate observables rather than established algebraic components.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Delta_R(D) = D - R should not be assumed. The difference between source and representation may require a typed operator: Delta_T(D,R). The representation may not even live in the same algebraic space as the source. Difference requires a defined type and operation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects assuming the difference between source and representation is simple subtraction (Delta_R(D)=D-R), requiring instead a typed operator Delta_T(D,R) since the representation may not live in the same algebraic space as the source, establishing the general principle that difference requires a defined type and operation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Vedic transformations provide examples of systematic representation changes that can be formalized and empirically tested. ... Historical pattern -> formal candidate -> controlled experiment -> audit -> possible theory. Historical interpretation and mathematical validation therefore remain separate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates Vedic Mathematics's role as a generator of candidate transformation patterns (never proof of the theory), formalizing the research architecture Historical pattern -> formal candidate -> controlled experiment -> audit -> possible theory, keeping historical interpretation and mathematical validation strictly separate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: encode_B(K) = (B, delta_K) ... We do not assume that K = B - delta_K. ... Q(decode(B,delta_K)) === Q(K). The base-selection rule must be predeclared. Otherwise dynamic optimization can overfit the test data. ... f(a otimes_A b) = f(a) otimes_B f(b). If this fails, define a homomorphic defect ... P(x
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates four candidate Vedic-inspired operators into formal notation: reference-relative encoding encode_B(K)=(B,delta_K) with predeclared base-selection to avoid overfitting and correctness condition Q(decode(B,delta_K))=Q(K); structure-preserving composition f(a otimes_A b)=f(a) otimes_B f(b), with a 'homomorphic defect' quantity defined when it fails rather than assuming structure preservation; guarded specialized rewrite operators P(x)=>O_special(x)===O_general(x); and local transformation T(D)=Reconstruct(T(W_1(D)),...,T(W_n(D))) testing whether no information crosses locality boundaries.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim + not-Claim = 0 [rejected as a simplistic rule]. Cancellation is valid only when an appropriate inverse or observational cancellation structure has been demonstrated. ... Cancellation is a specialized emergent property, not a universal primitive.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms that cancellation must remain conservative: the simplistic rule Claim+notClaim=0 is rejected, cancellation being valid only once an appropriate inverse or observational cancellation structure is demonstrated, establishing cancellation as a specialized emergent property rather than a universal primitive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An attractive interpretation must yield to an audit finding. ... the representation-reduction audit found: the bootstrap confidence interval procedure was invalid for the sparse conditional-entropy estimator; the rank invertibility claim failed because of tie handling. Those failures did not invalid
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports that the representation-reduction audit found two specific problems -- the bootstrap confidence-interval procedure was invalid for the sparse conditional-entropy estimator, and the rank-invertibility claim failed due to tie handling (matching the desc=(n+1)-asc falsification) -- neither of which invalidated the main structural conclusions (which rested on exact violation counts and train/test agreement), but both of which forced withdrawal of the affected claims, establishing the principle that an attractive interpretation must yield to an audit finding, essential if KnowledgeOS is to govern AI-generated knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Ascending and descending rank are merely invertible recodings.' The audit showed that deterministic tie-breaking makes this claim false in the implemented experiment.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally records the rejection of the claim that ascending and descending rank encodings are merely invertible recodings, since the audit showed deterministic tie-breaking makes this false in the implemented experiment -- the theory-level record of the desc=(n+1)-asc falsification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Object = Reference + Deviation ... The base does not have to be numeric ... Base = Reference Model
b_rows_sample.statement: Abstracts the Vedic 'base and deviation' multiplication method (e.g. computing 95x92 via deviations from 100) into Object=Reference+Deviation and a typed Represent(D|K0)=(K0,Delta_{K0}(D),R_{K0}(D)), generalizing the base K0 beyond numeric to textual/ontological/temporal/inquiry-relative/organizational reference models, e.g. a reference architecture document as K0 against which a new document's deviation is computed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Vertically and Crosswise ... Interaction = Direct Relations + Cross Relations ... an information relation algebra.
b_rows_sample.statement: Abstracts the Vedic 'vertically and crosswise' multiplication procedure (computing (a+b)(c+d) as ac+ad+bc+bd) into a candidate Cross(X,Y) relational-interaction operation over the dimensions of two information objects, illustrated with a worked example (Document A's Authentication/Tenant/User dimensions crossed with Document B's Keycloak/Realm/Role dimensions) revealing relevant crosswise relations (Tenant<->Realm, User<->Role, Authentication<->Keycloak) among mostly-irrelevant combinations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Alternative Elimination and Retention ... D -> (E,R) ... E = {x in D : Zero_{T,Pi}(x)}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the Vedic sutra 'By Alternative Elimination and Retention' as almost directly usable: abstracted as D->(E,R) with E the eliminated candidates under the declared method and R the retained remainder, directly combined with the KR-ZERO-ALGEBRA Zero definition as E={x in D: Zero_{T,Pi}(x)}, with every elimination assigned a witness x->W_x.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K = (B, Delta, I, R, Gamma) ... Observe, Base, Diff, Cross, Transform, Eliminate, Retain, Verify, Compose
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a Candidate Transformation Algebra with carrier K=(B,Delta,I,R,Gamma) (base/reference, differences, invariants, remainder, boundary/context constraints) and nine candidate operations (Observe, Base, Diff, Cross, Transform, Eliminate, Retain, Verify, Compose), explicitly deferring the question of whether these satisfy identity, composition, associativity, idempotence, commutativity, conservation, remainder stability, or Zero compositionality to future experiments rather than assuming any of them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can the structural principles underlying multiple Vedic transformations be abstracted into a general algebra of information transformation? ... take one very small corpus and implement perhaps only five operations: Base, Diff, Cross, Eliminate, Remainder.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes reframing the research question from 'can Vedic Mathematics solve text?' to whether structural principles across multiple Vedic sutras generalize into an information-transformation algebra, and proposes a minimal new research lane implementing five base operations (Base, Diff, Cross, Eliminate, Remainder) on a small corpus before asking what algebraic structure their composition forms.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Tiryagbhyam: Good research hypothesis; Vinculum: Good representation hypothesis; Nikhilam: Strong candidate representation pattern; Sub-sutras: Strong architectural hypothesis; Moving-window methods: Plausible computational strategy; Sunya/Zero: Empirically grounded, but not yet algebraic. Vedic mat
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates principles worth investigating from structures already justified across six Vedic principles (Tiryagbhyam, Vinculum, Nikhilam, sub-sutras, moving-window methods, Sunya/Zero), each assigned a status from 'good research hypothesis' to 'empirically grounded but not yet algebraic', on the general ground that Vedic mathematics demonstrates computational techniques but does not by itself demonstrate that the corresponding abstractions form the required algebraic structures for knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: An operator may be lifted across representations when a structure-preserving mapping exists. ... f(a otimes_A b) = f(a) otimes_B f(b). That is a homomorphism condition, not merely an analogy. Abstraction is valid when the relevant structure is preserved. But the structure being preserved must be ide
b_rows_sample.statement: Reformulates the Tiryagbhyam ('vertically and crosswise') analogy from the overly strong claim 'the same operator works on everything' into a homomorphism condition f(a otimes_A b)=f(a) otimes_B f(b) for a mapping f:A->B, yielding the principle that abstraction is valid when the relevant structure is preserved, while insisting that structure must be identified experimentally or formally rather than assuming semantic knowledge has one universal algebraic structure (rejecting a universal 'knowledge tensor product').

b_rows_sample.anchor: 29 = 3-bar-1 = 30-1. ... X = B - delta ... K = (B, delta_K) rather than necessarily K = B - delta_K. The tuple form is safer because subtraction may not even exist in the eventual carrier. ... encode_B(K) = (B, delta_K). Then ask experimentally: Is the representation lossless? Is it smaller? Can the
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the Vinculum (signed/complement) device from 'negative knowledge' into a reference-plus-deviation representation, preferring the safer tuple form K=(B,delta_K) over the subtractive K=B-delta_K since subtraction may not exist in the eventual carrier, defining a representation constructor encode_B(K)=(B,delta_K) and posing five experimental questions (losslessness, size, observable recoverability, relation preservation, local composability of delta) to connect this directly to the existing representation-reduction research without assuming the answer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'allows automatic cancellation when resolving contradictory or updating knowledge states' is an attractive hypothesis, but it is not yet established. ... claim + counterclaim -> conflict rather than claim + counterclaim = 0. ... resolve(K1,K2) -> K'... only specialize it to cancellation if experimen
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that the hypothesis of automatic cancellation for resolving contradictory or updating knowledge states is not yet established, since knowledge more plausibly behaves as claim+counterclaim->conflict rather than claim+counterclaim=0 (an additive-inverse structure); proposes the conservative abstraction resolve(K1,K2)->K', to be specialized to cancellation only once experiments demonstrate an appropriate inverse/identity structure, explicitly noting that the existing Transformation-relative Zero result does not establish Zero as an algebraic cancellation element.

b_rows_sample.anchor: General operator + recognized structural condition => specialized operator. O_general(x), and when predicate P(x) holds, P(x) => O_special(x), with a required correctness condition O_special(x) === O_general(x) with respect to the relevant observable. Otherwise the 'sub-sutra' is merely an optimizat
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the sub-sutra idea as a specialization rule: given a general operator O_general(x) and a recognized structural condition P(x), a specialized operator O_special(x) is admissible only if it satisfies the correctness condition O_special(x) equivalent-to O_general(x) with respect to the relevant observable, since without that clause the specialization is merely an optimization that happens to work rather than a certified rewrite rule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: (B-delta_1) otimes (B-delta_2) = B otimes (B-delta_1-delta_2) oplus (delta_1 otimes delta_2), is mathematically meaningful for certain algebraic structures, but should not yet be declared as a Knowledge Algebra law. Level 1 -- Representation. Level 2 -- Transformation. Level 3 -- Closure: determine
b_rows_sample.statement: Declines to promote the Nikhilam-inspired composition formula (B-delta1) otimes (B-delta2) = B otimes (B-delta1-delta2) oplus (delta1 otimes delta2) to a Knowledge Algebra law, instead requiring a four-level research progression before any algebraic-operation claim: Level 1 Representation (K -> (B,delta_K)), Level 2 Transformation (combining two (B,delta) states), Level 3 Closure (whether delta' can always be represented in the same carrier), and Level 4 Laws (testing associativity, commutativity, identity, inverse, distributivity, idempotence).

b_rows_sample.anchor: avoid importing the most significant digit -> least significant digit hierarchy into knowledge without evidence. Instead define a general locality operator W_i(D) ... T(D) = T(W_1(D)), T(W_2(D)),... is valid only if the global result can be reconstructed from those local computations. Can global kno
b_rows_sample.statement: Reformulates the moving-window idea as a general locality operator W_i(D) rather than importing the Vedic most-significant-to-least-significant-digit hierarchy without evidence, requiring that a decomposed transformation T(D)=T(W1(D)),T(W2(D)),... be valid only if the global result is reconstructable from local computations, posing the concrete research question of whether global knowledge transformation can be decomposed into bounded local transformations, and noting locality may itself become a representation-cost dimension.

b_rows_sample.anchor: our current experimental evidence does not justify Zero = algebraic identity or Zero = cancellation. What we have justified is much narrower: Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) iff Pi(T(D)) = Pi(T(E_S(D))). Therefore Zero is currently best understood as a contract-relative observational predicate. It may eventually i
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues a major correction refusing to place Zero alongside proposed Knowledge Algebra operators as an algebraic identity or cancellation element, since current evidence justifies only the narrower contract-relative predicate Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) iff Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))); Zero may eventually induce an algebraic structure, but that remains to be discovered rather than assumed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: REPRESENTATION / TRANSFORMATION / OBSERVATION -> PRESERVATION -> Adequacy / Zero -> DERIVED OPERATORS (Crosswise composition, Deficiency encoding, Local Window transformation) -> SPECIALIZED RULES -> certified heuristics. This architecture has a major advantage: It does not assume the algebra before
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a four-layer Knowledge Algebra architecture -- Representation/Transformation/Observation feeding a Preservation layer (splitting into Adequacy and Zero), which in turn supports Derived Operators (crosswise composition, deficiency encoding, local window transformation) and finally Specialized Rules/certified heuristics -- whose major advantage is that it does not assume the algebra before discovering it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Vedic mathematical procedures provide a source of candidate computational invariants and representation transformations for Knowledge Algebra. They do not by themselves establish the corresponding algebraic laws. Each candidate must be formalized as an operator, its preservation conditions identifie
b_rows_sample.statement: Rewrites the core proposition governing this whole research thread: Vedic mathematical procedures provide a source of candidate computational invariants and representation transformations for Knowledge Algebra, but do not by themselves establish algebraic laws -- each candidate must be formalized as an operator, its preservation conditions identified, and its closure/algebraic properties experimentally or mathematically verified -- yielding the five-stage pipeline 'Vedic computational pattern -> formal candidate operator -> representation -> preservation test -> algebraic-law test', explicitly rejecting the direct shortcut 'Vedic sutra -> Knowledge Algebra law'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Reference-relative representation K->(B,delta). 2. Structure-preserving cross-composition. 3. Certified specialized rewrite operators. 4. Local/windowed transformation. 5. Signed/complement representation. 6. Cancellation as a special case, only after an inverse structure is demonstrated. 7. Zero
b_rows_sample.statement: Prioritizes seven candidates for future testing in order: reference-relative representation, structure-preserving cross-composition, certified specialized rewrite operators, local/windowed transformation, signed/complement representation, cancellation as a special case (only after an inverse structure is demonstrated), and Zero as an algebraic element (only if future experiments establish that connection), keeping the Vedic material scientifically useful without letting the historical analogy dictate the mathematical ontology.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the most promising direction is not to build a 'Vedic Knowledge Algebra.' It is to use Vedic computational ideas as a generator of falsifiable candidate representations and operators, then let the experiments determine which ones actually belong in the Knowledge Algebra.
b_rows_sample.statement: Concludes that the most promising direction is not to build a 'Vedic Knowledge Algebra' but to use Vedic computational ideas purely as a generator of falsifiable candidate representations and operators, letting experiments determine which ones actually belong in the eventual Knowledge Algebra.

b_rows_sample.statement: Accepts a further 'extension' document as research-program guidance only, not an experimental result or new theory claim, judged consistent with the just-established recalibration progression Vedic Pattern -> Candidate Operator/Representation -> Preservation Test -> Algebraic Law Test.

b_rows_sample.statement: Praises the extension's strongest feature as keeping Zero/cancellation conservative rather than turning the Vedic analogy into an axiom, and endorses preserving a four-way distinction between representation (K->(B,delta_K)), transformation (structural composition), observation (Q,Pi), and preservation (whether the required observable survives) as a framework for evaluating future Vedic-inspired experiments.
