a_rows_sample.anchor: EXPERIMENT ID KR-BRIDGE-01-ZERO-PRESERVATION-2026-09 ... Determine whether there is any reproducible empirical or structural relationship between: A. elimination/Transformation-relative Zero, B. representation preservation/adequacy. WITHOUT assuming that Zero is a preservation criterion. ... The exp
a_rows_sample.statement: Commissions KR-BRIDGE-01-ZERO-PRESERVATION-2026-09, a bridge/falsification experiment explicitly designed to determine whether there is any reproducible relationship between elimination/Transformation-relative Zero and representation-preservation adequacy without assuming Zero is a preservation criterion, required to remain capable of falsifying the hypothesized relationship, and prohibited from constructing an algebra, pre-selecting a carrier, modifying Theory v1.2, creating Theory v1.3, selecting a kernel operator, or merging KR-ZERO and KR-REP-REDUCTION into one formalism.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO: ~89.7% singleton-determined levels ... ~8.2% irreducible levels ... Does NOT establish Zero as a preservation criterion. KR-REP-REDUCTION: R5 adequate, R4 inadequate ... Found no observed Zero/boundary association in that experiment. Does NOT establish a KR-ZERO law. ... These experiments a
a_rows_sample.statement: Summarizes the existing empirical baseline the bridge experiment builds on: KR-ZERO (89.7% singleton-determined, 8.2% irreducible, does not establish Zero as a preservation criterion) and KR-REP-REDUCTION (R5 adequate/R4 inadequate, no observed Zero/boundary association), framed as complementary but analytically independent results whose missing bridge the new experiment must test rather than assume.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H0: Zero and preservation are not systematically related in the tested regime. H1: Zero is associated with preservation under specified conditions. H2: Zero is predictive of preservation only under particular transformation/observable/contract configurations. H3: Any apparent relationship is explain
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies four competing hypotheses to be distinguished -- H0 no systematic relationship, H1 association under specified conditions, H2 predictive only under particular transformation/observable/contract configurations, H3 apparent relationship explained by a confounding factor (transformation class, contract, observable, redundancy, representation regime) -- with an explicit instruction not to privilege H1, and defines success as producing a clear positive or negative result regarding the tested relationship.

a_rows_sample.anchor: USE A PARALLEL REPRESENTATION FAMILY. Do NOT use only a deterministic sequential chain. A sequential chain ... has a data-processing constraint H(Q|Rn) <= H(Q|R(n-1)) and therefore cannot test non-monotone adequacy. The present experiment requires independently generated representations: Ra = Ta(D),
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates the critical design rule that the bridge experiment use a parallel representation family (independently generated representations Ra=Ta(D), Rb=Tb(D), neither a deterministic function of the other) rather than only a deterministic sequential chain, since a sequential chain's data-processing constraint H(Q|Rn)<=H(Q|R(n-1)) structurally prevents testing non-monotone adequacy -- directly addressing the H-C category error found in the prior KR-REP-REDUCTION reviews.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The mathematical carrier must be the minimum structure required by the actual experiment. Do not declare: set, graph, hypergraph, lattice, matroid, closure system, rewriting system, category, algebra as the carrier before the experiment. ... clearly distinguish: experimental carrier, mathematical ca
a_rows_sample.statement: Prohibits declaring any specific mathematical carrier (set, graph, hypergraph, lattice, matroid, closure system, rewriting system, category, algebra) before the experiment runs, requiring the carrier to be the minimum structure the experiment actually needs, and mandates keeping experimental carrier, mathematical carrier, and future KnowledgeOS knowledge representation explicitly distinct with no unevidenced transfer between them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use a finite structured source D ... rich enough to permit: redundancy, relational dependence, context dependence, individually removable elements, jointly non-removable groups, preservation and information-loss cases. ... For every source case store D, Q(D), contract parameters, transformation para
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the source data D to be a finite, deterministically-seeded structured source rich enough to permit redundancy, relational dependence, context dependence, individually removable elements, jointly non-removable groups, and both preservation and information-loss cases, with complete persistence of every source case's D, Q(D), contract parameters, transformation parameters, Zero ground truth, every representation, adequacy result, and decoder result, so no result depends on regenerated or hidden data.

a_rows_sample.anchor: At minimum construct representations with: R_A: information-preserving transformation, R_B: controlled lossy transformation, R_C: redundancy-removing transformation, R_D: relational/context-sensitive transformation. ... Do not optimize transformations after seeing results.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires at minimum four independently constructed representations -- R_A (information-preserving), R_B (controlled lossy), R_C (redundancy-removing), R_D (relational/context-sensitive) -- each fully specified (transformation ID, mathematical definition, input/output type, deterministic/random status, seed, provenance, expected information effect, contract dependencies) before results are examined, with no post-hoc optimization of transformations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Define Q BEFORE generating representations. ... Adequate(R) iff Q is recoverable from R. Operationally measure both empirical conditional information Hhat(Q|R) and exact semantic violation count Nviol ... Do not treat Hhat(Q|R)=0 as proof that population H(Q|R)=0.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the preservation target Q to be defined before representations are generated, with adequacy defined as Q being recoverable from R, measured operationally via both empirical conditional information Hhat(Q|R) and an exact semantic violation count Nviol, while never treating the empirical Hhat(Q|R)=0 as proof of the population-level H(Q|R)=0.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use the existing Transformation-relative Zero definition. For elimination E_S: Zero(T,Pi,S;D) iff Pi(T(D)) = Pi(T(E_S(D))). ... NEVER DEFINE ZERO USING Q. Do NOT define: Zero(S) := Q(D) = Q(E_S(D)). That would build the desired bridge into the definition. Zero must use its own declared observable/op
a_rows_sample.statement: Reuses the existing Transformation-relative Zero definition Zero(T,Pi,S;D) iff Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))), calculated independently from the preservation measurement, and issues a critical prohibition against ever defining Zero in terms of Q (e.g. Zero(S):=Q(D)=Q(E_S(D))), since that would build the desired bridge directly into the definition and make the experiment circular; Zero must use its own declared observable Pi while preservation uses Q.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The experiment must deliberately seek all four cells: Zero+Adequate, Zero+Inadequate, Non-Zero+Adequate, Non-Zero+Inadequate. ... Zero+Inadequate would directly demonstrate that Zero is not sufficient for preservation. Non-Zero+Adequate would demonstrate that Zero is not necessary for preservation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires a four-cell crossing design (Zero+Adequate, Zero+Inadequate, Non-Zero+Adequate, Non-Zero+Inadequate) deliberately populated in all cells where possible, noting that a populated Zero+Inadequate cell would show Zero is not sufficient for preservation and a populated Non-Zero+Adequate cell would show Zero is not necessary for it, while an empty cell must be investigated for generator/contract/transformation/sample-size/mathematical-necessity/implementation causes rather than treated as a law.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sweep the parameters that plausibly influence the relationship, including redundancy level, group size, representation loss, transformation class, observable Pi, preservation target Q, contract parameters, context dependence, relational interaction, source cardinality. Every parameter sweep must be
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires declared-in-advance parameter sweeps across ten plausibly influential parameters (redundancy level, group size, representation loss, transformation class, observable Pi, preservation target Q, contract parameters, context dependence, relational interaction, source cardinality), explicitly forbidding silent tuning to obtain balanced four-way cells.

a_rows_sample.anchor: At minimum stratify results by: transformation T, observable Pi, contract C, representation family, source structure, elimination size |S|. Report both pooled relationship and stratified relationship. An association that disappears after stratification must NOT be reported as a general Zero-preserva
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates confounding analysis stratifying results by transformation T, observable Pi, contract C, representation family, source structure, and elimination size |S|, reporting both pooled and stratified relationships, and forbidding reporting an association as a general Zero-preservation relationship if it disappears after stratification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Explicitly test T x Pi ... Do not classify transformations as simply relational / element-wise and stop there. Measure the actual interaction between transformation and observable. If higher-order or preservation behavior occurs under an element-wise transformation, record it. Do not resurrect the w
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires explicitly testing the transformation-times-observable interaction (T x Pi) rather than stopping at a coarse relational/element-wise classification, recording higher-order or preservation behavior even under element-wise transformations, and explicitly forbidding resurrection of the already-withdrawn claim that relational transformations produce higher order while element-wise ones do not.

a_rows_sample.anchor: retain the KR-ZERO determination-order analysis. Measure k=1,2,3,...,irreducible where feasible. Do not assume higher k -> more reduction, higher k -> less preservation, irreducibility -> information loss. Those are hypotheses to test, not definitions. In particular, do not equate determination orde
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires retaining the KR-ZERO determination-order analysis (k=1,2,3,...,irreducible) in the bridge experiment while explicitly forbidding the assumptions that higher k implies more reduction, less preservation, or that irreducibility implies information loss -- these remain hypotheses to test -- and forbidding equating determination order with preservation boundary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Retain the KR-REP-REDUCTION principle that reduction is multidimensional. Measure independently ... encoded size, cardinality, field count, representation entropy, number of relations, number of records, other declared structural measures. Do NOT invent a single 'reduction score' ... If a decoder is
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires measuring reduction multidimensionally (encoded size, cardinality, field count, entropy, relation count, record count, other declared measures) without inventing a single reduction score or assuming statistical independence among dimensions, and requires keeping representation adequacy strictly separate from decoder realization when a decoder is used, including an invertible recoding control to rule out decoder-sensitivity confounds.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTROL A: A known information-preserving representation. CONTROL B: A known information-destroying representation. CONTROL C: An invertible recoding of the same representation. CONTROL D: A representation where Zero is known to vary independently of the preservation target ... CONTROL E: Positive c
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies six mandatory controls that must execute before any interpretation: A) a known information-preserving representation; B) a known information-destroying representation; C) an invertible recoding of the same representation; D) a representation where Zero is known to vary independently of the preservation target (if the generator permits); E) a positive control that the preservation test can detect information loss; F) a positive control that the Zero test can detect elimination differences.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use independent TRAIN and TEST populations. Declare seeds, population size, generator, parameter distributions before execution. Persist the complete populations. No training result may influence test generation. No test result may influence transformation definitions. No post-hoc filtering may be u
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires independent train/test populations with pre-declared seeds, population size, generator, and parameter distributions, complete population persistence, and strict separation preventing training results from influencing test generation, test results from influencing transformation definitions, or post-hoc filtering to manufacture desired four-way cell counts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q1: Can Zero occur while preservation fails? Q2: Can preservation hold while Zero fails? Q3: Does the Zero/Adequacy relationship survive changes in T? ... Q7: Does determination order predict preservation independently of T/Pi/C? Q8: Does the relationship survive an invertible recoding? Q9/Q10: Is a
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates that the implementation explicitly answer ten falsification questions (Q1-Q10) covering whether Zero can occur without preservation and vice versa, whether the relationship survives changes in T, Pi, contract, redundancy, an invertible recoding, whether determination order predicts preservation independent of T/Pi/C, and whether any apparent relationship is explained by transformation class or by the preservation target Q itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: OUTCOME A -- NO RELATIONSHIP OBSERVED ... does NOT prove universal independence. OUTCOME B -- CONDITIONAL RELATIONSHIP ... Do NOT generalize. OUTCOME C -- ROBUST RELATIONSHIP ... Only in this case may a formal bridge hypothesis be proposed for a new experiment. OUTCOME D -- DESIGN FAILURE ... Do NOT
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines four mutually exclusive possible outcome classes for the experiment: A) no relationship observed (does not prove universal independence); B) conditional relationship under particular configurations (must not be generalized); C) robust relationship surviving transformations/observables/contracts/controls (the only case permitting a formal bridge hypothesis for a new experiment); D) design failure, in which case results must not be interpreted theoretically and the experiment must be revised.

a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies two required deliverable artifacts with exact filenames -- verification/zero-algebra/KR-BRIDGE-01-AUDIT-2026-09.md, a 16-item forensic audit covering source/Q/Pi/transformation/elimination/Zero/adequacy/decoder generation, train/test independence, seeds, serialization, parameter sweeps, contingency tables, statistics, absence of post-hoc selection, and reproducibility; and verification/zero-algebra/KR-BRIDGE-01-RESULTS-2026-09.md, a 22-section result document (executive verdict through epistemic status) -- with every important empirical claim required to trace to persisted data.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R1 Boundary Preservation [EXP] ... R2 Sequential Conditional-Information Monotonicity [THEORY] ... R3 Multi-Dimensional Reduction [EXP] ... R4 Tripartite Structural Separation [EXP/THEORY] ... R5 Disjunction of Zero & Preservation [NEG/EXP] ... R6 Dual Architectural Regimes [PROP] ... R7 Complex Sem
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the entire research-review chain into a canonical seven-row Epistemic Classification Ledger, each with an ID, finding, epistemic status tag, and explicit governing boundary/definition: R1 Boundary Preservation [EXP] scope-bounded to the specified (Carrier,Q,Pi,T,Sigma); R2 Sequential Conditional-Information Monotonicity [THEORY] as structural mathematical necessity; R3 Multi-Dimensional Reduction [EXP] requiring a vector representation rather than scalar collapse; R4 Tripartite Structural Separation [EXP/THEORY] (Representation != Recoverability != Decoder Realization) proven via rank-inversion decoupling; R5 Disjunction of Zero and Preservation [NEG/EXP]; R6 Dual Architectural Regimes [PROP] (sequential vs parallel); R7 Complex Semantic Domain [OPEN] (extension to graphs/entities/temporal constraints/narrative claims untested).

Decoder Realization: O_f(R)=Q ... Q-Relative Residual Representation: H(R|Q) representing essential context, provenance, audit met
b_rows_sample.statement: Fixes a five-term rigorous research vocabulary: Information-Theoretic Recoverability (population property H(Q|R)=0), Empirical Recoverability (sample-bounded estimator result Hhat(Q|R)=0 under a specified estimator, sample size N_n, and confidence bound), Representation Adequacy (theoretical preservation of all distinctions required by contract Pi for target inquiry Q), Decoder Realization (operational execution matching contract target O_f(R)=Q given explicit computational/decodability constraints), and Q-Relative Residual Representation (H(R|Q), representing essential context, provenance, audit metadata, or temporal states irreducible under inquiry Q).

b_rows_sample.anchor: SOURCE DATA D -> SEQUENTIAL REPRESENTATIONS (R5->R4->R3->R2) / PARALLEL REPRESENTATIONS (R_A, R_B) -> INQUIRY/CONTRACT (Q,Pi) -> RECOVERABILITY / ZERO(eliminability) / REDUCTION COST VECTOR -> ADEQUACY -> DECODER REALIZATION -> FUTURE KNOWLEDGEOS FORMAL LAYER.
b_rows_sample.statement: Diagrams a Research Governance Topology: source data D branches into Sequential Representations (R5->R4->R3->R2) and Parallel Representations (R_A, R_B), both feeding an Inquiry/Contract stage (Q,Pi), which fans into Recoverability (H(Q|R)), Zero/eliminability, and a Reduction Cost Vector, with Recoverability feeding Adequacy and then Decoder Realization, all converging on a Future KnowledgeOS Formal Layer.

[ ] Formally prove that ascending and descending rank conventions act as strictly invertible recodings ... [ ] Audit exact violation counts (N_viol) around the R5->R4 crossing point ... [ ] Audit times
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the complete KR-REP-REDUCTION-AUDIT-2026-09 operational checklist as the formal execution gate before any theory adjudication, organized into five categories with 18 checklist items total: (1) Information Theory & Estimators (raw Hhat calculation, Miller-Madow bias correction, bootstrap/confidence bounds, sample-vs-population Hhat=0 vs H=0 inference); (2) Decoder & Rank Mechanics (ascending/descending rank mapping implementation, tie-breaking mechanics, formal proof of invertible recoding); (3) Boundary Dynamics (exact sample size N_n per step, exact collision counts, N_viol audit around the R5->R4 crossing); (4) Transformation & Serialization Integrity (timestamp removal logic and float-to-integer cast boundaries, precision-reduction pipeline verification, canonical serialization with no hidden struct/padding metadata); (5) Contract & Isolation Guarantees (C evaluates R exclusively without touching raw D, decoder O_f is strictly fixed and distinct from optimal O*, train/test splitting and seeding guarantee zero leakage into Q).

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-REP-REDUCTION -> AUDIT GATE -> ADJUDICATION -> THEORY v1.3. Theory Status: Theory v1.2 remains frozen. No updates, al
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues the Final Research Governance Freeze: the pipeline KR-REP-REDUCTION -> AUDIT GATE -> ADJUDICATION -> THEORY v1.3 with no shortcut; the governance principle that KR-ZERO (relational eliminability) and KR-REP-REDUCTION (inquiry preservation under transformation) be kept strictly decoupled as orthogonal analytical systems; and the theory status that Theory v1.2 remains frozen, with no updates, algebra declarations, or kernel code modifications until KR-REP-REDUCTION-AUDIT-2026-09 is fully executed, reviewed, and adjudicated.

b_rows_sample.statement: Accepts the governance freeze with one wording adjustment: R4 'Tripartite Structural Separation' should be classified primarily as [EXP] (the experiment provides the empirical evidence for the separation) with [THEORY] noted as providing the formal distinction, rather than the combined tag [EXP/THEORY], on the ground that separating evidence from formal interpretation is cleaner.

b_rows_sample.statement: Makes it a mandatory rule for all future experiment reports that empirical recoverability be notated explicitly as Hhat(Q|R)=0 and never silently promoted to the population claim H(Q|R)=0.

No shortcut from experiment directly into theory or kernel implementation. Representation != Recoverability != Realization ... Zero
b_rows_sample.statement: Records the frozen state of the research program: KR-ZERO and KR-REP-REDUCTION are treated as analytically independent for now (not proven mathematically unrelated), the governance transition EXPERIMENT -> AUDIT -> ADJUDICATION -> THEORY v1.3 permits no shortcut into theory or kernel implementation, and the two frozen distinctions -- Representation != Recoverability != Realization, and Zero != Preservation Criterion -- hold unless future evidence establishes a relationship under explicitly defined conditions.

b_rows_sample.statement: Concludes that this governance freeze gives KnowledgeOS a disciplined research foundation without prematurely claiming a general Knowledge Algebra or Knowledge Extraction calculus, naming KR-REP-REDUCTION-AUDIT-2026-09 as the current next gate and reaffirming Theory v1.2 stays frozen until that audit produces an explicit adjudication.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The audit's decisive finding was not a computational error. It was an assumption two parties held and neither tested -- that desc = (n+1) - asc. I asserted it; review restated it in better vocabulary; the tie-break falsified it, 21 369 times.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the first concrete finding of the actually-executed KR-REP-REDUCTION-AUDIT-2026-09: the decisive problem was not a computational error but a shared, never-tested assumption that the descending rank equals (n+1) minus the ascending rank (desc=(n+1)-asc), which the tie-breaking mechanics falsified 21,369 times -- an assumption asserted by one party and merely restated in better vocabulary by a reviewing party, caught only because the audit protocol required 'formally prove' rather than 'state'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: An attractive interpretation must yield to an audit finding. ... the representation-reduction audit found: the bootstrap confidence interval procedure was invalid for the sparse conditional-entropy estimator; the rank invertibility claim failed because of tie handling. Those failures did not invalid
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports that the representation-reduction audit found two specific problems -- the bootstrap confidence-interval procedure was invalid for the sparse conditional-entropy estimator, and the rank-invertibility claim failed due to tie handling (matching the desc=(n+1)-asc falsification) -- neither of which invalidated the main structural conclusions (which rested on exact violation counts and train/test agreement), but both of which forced withdrawal of the affected claims, establishing the principle that an attractive interpretation must yield to an audit finding, essential if KnowledgeOS is to govern AI-generated knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Ascending and descending rank are merely invertible recodings.' The audit showed that deterministic tie-breaking makes this claim false in the implemented experiment.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally records the rejection of the claim that ascending and descending rank encodings are merely invertible recodings, since the audit showed deterministic tie-breaking makes this false in the implemented experiment -- the theory-level record of the desc=(n+1)-asc falsification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: desc != (n+1)-asc [for D with ties, e.g. D=[23000,46000,46000]] ... The implemented ascending/descending rank transformations were not proven to be simple invertible recodings. ... A representational convention can carry operational consequences. But the pure 'decoder-only effect' attribution was to
b_rows_sample.statement: Records the formal audit correction that the ascending/descending rank transformations were not proven to be simple invertible recodings, since deterministic tie-breaking on data with repeated values (e.g. D=[23000,46000,46000]) makes desc != (n+1)-asc; the broader lesson survives (a representational convention can carry operational consequences) but the pure 'decoder-only effect' attribution was too strong and had to be corrected after audit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the representation-reduction audit discovered that a proposed bootstrap confidence interval for conditional entropy was invalid because sparse resampling changed the support structure. ... define the estimator, establish its assumptions, evaluate finite-sample bias, use appropriate corrections, vali
b_rows_sample.statement: Details the specific audit finding that a proposed bootstrap confidence interval for conditional entropy was invalid because sparse resampling changed the support structure, listing six required remedial steps (define estimator, establish assumptions, evaluate finite-sample bias, apply corrections, validate bootstrap conditions, distinguish empirical from population support), while noting the main preservation conclusion survived since it rested on exact violation counts and train/test agreement rather than the invalid confidence interval.

a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a new experiment, KR-CONTEXT-INTEGRATION-01, to replace further symmetric Zoom-in/Zoom-out testing: given (K_t,Q)->K_t^focus->Investigation->D_t->Integration->K_{t+1}, test whether K_{t+1} preserves unrelated context, incorporates the new determination, preserves provenance/history, permits later revision, changes the answer to the original broader inquiry, does not require an inverse operation, and distinguishes local graph traversal from global epistemic state change -- argued to be a more faithful test of the original Nexus intuition, and doable without touching Theory v1.2 or reopening kernel selection.

b_rows_sample.statement: Governance decision: name the 19-section formal extension 'KR Integration — Proposed Theory Extension' rather than Theory v1.3, with individual propositions marked [PROP] until HPA ratification; a dated (2026-09-02) HPA Supervisory advisory reviews the extension and formally recommends 'ADOPT the proposed extension', confirming Theory v1.2 remains frozen, no proposition is promoted to [ESTABLISHED] without evidence and adjudication, the Kernel remains NOT SELECTABLE/[BLOCKED], and seven open decisions (R_req, non-evidential invariance, phi semantics, cross-frame policy, Contr, ≡sem, Lifecycle) remain OPEN.

No result produced by one function is automatically equivalent to the result of another. Formally: Rep != Reason != Eval != Det. This should become a theory-level principle, not merely a candidate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Central addition #1: make explicit the chain Evidence -> Representation -> Reasoning -> Evaluation -> Determination as a semantic separation of distinct epistemic functions (not merely an architectural pipeline); proposes the theory-level principle Rep != Reason != Eval != Det, citing the Handbook's distinction of knowledge representation from reasoning mechanisms and from task-level knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Add Explicit vs Derived Knowledge ... K_t^{exp} and K_t^{der,S} with K_t^{der,S}=Cn_S(K_t^{exp}) ... K^{exp}!=K^{der} and Derivability does not imply operational availability. Therefore K^{der,S} != K^{available,S}.
a_rows_sample.statement: FR-1 (section 2): defines K_t^exp (explicit) and K_t^der,S = Cn_S(K_t^exp) (derived under reasoning system S) as distinct conceptual layers; states K^exp != K^der and that derivability does not imply operational availability, so K^der,S != K^available,S. Grounded in the Handbook's distinction between explicit beliefs and logical-closure consequences, and the problem of logical omniscience. Status: STRONG.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Add the Reasoning-System parameter S ... K |-_S p ... S=(L,Sigma,R,Sem,B) ... We should not claim this tuple is the final KnowledgeOS definition of a ReasoningSystem ... neg Derive_S(K,p) does not entail neg p. And neg Derive_S(K,p) does not even necessarily entail neg Derivable_S(K,p). That distinction is extremely important for Zero and UNKNOWN.
a_rows_sample.statement: FR-2 (section 3): derivability should be indexed by a reasoning regime, Derive_S(K,p) rather than absolute K|-p, with S conceptually = (L representation language, Sigma vocabulary/signature, R inference rules, Sem semantics, B computational/resource boundary) explicitly NOT claimed as the final KnowledgeOS ReasoningSystem definition. Important consequence: not-Derive_S(K,p) entails neither not-p nor not-Derivable_S(K,p) -- a distinction flagged as extremely important for Zero and UNKNOWN.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Query != Evaluation != Determination ... ASK_S(K,q)->QueryResult ... Eval_c(K,r,Gamma)->EVal ... Det(EVal,Gamma)->Determination ... We must not define Sat = ASK or Sat = Truth or Determination = Truth. This should become an explicit KnowledgeOS invariant.
a_rows_sample.statement: FR-3 (section 4): promotes Query != Evaluation != Determination from research observation to theory principle, with ASK_S(K,q)->QueryResult, Eval_c(K,r,Gamma)->EVal, Det(EVal,Gamma)->Determination as the three distinct operations; explicitly forbids Sat=ASK, Sat=Truth, and Determination=Truth as an invariant, motivated by the Handbook's model-based-reasoning distinction between obtaining predictions, comparing to observations, and drawing conclusions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Computationally Bounded Knowledge ... Avail_S(K,B) subseteq Cn_S(K) ... Explicit != Derivable != Available ... This is not UNKNOWN in the same sense as absence of representation. It is a computational boundary.
a_rows_sample.statement: FR-4 (section 5): distinguishes Cn_S(K) (all consequences) from Avail_S(K,B) (what a bounded reasoning process can actually compute), with Avail_S(K,B) subseteq Cn_S(K), giving a three-way distinction Explicit != Derivable != Available; a proposition can be derivable-but-unavailable, which is a computational-boundary phenomenon, explicitly NOT the same kind of UNKNOWN as absence of representation. Flagged as feeding the future Zero/Evaluation model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Epistemic Change as multiple mechanisms ... reject a single undifferentiated K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,x). Instead ... Revision != Contraction != Update ... revision concerns correcting an epistemic state regarding a static world, whereas update concerns becoming current after the world itself changes.
a_rows_sample.statement: FR-5 (section 6): rejects a single undifferentiated transition K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,x); requires distinguishing Revision(K_t,e)->K_{t+1} (correction/reorganization of a static-world epistemic state), Contraction(K_t,p)->K_{t+1} (withdrawal of a commitment), and Update(K_t,Delta W)->K_{t+1} (the represented world changed) as semantic categories (not necessarily three implementation services), following the Handbook's revision-vs-update distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement non-monotonic knowledge evolution ... Classical accumulation K_t subseteq K_{t+1} is insufficient ... p in K_t while p not in K_{t+1} ... Knowledge evolution is not necessarily monotonic ... someone could incorrectly interpret K_{t+1} not-supseteq K_t as 'knowledge got worse.' It may instead be Correction or Retraction or World Update.
a_rows_sample.statement: FR-6 (section 7): classical monotone accumulation K_t subseteq K_{t+1} is insufficient; the theory must permit p in K_t while p not in K_{t+1} (Knowledge evolution is not necessarily monotonic), grounded in the Handbook's nonmonotonic-reasoning treatment of withdrawable conclusions. Warns explicitly against misreading K_{t+1} not-supseteq K_t as 'knowledge got worse' -- it may instead be Correction, Retraction, or World Update.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Representation Adequacy ... pi: X -> Y ... x1 != x2 can nevertheless satisfy pi(x1)=pi(x2) ... x1 ~_pi x2 iff pi(x1)=pi(x2) ... Adequacy(pi,Q) means the projection preserves every distinction required by question Q ... Structure -> Projection -> Induced Equivalence -> Information Loss -> Invariant Preservation -> Adequacy. I would now consider this a core KnowledgeOS theory principle.
a_rows_sample.statement: FR-7 (section 8): formalizes Representation Adequacy for a projection pi:X->Y, defining the induced equivalence x1 ~_pi x2 iff pi(x1)=pi(x2), and Adequacy(pi,Q) meaning pi preserves every distinction required by question Q; integrates with existing Projection work into the sequence Structure -> Projection -> Induced Equivalence -> Information Loss -> Invariant Preservation -> Adequacy. Elevated to a core KnowledgeOS theory principle, grounded in the Handbook's qualitative-representation/abstraction treatment. Status: STRONG CANDIDATE -> promote.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement 'failure to derive' as a typed epistemic distinction ... U_rep, U_der, U_avail, U_evid, U_eval, U_scope ... We do not need to make these six values of one enum ... we should not flatten them. Instead EVal=(Value,Reason,Boundary,...) remains the better direction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 9 (feeding FR-3/FR-4): distinguishes six typed causes of epistemic failure-to-derive -- U_rep (not represented), U_der (not derivable under S), U_avail (derivable but resource-unavailable), U_evid (insufficient evidence), U_eval (evaluation cannot determine), U_scope (outside declared scope) -- explicitly refusing to flatten them into one enum, per prior FDE/Zero experiments, and reaffirming the structured EVal=(Value,Reason,Boundary,...) direction as better than a flat value set. Grounded in the Handbook's observation that incomplete reasoning and incomplete knowledge can have different causes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Revision Lineage ... if p->q and p supports q, then removing p can invalidate the derivation of q. Therefore derived content should retain a dependency structure: Support(q)={p, p->q, ...} ... This is not merely provenance ... It is derivation dependency ... DerivationLineage as a candidate theory concept.
a_rows_sample.statement: FR-8 (section 10): if p->q and p supports q, removing p can invalidate the derivation of q; derived content should retain a dependency structure Support(q) = {p, p->q, ...}, named DerivationLineage and distinguished from ordinary provenance (it is derivation dependency, stronger than provenance-of-origin), grounded in the Handbook's belief-revision discussion. Status: STRONG CANDIDATE.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement 'revision is constrained, not uniquely determined' ... Constraints(delta) not=> Unique(delta) ... Semantic invariants constrain admissible operations but do not, by themselves, select a unique operation unless an additional selection criterion is established. This principle applies beyond revision: equality, evaluation, contradiction, aggregation, transition, policy semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 11 (general methodological principle): AGM-style material shows desirable rationality constraints do not determine a unique revision operator (Constraints(delta) does not imply Unique(delta)); generalized as 'semantic invariants constrain admissible operations but do not, by themselves, select a unique operation unless an additional selection criterion is established', explicitly extended beyond revision to equality, evaluation, contradiction, aggregation, transition, and policy semantics. Judged compatible with existing kernel discipline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Temporal Persistence as distinct from Knowledge ... An entity/state can persist because no terminating event has been represented, but that is not equivalent to knowing that it persists ... Persistence != Truth != Knowledge and NoKnownChange not=> NoChange. This is important for our future delta.
a_rows_sample.statement: FR-9 (section 12): persistence (an entity/state persisting because no terminating event has been represented) is distinct from knowing that it persists; states Persistence != Truth != Knowledge and NoKnownChange does not imply NoChange, drawn from the Handbook's Event Calculus inertia/release treatment; flagged as important for the future delta definition. Status: STRONG CANDIDATE.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement temporal qualification ... p@t or p@[t1,t2] ... Eval(p,t1) and Eval(p,t2) can legitimately differ without contradiction ... Epistemic validity may be temporally indexed; temporal disagreement is not automatically logical contradiction. This is especially important for our recent cross-frame contradiction work.
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 13: proposes temporal qualification p@t or p@[t1,t2] (instants, intervals, granularity as distinct representation choices, per the Handbook) so Eval(p,t1) and Eval(p,t2) can legitimately differ without contradiction; states the principle 'epistemic validity may be temporally indexed; temporal disagreement is not automatically logical contradiction', flagged as important for the corpus's cross-frame contradiction work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement distributed evidence -- but not distributed knowledge logic ... E1 union E2 union E3 may jointly support a determination even when Det(E1)=U, Det(E2)=U, Det(E3)=U ... JointEvidence != sum IndividualDeterminations ... do not import epistemic logic's D_G, common knowledge, or agent semantics into the kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: FR-11 (section 14): union of individually-undetermined evidence sources (Det(E1)=Det(E2)=Det(E3)=U) may jointly support a determination, drawn from the Handbook's distributed-knowledge treatment; proposes the weaker KnowledgeOS principle JointEvidence != sum(IndividualDeterminations) and JointSupport(E_G,p|Gamma), while explicitly forbidding import of epistemic logic's distributed-knowledge operator D_G, common knowledge, or full agent semantics into the kernel. Status: CANDIDATE.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Task Knowledge as a separate theoretical layer ... DomainKnowledge != TaskKnowledge != ReasoningMechanism ... PSM: Input -> ReasoningPattern -> TaskOutput ... otherwise KnowledgeOS risks treating every reasoning process as generic.
a_rows_sample.statement: FR-10 (section 15): drawing on the Handbook's Problem-Solving Method (PSM) material as highly DDD-compatible, proposes DomainKnowledge != TaskKnowledge != ReasoningMechanism, with PSM: Input -> ReasoningPattern -> TaskOutput, and a DDD interpretation chain BoundedContext -> DomainKnowledge -> Task -> PSM -> Reasoning -> Determination; motivated by the risk that KnowledgeOS otherwise treats every reasoning process as generic. Recorded as candidate theory structure, not kernel primitive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement model multiplicity as a determination concept ... M(K,Gamma) ... |M|=0 could indicate inconsistency under the relevant model semantics ... |M|=1 could indicate model-level uniqueness ... |M|>1 indicates underdetermination ... |M|=1 does not automatically mean KnowledgeOS has determined the proposition ... ModelUniqueness != KnowledgeDetermination.
a_rows_sample.statement: FR-12 (section 16): defines M(K,Gamma) as the set of models compatible with current knowledge and context: |M|=0 may indicate inconsistency under the relevant model semantics, |M|=1 model-level uniqueness, |M|>1 underdetermination; explicit warning that |M|=1 does NOT automatically mean KnowledgeOS has determined the proposition (model space and reasoning capability still matter), yielding ModelUniqueness != KnowledgeDetermination. Status: RESEARCH CANDIDATE, upgraded to 'very strong candidate'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement diagnosability as an evidence-quality property ... A useful observation/test is one that discriminates among competing hypotheses ... DiscriminativePower(e,H) ... this does not revive N_eff. Our previous negative result remains: PairwiseDistinguishability not=> FamilyComplexity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 17: proposes DiscriminativePower(e,H) as a candidate evidence-quality property (a useful observation/test discriminates among competing hypotheses, per the Handbook's model-based reasoning chapter), explicitly noting this does NOT revive the previously-rejected N_eff metric, and reaffirms the standing negative result PairwiseDistinguishability does not imply FamilyComplexity; final principle: evidence can be evaluated by the distinctions it preserves among admissible hypotheses.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The resulting KnowledgeOS theory structure ... Truth/World State -> Observation -> Evidence -> Representation (Explicit/Derived/Contextual) -> Reasoning S -> Evaluation Eval_c -> Determination -> Decision -> Action -> Observation' ... Orthogonal dimensions: Context, Time, Provenance, Authority, Scope, Computational Boundary ... And state change: K_t -> Revision / Contraction / World Update / New Observation / New Reasoning Capability -> K_t+1
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 19 assembles the whole review into one restructured theory diagram: a linear pipeline Truth/World-State -> Observation -> Evidence -> Representation(Explicit/Derived/Contextual) -> Reasoning-S -> Evaluation(Eval_c) -> Determination -> Decision -> Action -> Observation', six orthogonal dimensions (Context, Time, Provenance, Authority, Scope, Computational Boundary), and a five-way state-change fan-out from K_t (Revision, Contraction, World Update, New Observation, New Reasoning Capability) into K_t+1.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If I reduce the entire book to the minimum theory contribution, I would make this the new KnowledgeOS epistemic law: Evidence is not directly Knowledge. More formally: E -> Rep -> Reason_S -> Eval_c -> Det, with Truth, Context, Time, Provenance, Authority remaining orthogonal dimensions. And knowledge evolution is not one operation: Revision != Contraction != WorldUpdate != Reasoning.
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 21, the review's single most-reduced claim, proposed as a new KnowledgeOS epistemic law: 'Evidence is not directly Knowledge', formalized as the chain E -> Rep -> Reason_S -> Eval_c -> Det with Truth/Context/Time/Provenance/Authority as orthogonal dimensions, and knowledge evolution decomposed as Revision != Contraction != WorldUpdate != Reasoning; judged to be what can actually be implemented into the theory now without violating existing epistemic discipline.

TELL = requirement insertion. Rejected ... Model uniqueness = Determination. Not yet ... Distributed knowledge logic = KnowledgeOS social ontology. Not yet ... N_eff. Still off the critical path.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What would we expect to see if the hypothesis were true, but do not see? ... Observed / Not observed / Expected but absent / Unexpectedly present / Unknown / Not measurable / Not collected ... Not observed does not mean Does not exist.
a_rows_sample.statement: Absence becomes evidence: proposes recording Observed/Not observed/Expected-but-absent/Unexpectedly-present/Unknown/Not-measurable/Not-collected as non-equivalent states, with the invariant that 'not observed' does not mean 'does not exist'; further refined into an Observed/Unobserved/Unknown state model per proposition, explicitly contrasted with a true/false binary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: UNKNOWN / UNCERTAIN / SUPPORTED / CONTRADICTED / ESTABLISHED ... even 'established' should not mean metaphysical certainty. ... the book explicitly advocates remaining comfortable with uncertainty and not claiming absolute final answers.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a five-state epistemic vocabulary (UNKNOWN/UNCERTAIN/SUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED/ESTABLISHED) with the caveat that even ESTABLISHED (a governance-permitted stronger status) must never imply metaphysical certainty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero = Neutral starting condition ... It begins as: UNKNOWN
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero as neutral knowledge state: Zero != Nothing, it is a neutral starting condition. A new knowledge object begins without authority, evidence, validation or interpretation -- it begins as UNKNOWN.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UNKNOWN != False. UNKNOWN != Missing. UNKNOWN = Known unresolved state
b_rows_sample.statement: UNKNOWN is proposed as a first-class state, distinct from False and from Missing: UNKNOWN = a known, unresolved state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UNKNOWN != False. UNKNOWN != Missing. UNKNOWN = Known unresolved state
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero lens: UNKNOWN restated as a first-class known-unresolved state, distinct from False and Missing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS should not force: Unknown -> False / Unknown -> Guess / Unknown -> Empty. Instead: Unknown -> Known Unknown
b_rows_sample.statement: Combining Zero ('unknown is a valid state') with ECS ('failure does not destroy truth, failure pauses advancement'): Unknown should be preserved and later resolved, never forced into False/Guess/Empty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Different observations may represent different projections of the same underlying object.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets the elephant-and-blind-men story (cited by the source) not as 'everyone is equally right' but as 'different observations may represent different projections of the same underlying object', formalized as perspectives A/B/C/D undergoing structural comparison to yield a common invariant = ZERO.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge is perspective dependent, but structure may be perspective invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Abstracts the source's citation of Subhash Kak's six-darsanas-as-cube-walls metaphor into the principle 'knowledge is perspective dependent, but structure may be perspective invariant', with the research question 'what survives when we rotate the perspective?' answered by ZERO = invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z_M(K) = invariant across plausible worlds ... The technology disappears. The invariant remains.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces modal Zero Z_M(K) = invariant across plausible worlds, alongside a claimed prior representation Zero Z_R(K)=invariant across representations and temporal Zero Z_T(K)=invariant across time; illustrated by four possible event-bus technology choices (Kafka/RabbitMQ/sync API/another event bus) all preserving the invariant requirement 'evidence publication must remain replayable' -- the technology disappears, the invariant remains.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z = ⋂_i Structure(I_i) ... What structure remains invariant across competing models, representations, times, and perspectives? That may be one of our strongest candidates for robust knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the Zero lens as Z=intersection_i Structure(I_i) over interpretations generated from multiple world models W1..Wn (not necessarily literal set intersection in implementation), asking what structure remains invariant across competing models, representations, times and perspectives, proposed as one of the strongest candidates for robust knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O_i = π_i(R) ... O1 ≠ O2 doesn't necessarily mean R1 ≠ R2. It may simply mean π1 ≠ π2. This gives us a very useful projection lens.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the elephant analogy as a projection: observation Oi=pi_i(R) for underlying reality/object R and observer perspective pi_i, concluding that differing observations O1!=O2 need not imply differing underlying realities R1!=R2 -- it may simply reflect differing perspectives pi1!=pi2 -- named the 'projection lens'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z = Invariant(O1,...,On) ... Zero is not "nothing." It is the minimum invariant structure that survives changes in representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Given observations O1..On, defines Z=Invariant(O1,...,On) and explicitly corrects a possible misreading: Zero is not 'nothing', it is the minimum invariant structure that survives changes in representation -- called one of the strongest concepts in the entire exploration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dhātu = transformation structure ... Zero = invariant structure ... what changed? / what remained?
b_rows_sample.statement: States a Dhatu/Zero duality: given O1 --T1--> O2 --T2--> O3, Dhatu asks what transformation generated the new state (Dhatu = transformation structure) while Zero asks what remained (Zero = invariant structure).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens result on Williamson: after removing beliefs, documents, language, databases, probabilities, possible worlds, embeddings, topics, LLMs, what survives is minimal: 'A participant is related to a proposition/content in a world/context/time such that the proposition is true and the participant is in a factive state of knowing.' Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Participants make commitments. 2. Commitments have inferential consequences. 3. Some commitments are supported/entitled...
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brandom (removing language/English/sentences/speech/Frege/Wittgenstein/philosophy) yields ten survivor claims: participants make commitments; commitments have inferential consequences; some commitments are supported/entitled; commitments can conflict; participants assess one another's commitments; new actions alter the state; implicit relations can become explicit; concepts are characterized partly by inferential roles; objectivity can emerge within social assessment; a claim is not merely a string but a position in a normative/inferential structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown is not simply an error state. It is a legitimate epistemic condition.
b_rows_sample.statement: ASP answer-set semantics give TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN query results and ground at least three distinct kinds of 'unknown': unknown because alternatives remain (P and ¬P both possible), unknown because the agent is unaware (neither represented), and unknown because a default was blocked (an exception/missing condition prevented an otherwise-applicable default). The earlier flat UNKNOWN category should become an Epistemic Status taxonomy: true/false/unresolved-alternatives/not-represented-unaware/defeasibly-inferable-but-blocked/etc; the exact taxonomy remains a research question but the distinction itself is now strongly grounded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Absence must not silently become an epistemic state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Danger flagged in the Projection model: 'If Projection P2 doesn't contain X, therefore X is false' would be wrong, since absence from a projection could mean not relevant, not visible, not assessed, outside scope, unavailable, superseded, or genuinely no longer justified — these are different meanings. This connects to the ZERO lens: absence must not silently become an epistemic state, giving another reason to preserve ZERO discipline within the Projection idea.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U(e) ∈ {alternative, unrepresented, blocked-default, outside-scope, computationally-unresolved}
b_rows_sample.statement: Unknownness U(e) is proposed not as a Boolean but a classification (alternative / unrepresented / blocked-default / outside-scope / computationally-unresolved), with the exact taxonomy left empirical and countable for future statistical analysis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. There is an underlying world/domain. 2. A participant has beliefs/knowledge about it. 3. Only part of that knowledge may be explicitly represented...
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brachman & Levesque (removing FOL/Prolog/frames/description logic/SAT/default logic/Bayesian networks/STRIPS/GOLOG) yields twelve survivor claims: an underlying world/domain exists; a participant has beliefs/knowledge about it; only part is explicitly represented; representation is a mapping between domains; reasoning derives implicit content from explicit content; meaning depends on interpretation/context; different representation languages have different expressive power; reasoning capability is resource-limited; knowledge changes and can be revised; uncertainty/vagueness require richer representations; the same knowledge may have different representations; action depends on knowledge — described as extraordinarily close to the current model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: what survives across *both* phases is: **a knower/participant · something known · a ground · and a record that the two were connected.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens applied across both phases: after stripping optional attributes, what survives universally is a knower/participant, something known, a ground, and a record that the two were connected — every phase and nearly every model retains those four; nothing else survives universally. The corpus distinguishes 'nothing exists' from 'we do not know' (0258: 'Knowledge is not only about what exists'; formal law §9: unknown≠absent≠false). Whether UNKNOWN is the absence of Knowledge or a state of an identified object is NOT resolved by the corpus: formal law (⟨Z-1⟩) says UNKNOWN/ABSENT/FALSE/REJECTED are states of an identified epistemic object, while kernel document 125708 §17 pushes the other way ('UNKNOWN must not be a single epistemic state', eight readings) — no new state proposed here.

b_rows_sample.statement: Repository Zero (Z-KOS-001) is a foundational meta-principle explicitly refused as kernel article and implementation object ('Zero is the name for that prevention', 'Zero != Component = Property of the boundaries'), whereas v0.2 Zero is the computable goal-gap function Zero(K, EC); same term, incompatible senses, extending the CON-01 lineage with an implementation-side third sense; no repository counterpart of the goal-gap function exists, and the eta-totality/G-residual question (T-9) stays open.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We want to know whether there exists a corresponding state transformation T:K x I -> K such that F(That(H,i)) = T(F(H),i) for every valid H and input i. If this holds, then the history dynamics descend to the state space.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sets up the formal question of state sufficiency: given a history space H, a proposed state abstraction F:H->K, and a history-level transformation That:HxI->H, does a corresponding state-level transformation T:KxI->K exist such that F(That(H,i))=T(F(H),i) for all valid H,i -- i.e. do history dynamics descend to the state space.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H_A ~_F H_B iff F(H_A)=F(H_B). Then state sufficiency requires: H_A ~_F H_B => That(H_A,i) ~_F That(H_B,i). Thus ~_F must be a congruence with respect to valid transformations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the equivalence relation ~_F induced by the state abstraction (H_A~_F H_B iff F(H_A)=F(H_B)) and states the central congruence requirement: this equivalence must be preserved by every valid transformation for the state representation to be sufficient.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Now suppose the proposed state representation retains only Content(K)={p}. ... Authorized(A)=true but Authorized(B)=false. Then F(That(H_A,validate)) != F(That(H_B,validate)). Yet initially F(H_A)=F(H_B). Content-only K fails the congruence test. This is a genuine falsification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsifies a content-only knowledge state via a worked example: two histories with different evidence sources (A authorized, B not) collapse to the same content-only state, but a governance-sensitive validation transformation produces divergent outcomes (Validated vs Unvalidated) depending on the discarded source information -- a genuine congruence failure, showing content-only K is insufficient once authority-sensitive transformations are valid operations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose we enrich the state with lambda(e)=source(e). Now F(H_A) != F(H_B) ... The previous counterexample disappears. But this does not yet prove sufficiency. We have only shown one missing distinction has been restored.
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows adding a source/provenance field lambda(e)=source(e) to the state resolves the specific counterexample found, but explicitly cautions this only restores one missing distinction and does not establish global sufficiency -- more collapsed-but-behaviorally-different histories must still be searched for.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose H_C and H_D have identical Content and Provenance. But H_C was produced under policy pi_1 while H_D was produced under pi_2 ... F(H_C)=F(H_D) under a representation that omits policy history. But T(H_C,i) != T(H_D,i). ... Is Policy part of state, provenance, or external context? ... It is de
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a further counterexample: two histories identical in content and provenance but produced under different policies collapse to the same state under a policy-omitting representation, yet future validation depending on the original governing policy produces different results -- concluding whether policy belongs to state, provenance, or external context cannot be decided by convenience but is determined by transformation sufficiency (independently arriving at a question the parallel verifier track, S1602/S1603, was also attacking).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Two histories have the same proposition but different validity intervals theta_A(p)=[t0,t1), theta_B(p)=[t1,t2). Suppose a transformation asks CurrentVersion(S,t1+epsilon)? Then the two states produce different results. ... Temporal validity is not merely decorative metadata if temporal queries are
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows via a temporal-query counterexample (CurrentVersion(S,t1+epsilon)?) that a state representation omitting temporal qualification fails congruence when temporal queries are valid operations -- confirming temporal validity is functionally load-bearing, not decorative metadata.

a_rows_sample.anchor: e1->p and e2->not p. Compare K_A={p,e1} with K_B={p,e1,e2,not p}. A transformation T_assess may produce Assessment(K_A)=Supported but Assessment(K_B)=Conflicted. ... A state representation containing only the latest proposition K={p} would lose information necessary for future assessment.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a contradictory-evidence counterexample showing evidence multiplicity is semantically relevant: two states differing only in whether conflicting evidence is retained produce different Assessment outcomes (Supported vs Conflicted) under T_assess, so a state keeping only the latest proposition would lose information needed for future assessment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose an information component x can affect the result of a valid future transformation T(K,i). Then x cannot be discarded from the state abstraction unless it is recoverable from other state information. Formally: x is semantically disposable => x=f(K) for some reconstruction function f, or no va
a_rows_sample.statement: States a general disposability criterion generalizing all the preceding counterexamples: an information component x may be discarded from the state abstraction only if it is reconstructible from the remaining state (x=f(K) for some f) or no valid operation can distinguish states differing only in x -- giving a formal test for classifying any candidate field as state, metadata, provenance, external context, or truly redundant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K=F(H) is a transformation-sufficient representation if all permitted future semantics can be determined from K, rather than the complete H. But we should not call K a sufficient statistic without qualification. ... K must be sufficient for the permitted KnowledgeOS transformation semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Draws an explicit but qualified analogy to the statistical notion of a sufficient statistic: a state K=F(H) is transformation-sufficient if all permitted KnowledgeOS transformation semantics can be determined from K rather than the full history H -- but the file cautions the statistical term applies to a specific model/parameter and should not be borrowed unqualified, since the KnowledgeOS requirement is broader (sufficiency for a whole permitted transformation semantics, not one parameter).

a_rows_sample.anchor: H ~ mu_H. Then K=F(H) induces a push-forward distribution mu_K = F_* mu_H. ... mu_K is a regime-level object, not necessarily part of K.
a_rows_sample.statement: Connects the state abstraction to measure theory without making it foundational: if H is a random history with distribution mu_H, then K=F(H) induces a push-forward distribution mu_K=F_*mu_H (mu_K(A)=mu_H(F^{-1}(A)) for measurable A); explicitly classifies mu_K as a regime-level object, consistent with the parallel Step 246 finding (S1601) that probability belongs to a regime projection, not to K itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F is a compression map. The question becomes: Is this compression lossless with respect to the semantics we care about? That is exactly the congruence question. ... F o That = T o F. This is the formal expression of state sufficiency.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the commutative-diagram criterion F o That = T o F as the formal expression of state sufficiency (the state abstraction F is a compression map; sufficiency means the compression is lossless with respect to the transformation semantics), calling it one of the strongest formal tests obtained in the corpus so far, and gives the corresponding failure interpretation (a non-commuting diagram means the proposed state representation has lost necessary information).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K=(Content,Qualification,Governance) survives the experiments only if those components contain all information required by valid transformations. ... we should not yet assert K=(G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) as a final decomposition. a_rows_sample.statement: Finds 'Assurance' irreparably overloaded across 31 definitional statements collapsing into 6 mutually incompatible types (composed local contracts, a function of irreversibility/impact/criticality, a 'Strong BC Candidate' label, BackwardTraceability, a self-referential DeterministicAssurance, and a plain boolean); Step 230's self-referential definition directly contradicts the corpus's own imported Williamson result that assurance cannot recursively certify itself; and by the corpus's own most-repeated epistemological claim (assurance is strong only where executable, weak where prose), the corpus's own assurance concept is weak -- named completion blocker CB-1, a hard blocker on formal closure.

a_rows_sample.statement: Extends S1612's proven results with 5 further executed algebraic facts: (K,Merge,empty-set) forms a commutative idempotent monoid, i.e. a join-semilattice; Contradict is symmetric and irreflexive but NOT transitive, making it a tolerance relation rather than an equivalence (any equivalence-class-based construction on contradiction is wrong); Remove has no total inverse (cascading removal loses relations R, non-cascading breaks Valid); Split is lossy on R; and Merge preserves structural validity but not consistency, demonstrated by an executed counterexample where two individually consistent states merge into a contradictory one.

a_rows_sample.statement: Reports the one failing probe (probe 6 of 14) as genuine unresolved theory, not a test defect: an assertion constructed to supersede another is also flagged as contradicting it, since supersession and contradiction are indistinguishable to a purely pairwise predicate when both assertions are open-ended and their intervals overlap; of three attempted repairs, one (closing the superseded interval) is refuted (breaks content-addressed identity and Valid), while two are viable -- (a') excluding interval-end from the identity hash (at the cost of making temporal validity mutable state) and (c) making Contradict discount differences already explained by the relation set R (no mutation needed) -- with implementation evidence (ReplayAssertion's immutability invariant) favoring (c), which independently re-derives, from the opposite direction, that R is not reducible to the assertion set A alone.

b_rows_sample.statement: Argues that any invariant comparing objects is relation-relative among the four equality relations (=, ≡, ≈, ≅_λ): a transformation can preserve semantic state (K_t ≡ K_{t+1}) while changing structurally (K_t ≠_structural K_{t+1}) because metadata/representation changed, and provenance-sensitive equality may distinguish states that semantic equality identifies.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 287 must distinguish: $$ \text{invariant} $$ from: $$ \text{conserved information} $$ ... This distinction prevents the persistence research from accidentally collapsing into state immutability.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes an invariant (P(Kt) implies P(Kt+1)) from a conservation claim (a stronger statement about preserved content or quantity): the existence of Lineage does not imply every aspect of the previous state is conserved, and N persisting does not mean K_t=K_{t+1} — preventing identity-persistence research from collapsing into state immutability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: For every invariant: 1. establish that the antecedent can actually hold; 2. establish that the transition class is non-empty; 3. establish that the equality relation permits meaningful comparison; 4. only then evaluate preservation. Thus: **No vacuous invariant counts as substantively established.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes the D285-5 vacuity lesson into a mandatory four-step vacuity check for every candidate invariant: establish the antecedent can actually hold, establish the transition class is non-empty, establish the equality relation permits meaningful comparison, and only then evaluate preservation — no vacuous invariant counts as substantively established.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 2. ⭐⭐⭐ The Sat_c executability boundary is an inheritance boundary ... EXECUTABLE_NOW = ['content','evidence','provenance'] ... BLOCKED = ['status','consistency','governance','temporal','operational'] ... The three executable Sat_c classes are exactly the three with an ancestor in Theory v1.0. The five blocked classes are exactly the five added afterwards with no ancestor.
a_rows_sample.statement: Discovers the historical cause of Sat_c's 3-executable/5-blocked class split (from satc_spec.py, previously established in this programme): Theory v1.0 carries two requirement/gap taxonomies (SS28 DEF-20's requirement kinds including evidence and provenance requirements; SS30's typed gap Delta_t=(Delta^content,Delta^uncertainty,Delta^model,Delta^observability,Delta^requirement)). An occurrence census across the whole document (with positive controls) finds content/evidence/provenance each have an ancestor while status/consistency/governance/temporal/operational all score exactly 0 as requirement or gap dimensions (despite occurring as bare words elsewhere in the document). Concludes the three executable Sat_c classes are EXACTLY the three with a Theory v1.0 ancestor, and the five blocked classes are exactly the five added afterward with no ancestor at all.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ⭐⭐ Executability tracks provenance, not difficulty. ... status: '⪰ IS NOT DEFINED BY THE THEORY', governance: 'no evaluator exists', temporal: 'no temporal semantics defined', operational: 'δ is Step 290 and is open'. ... BLOCKED here means UN-INHERITED, and that is a fourth thing beside UNDEFINED, UNFORMALIZED and UNIMPLEMENTED. ... uncertainty and model were inherited and dropped.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues Sat_c executability tracks PROVENANCE, not difficulty: satc_spec.py's own blocker notes for each blocked class explicitly say the theory does not define it (status not defined by the theory, no governance evaluator exists, no temporal semantics defined, delta/operational is an open Step 290 item). Proposes BLOCKED here means UN-INHERITED, a fourth epistemic category distinct from UNDEFINED, UNFORMALIZED, and UNIMPLEMENTED. Notes the mapping is not a clean bijection -- uncertainty and model classes were inherited from Theory v1.0's taxonomy but then dropped from the final eight-class Sat_c list, so the eight-class list is neither a subset nor superset of either v1.0 taxonomy. Explicitly states this feeds but does not reopen the prior G-33 disposition (all 8 Sat_c classes defined/formalised, 5 dependency-blocked stands) -- it supplies only the historical CAUSE of the split.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 3. Object-by-object: Δ_t Gap is a SET (DEF-21) ... §29 explicitly rejects the older K_t^* - K_t subtraction ... direct predecessor of v1.2's GapPartition ... Sat 2-argument and two-valued at birth ... the birth of U is exactly the v1.0 → v1.2 step ... Zero DEF-22 ... Adequate ≡ Zero collapse ... visible in the theory text itself — it is not an artifact of the simulation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Fixes several object definitions from Theory v1.0: Delta_t=Gap(K_t,EC_t)={r in Req(EC_t): not Sat(K_t,r)} (DEF-21, 'the canonical v1.0 definition'), with SS29 explicitly rejecting an older K_t^*-K_t subtraction form ('heterogeneous epistemic structures cannot generally be subtracted') -- identified as the direct predecessor of v1.2's GapPartition(K,Req)=(violated,undetermined,satisfied), giving a two-step declared supersession chain subtraction->set->partition; Sat at birth (DEF-21) is 2-argument and strictly TWO-VALUED (clean negation, no third value), meaning the birth of the U/undetermined value is exactly the v1.0->v1.2 transition, though the registry notes Sat carries two different arities within this one document (per-requirement Sat(K_t,r) and per-contract Sat(K_t,EC_t)); Zero(K_t,EC_t) iff Delta_t=empty-set iff K_t models EC_t (DEF-22), with Adequate(K_t,EC_t) iff Sat(K_t,EC_t) (DEF-20) and SS29 giving Delta_t=empty-set iff Adequate(K_t,EC_t) -- meaning the Adequate=Zero collapse (previously flagged elsewhere as TG-3/CIRC-3) is visible directly in the theory's own text, not merely an artifact of a downstream simulation; also fixes Zero_epistemic != Zero_probabilistic.

a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the investigation's own prior registry entry for the Ideal State object: finds a third formulation, DEF-19's I(EC_t)={K in K: Sat(K,EC_t)} (2026-09-02 00:46:31, a REGION of knowledge states, type P(K)) precedes the registry's previously-recorded 'I_t_v1' formulation (I_t=R_t, the requirement set, 2026-09-02 08:23:33) by 7 hours 37 minutes and has a fundamentally different codomain -- meaning I_t underwent a RE-TYPING across its history, not merely a refinement, and the registry's 'v1' label was itself an error (the witness/timestamp was correct, only its version-ordering label was wrong).

a_rows_sample.anchor: DEF-33 — minimality is explicitly not operator count ... K_min = argmin_K Complexity(K) subject to CapabilityClosure, SemanticAdequacy, Preservation, InvariantPreservation, TransitionCompleteness. ... custody(I,K) = {o ∈ K : I fails in K−{o}} ... Smaller Kernel ⇏ Better Kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Fixes DEF-33's minimality definition: K_min=argmin_K Complexity(K) subject to five explicit constraints (CapabilityClosure, SemanticAdequacy, Preservation, InvariantPreservation, TransitionCompleteness) -- deliberately NOT defined as operator count. SS74 adds a custody function custody(I,K)={o in K: invariant I fails in K minus {o}} and concludes the boxed principle Smaller Kernel does NOT imply Better Kernel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §47 — the backbone, and a substitution inside it ... O_t → K_t → I_t → Δ_t → K_{t+1} refined to O_t → ℱ_t → K_t → EC_t → Δ_t → T_t → K_{t+1}. The refinement replaces I_t with EC_t. ... Two new objects appear here and nowhere in my registry: ℱ_t and T_t.

a_rows_sample.statement: Records Theory v1.0's four-way gap-boundary taxonomy (Z1 known dimension/unknown value, Z2 unknown dimension, Z3 unknown relationship, Z4 representation/observability failure), with Z4 itself explicitly subdivided into a boxed four-way distinction: Unobserved != Unobservable != Uninterpretable != Representationally inadequate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: OPEN-3 — a definition that removes the circularity by name ... R_1≡_sem R_2 ⟺ ∀(Q,C,EC): Obs_{EC,Q,C}(R_1)=Obs_{EC,Q,C}(R_2) ... eight enumerated observables: Identity, Meaning, EvidenceRelations, Assessment, Gap, Determination, History, ValidTransitions. ... b_rows_sample.statement: Finds the reply document proposes an observational equiv_sem definition addressing OPEN-3: R1 equiv_sem R2 iff for all (Q,C,EC), Obs_{EC,Q,C}(R1)=Obs_{EC,Q,C}(R2), with eight explicitly enumerated observable dimensions (Identity, Meaning, EvidenceRelations, Assessment, Gap, Determination, History, ValidTransitions), self-described as removing the circularity of 'they are equivalent because they mean the same thing.' Connects this directly to the prior batch's CIRC-5 finding (equiv_sem defined via an arbitrarily-chosen behavioral projection) -- argues an ENUMERATED observable set is precisely what would stop the projection choice from being arbitrary, which is exactly what CIRC-5 and a separate J-proof-obligations document (filing 'equiv_sem is well defined' as still requiring mathematical work) both need. Notes as UNDECIDABLE whether the separately-dated v1.1-simulation package (no internal timestamp, datable only to after 00:46:31) could have known about this definition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 3. ⭐⭐⭐ But ≡_sem now has THREE rival definitions, and they conflict ... A ... B CLOSURE-4 ... reviewed as 'the semantic equivalence claim is too strong' ... C 𝔎 = (K, =_str, ≡_sem, ≈_obs, SameId, ≡_H, ≡_P) — a 7-tuple ... in which ≡_sem and ≈_obs are distinct tuple positions ... The conflict is structural, not stylistic. A defines ≡_sem observationally. C exists to keep ≡_sem and ≈_obs apart. If semantic equivalence IS observational equivalence, the two positions of C's 7-tuple collapse.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a genuine three-way structural conflict among rival equiv_sem definitions in the corpus: (A) the newly-found observational definition with 8 enumerated observables, never cited by any other lane; (B) CLOSURE-4's executable, Q/Gamma/O-indexed tester (K1 equiv_sem^{Q,Gamma,O} K2 iff determinations match for all q,o), previously reviewed elsewhere as 'the semantic equivalence claim is too strong'; (C) Step 261's 7-tuple K-fraktur=(K,=_str,equiv_sem,approx_obs,SameId,equiv_H,equiv_P), carried through Steps 288-291, in which equiv_sem and approx_obs are DELIBERATELY DISTINCT tuple positions. Argues the conflict is structural, not stylistic: definition A defines equiv_sem observationally, while structure C exists specifically to KEEP equiv_sem and approx_obs apart -- if semantic equivalence really is observational equivalence, C's two positions collapse into one, exactly the collapse C was constructed to prevent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reclassified on this evidence: CIRC-5/TG-4 ... TG-1 three repairs unchosen ... the 10 notation collisions ... J's four STILL REQUIRING MATHEMATICAL WORK rows ... b_rows_sample.statement: Reclassifies four specific items using the new category: CIRC-5/TG-4's circular equiv_sem ('blocks minimality') from 'apparent gap' to OPEN BY COMMISSION (the prompt's SS26 commissioned the circularity audit while its line 1449 forbade repair); TG-1's three unchosen repairs R1/R2/R3 from 'apparent indecision' to OPEN BY COMMISSION ('do not choose', and the lane says so); the 10 notation collisions from 'apparent debt' to OPEN BY COMMISSION (commissioned at line 1405, constrained at line 1422); and J's four 'STILL REQUIRING MATHEMATICAL WORK' rows from 'apparent incompleteness' to OPEN BY COMMISSION (the proof-obligation register was itself commissioned to say exactly this). Explicitly clarifies this reclassification does NOT dissolve the underlying issues -- equiv_sem still genuinely has three rival, unreconciled definitions (per the prior G-40 finding, S2924), TG-1 still genuinely holds -- what changes is only the EVIDENCE CLASS of the silence: it is now understood as a declared experimental boundary, not an omission, joining the same category as rho_A, Det_r, Omega-B, succeq, and OPEN-1..6.
